IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p133/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p133/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p133/r1.claim: A common construction omits a possessive head noun, promotes its dependent noun into its place, and assigns the verb to that dependent.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p133/r1.anchor: من ذلك: أن تحذف المضاف وتقيم المضاف إليه مقامه وتجعل الفعل له.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p133/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p133/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p133/r6.claim: Prayer itself cannot be demolished; the omitted noun is houses or buildings of prayer.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p133/r6.anchor: وقوله سبحانه: لهدمت صوامع وبيع وصلوات ومساجد [الحج: 40] فالصلوات لا تهدم، وإنما أراد بيوت الصلوات.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p133/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p133/r7.speaker: المفسرون
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p133/r7.claim: Exegetes assign monasteries to Ṣābians, churches to Christians, prayer houses to Jews, and mosques to Muslims.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p133/r7.anchor: قال المفسرون: الصوامع للصابئين، والبيع للنصارى، والصلوات: كنائس اليهود، والمساجد للمسلمين.

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r1.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r1.claim: One dating view holds that the surah is Madinan except verses 52–55, which are Makkan.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r1.anchor: Some say it is Madinan except for vv. 52–55, which are Makkan (IK)

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r2.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r2.claim: Another dating view holds that the surah is Makkan except verses 19–22, which are Madinan.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r2.anchor: others say it is Makkan except for vv.19–22, which are from the Madinan period (Q)

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r3.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r3.claim: Most authorities regard the surah as containing both Makkan and Madinan verses.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r3.anchor: Most say it is a mix of Makkan and Madinan verses (Q)

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r4.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r4.claim: A tradition calls the surah remarkable because it came at night and by day, on journeys and at home, in war and peace, and includes abrogating and abrogated as well as clear and allegorical verses.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r4.anchor: and it has both muḥkam (unambiguous) and mutashābih (symbolic or allegorical) verses (Q)

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r10.speaker: many scholars
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r10.claim: Many scholars regard verses 39–41 as the first revelation permitting the Muslim community to use force in self-defense against persecution.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r10.anchor: many scholars to be the first verses revealed giving the Muslim community permission to resort to the use of force

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Qur'an also calls Jewish and Christian synagogues and churches mosques.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: synagouges and churches of the Jews and Christians as mosques

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p162/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p162/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p162/r4.claim: Only verses 38–41 were revealed in Madinah; they permit Muslims to fight defensively if Quraysh block Hajj, since the Muslims are the House’s rightful custodians.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p162/r4.anchor: In these verses, Muslims are permitted to take up arms in defence if the disbelievers of the Quraysh try to forcibly stop them from doing ḥajj.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p162/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p162/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p162/r5.claim: Although exegetes dispute the sūrah’s place of revelation because of those verses, Islahi holds that a few explanatory Madinan verses do not make the whole sūrah Madinan, as with Sūrah al-Muzzammil.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p162/r5.anchor: then this does not make the whole sūrah into a Madīnan one.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p203/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p203/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p203/r8.claim: The Madinan verses 38–41 explain the earlier discourse, which is why they were placed here.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p203/r8.anchor: they explain what is stated in earlier verses, they were placed here.

AKHFASH:v2p451#2/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p451#2/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p451#2/r2.claim: Because prayers themselves are not demolished, the verb is carried to an implied action, as if the text said that prayers were left.
AKHFASH:v2p451#2/r2.anchor: وقال {لهدمت صوامع وبيع وصلوات ومساجد} فالصلوات لا تهدم ولكن حمله على فعل آخر كأنه قال "وتركت صلوات"

AKHFASH:v2p451#2/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p451#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v2p451#2/r3.claim: Some say the phrase means the places of prayer.

AKHFASH:v2p451#2/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p451#2/r4.speaker: رجل من رواة الحسن
AKHFASH:v2p451#2/r4.claim: A transmitter of al-Hasan reports the form صلوت and says it means Jewish synagogues, called صلوثا in Aramaic.
AKHFASH:v2p451#2/r4.anchor: وقال رجل من رواة الحسن {صلوت} وقال: "هي كنائس اليهود تدعى* بالعبرانية "صلوثا"

AKHFASH:v2p451#2/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p451#2/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p451#2/r5.claim: In ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض, بعضهم is a grammatical substitute for الناس.
AKHFASH:v2p451#2/r5.anchor: وقال {ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض} لأن {بعضهم} بدل من {الناس} .

FARRA:v2p226/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p226/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p226/r8.claim: The expelled believers had done nothing except say that God is their Lord.

FARRA:v2p226/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p226/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p226/r9.claim: One parsing puts the exceptive phrase in the genitive, governed by the preposition in bi-ghayri haqq.
FARRA:v2p226/r9.anchor: في موضع خفض ترده على الباء

FARRA:v2p226/r10.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p226/r10.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p226/r10.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is an exception, as in the construction except seeking the face of his Lord.
FARRA:v2p226/r10.anchor: جعلت (أن) مستثناة كما قال (إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه الأعلى)

FARRA:v2p226/r11.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p226/r11.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p226/r11.claim: He identifies ṣawāmiʿ as Christian monks’ hermitages, biyaʿ as Christian prayer places, ṣalawāt as Jewish synagogues, and masājid as Muslim mosques.
FARRA:v2p226/r11.anchor: الصوامع للرهبان وأما الصلوات فهي كنائس اليهود والمساجد (مساجد الإسلام)

FARRA:v2p226/r12.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p226/r12.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p226/r12.claim: The preceding clause means God protects each prophet’s religion through followers until He sent Muhammad.
FARRA:v2p226/r12.anchor: يدفع بأمره وأتباعه عن دين كل نبي إلى أن بعث الله محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABRISI:22:36-40/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:36-40/r4.speaker: أهل المدينة ويعقوب
TABRISI:22:36-40/r4.claim: The people of Medina and Yaʿqūb read “were it not for God’s defense” with an alif; the others read it without one.
TABRISI:22:36-40/r4.anchor: وقرأ أهل المدينة ويعقوب ولولا دفاع الله بالألف والباقون دفع الله بغير ألف

TABRISI:22:36-40/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:36-40/r9.speaker: أهل المدينة ويعقوب
TABRISI:22:36-40/r9.claim: The people of Medina and Yaʿqūb read “the monasteries were destroyed” with a light dāl; the others use the doubled form.
TABRISI:22:36-40/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر أذن بفتح الألف يقاتلون بفتح التاء

TABRISI:22:36-40/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:36-40/r12.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
TABRISI:22:36-40/r12.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad reads ṣalawāt with ḍamma on both ṣād and lām.
TABRISI:22:36-40/r12.anchor: وقرأ جعفر بن محمد ع وصلوات بضم الصاد واللام

TABRISI:22:36-40/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:36-40/r13.speaker: الجحدري والكلبي
TABRISI:22:36-40/r13.claim: Al-Jaḥdarī and al-Kalbī read ṣalawāt with ḍamma on ṣād and fatḥa on lām.
TABRISI:22:36-40/r13.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري والكلبي وصلوات بضم الصاد وفتح اللام

TABRISI:22:36-40/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:36-40/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:36-40/r20.claim: The light reading of hadama can describe either a single or repeated act, while the doubled reading is specific to plurality.
TABRISI:22:36-40/r20.anchor: وقوله لهدمت بالتخفيف وإنما جاز لأن ذلك قد يكون للقليل والكثير تقول ضربت زيدا ضربة وضربته ألف ضربة فاللفظ في القلة والكثرة على حالة واحدة وهدمت بالتشديد يختص بالكثرة

TABRISI:22:36-40#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:36-40#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:36-40#2/r1.claim: The anonymous cited poem about opening and closing doors illustrates repeated action, supporting the distinction that the doubled form is specific to plurality.
TABRISI:22:36-40#2/r1.anchor: ما زلت أفتح أبوابا وأغلقها حتى أتيت أبا عمرو بن عمار

TABRISI:22:36-40#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:36-40#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:36-40#2/r5.claim: Ṣalawāt may be a plural of ṣalāt even though that plural is not otherwise used, like the variant plurals of ḥujra.
TABRISI:22:36-40#2/r5.anchor: وأما صلوات وصلوات فيمكن أن يكون جمع صلاة وإن كانت غير مستعملة فيكون مثل حجرة وحجرات وحجرات

TABRISI:22:36-40#2/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:36-40#2/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:36-40#2/r16.claim: Ṣawmaʿa derives from compression; aṣmaʿ describes ears close together, and anything compressed is mutaṣammiʿ.
TABRISI:22:36-40#2/r16.anchor: والصومعة أصلها من الانضمام ومنه الأصمع للاصق الأذنين وكل منضم فهو متصمع

TABRISI:22:36-40#2/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:36-40#2/r17.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
TABRISI:22:36-40#2/r17.claim: Abū Dhuʾayb’s poem describes a hunter’s feathers as mutaṣammiʿ, illustrating the sense “compressed.”
TABRISI:22:36-40#2/r17.anchor: قال أبو ذؤيب يصف صائدا: فرمى فأنفذ من نحوص غائط سهما فخر وريشه متصمع

TABRISI:22:36/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:36/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:36/r3.claim: The relative phrase “those expelled from their homes” may be genitive as an appositive to “those who fight,” nominative under an implied subject, or accusative for praise under an implied “I mean.”
TABRISI:22:36/r3.anchor: الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم في محل الجر بأنه بدل من الذين يقاتلون ويجوز أن يكون في موضع الرفع على تقديرهم الذين أخرجوا وفي محل النصب على المدح على تقدير أعني

TABRISI:22:36/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:36/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:36/r4.claim: “Without right” is circumstantial, or it qualifies an omitted verbal noun meaning they were expelled in an expulsion unjustly described.
TABRISI:22:36/r4.anchor: بغير حق في موضع نصب على الحال ويجوز أن يكون صفة مصدر محذوف وتقديره أخرجوا إخراجا بهذه الصفة

TABRISI:22:36/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:36/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:36/r5.claim: The exception after “they were expelled” breaks the negation and means “except for their saying,” or “because they said,” that God is their Lord.
TABRISI:22:36/r5.anchor: لنقض النفي وتقديره إلا بأن يقولوا أي بقولهم

TABRISI:22:36/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:36/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:36/r6.claim: Baʿḍahum is a partitive apposition to al-nās: God repels some people by means of others.
TABRISI:22:36/r6.anchor: وبعضهم منصوب على البدل من الناس وهو بدل البعض من الكل والتقدير دفع الله بعض الناس ببعض

BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r1.claim: Alladhīna ukhrijū is genitive as an adjective qualifying the relative pronoun.
BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r1.anchor: في حيز الجر على أنه صفة للموصول

BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r2.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r2.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says the expulsion explains the injustice that permitted fighting, and their homes were Mecca.
BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ : لما بين أنهم إنما أذنوا في القتال لأجل أنهم ظلموا فسر ذلك الظلم

BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r3.claim: Countries are called diyār because people move about within them; Arabs around Mecca called themselves people of the land, meaning the country.
BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r3.anchor: وتسمى البلاد الديار لأنه يدار فيها للتصرف يقال : ديار بكر

BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r4.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r4.claim: Al-Rāghib derives dār, a dwelling, from its circuit enclosed by a wall; diyār is its plural, and a town is also called dār.
BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r4.anchor: قال الراغب : الدار المنزل اعتبارا بدورانها الذي لها بالحائط

BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r5.claim: They were expelled without a valid cause; ḥaqq is what is due or obligatory.
BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r5.anchor: أي خرجوا بغير موجب استحقوا الخروج فالحق مصدر قولك حق الشيء يحق بالكسر أي وجب

BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r6.claim: The exception is parsed as a substitute for ḥaqq: their only “cause” was monotheism, which should merit acceptance, not expulsion; the ironic construction resembles a line by al-Nābigha.
BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r6.anchor: {إلا أن يقولوا ربنا الله} بدل من حق أي بغير موجب سوى التوحيد

BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r7.speaker: النابغة
BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r7.claim: Al-Nābigha’s verse exemplifies the ironic phrasing of treating a virtue as though it were a defect: the only flaw is that their swords are nicked from battle.
BURSEVI:v6p27#2/r7.anchor: لكن لا على الظاهر بل على طريقة قول النابغة :

BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r1.claim: God averts destruction by empowering believers against disbelievers in every age.
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r1.anchor: بتسليط المؤمنين منهم على الكفارين في كل عصر وزمان

BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r2.claim: Hadimmat means buildings would be torn down; tahdīm intensifies the sense of demolition, here through the polytheists’ conquest.
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r2.anchor: الهدم إسقاط البناء والتهديم للتكثير أي لخربت باستيلاء المشركين

BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r3.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r3.claim: Al-Rāghib describes ṣawāmiʿ as pointed or tapering buildings; they were monks’ worship places, often isolated in mountains or deserts.
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r3.anchor: قال الراغب : الصومعة كل بناء منصمع الرأس متلاصقة

BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r4.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r4.claim: Al-Rāghib identifies biyaʿ as Christian churches built in towns where congregations gathered to worship, unlike remote hermitages.
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r4.anchor: قال الراغب : الصومعة كل بناء منصمع الرأس متلاصقة والأصمع اللاصق أذنه برأسه والبيع جمع بيعة

BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r5.claim: Ṣalawāt refers to Jewish synagogues from the time of Moses; Kāshifī glosses the list as monks’ cells, Christian churches, and Jewish synagogues.
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r5.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (صومعهاي راهبان وكليساهاي ترسايان وكنشتهاي جهودان)

BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r6.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r6.claim: Al-Rāghib says a worship place may be called ṣalāt, which explains the name for churches.
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r6.anchor: قال الراغب : يسمى موضع العبادة بالصلاة ولذلك سميت الكنائس صلوات

BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r7.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r7.claim: Some authorities regard ṣalawāt as a borrowed Syriac term, ṣlotha, meaning a prayer place.
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم : هي كلمة معربة وهي بالعبرية

BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r8.claim: Masājid refers to Muslim mosques under Muḥammad’s law; they are listed last because that dispensation came later.
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r8.anchor: {ومساجد} للمسلمين في أيام شريعة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وقدم ما سوى المساجد

BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r9.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r9.claim: Al-Asʾila al-Muqḥima cautions that earlier mention does not imply superiority, citing the order “some of you are disbelievers and some believers.”
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r9.anchor: وفي "الأسئلة المقحمة" : تقديم الشيء بالذكر لا يدل على شرفه

BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r10.claim: Dhikran kathīran can mean remembrance repeated often or continued for a long time.
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r10.anchor: أي ذكرا كثيرا أو وقتا كثيرا صفة مادحة للمساجد خصت بها

BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r11.claim: The phrase may praise mosques and their people specifically, or describe all four kinds of worship places because their earlier communities remembered God there before their laws were abrogated.
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r11.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون صفة للأربع لأن الذكر في الصوامع والبيع والصلوات كان معتبرا

BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r12.claim: Inwardly, if God did not help hearts resist the ego, the pillars of sacred law, manners of the path, stations of reality, and mosques of the heart would be demolished; abundant remembrance needs a spacious heart lit by God.
BURSEVI:v6p27#3/r12.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى أنه تعالى لو لم ينصر القلوب على النفوس ويدافع عن القلوب

BURSEVI:v6p28/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p28/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p28/r1.claim: God surely aids whoever aids His friends or His religion; He fulfilled the promise by giving the Emigrants and Helpers victory over Arab, Persian, and Roman rulers and their lands.
BURSEVI:v6p28/r1.anchor: {ولينصرن الله من ينصره} أي : بالله لينصرن الله من ينصر أولياءه

BURSEVI:v6p28/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p28/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p28/r2.claim: God is powerful over all He wills and mighty, with nothing able to resist or repel Him.

BURSEVI:v6p28/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p28/r3.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v6p28/r3.claim: Baḥr al-ʿUlūm says God needs no human aid to destroy His enemies; requiring believers to fight with weapons, lives, and wealth lets them gain religious and worldly benefits by obeying.
BURSEVI:v6p28/r3.anchor: وفي "بحر العلوم" : يغني بقدرته وعزته في إهلاك أعداء دينه عنهم وإنما كلفهم النصر

BURSEVI:v6p28/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p28/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p28/r4.claim: Victory is an honored station unsuitable for unbelievers, but God alternates hardship between believers and unbelievers; otherwise faith would be forced and moral responsibility, reward, and punishment would disappear.
BURSEVI:v6p28/r4.anchor: إن النصرة والغلبة منصب شريف فلا يليق بحال الكافر لكن الله تعالى تارة يشدد المحنة

BURSEVI:v6p28/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p28/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p28/r5.claim: Tests also expiate believers’ sins, while hardship such as plague is mercy for believers but wrath and punishment for unbelievers.
BURSEVI:v6p28/r5.anchor: ولأن المؤمن قد يقدم على بعض المعاصي فيكون تشديد المحنة عليه في الدنيا كفارة له

BURSEVI:v6p28/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p28/r6.speaker: عامر
BURSEVI:v6p28/r6.claim: ʿĀmir saw a man crucified by al-Ḥajjāj and prayed that God’s forbearance not harm the oppressed; in a dream he saw the man in the highest heaven and heard that divine forbearance had placed him there.
BURSEVI:v6p28/r6.anchor: مر عامر برجل قد صلبه الحجاج قال : يا رب إن حلمك على الظالمين

RAZI-FULL:v23p35/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p35/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p35/r8.claim: Their oppression had two parts: they were expelled from their homes and expelled for saying God is their Lord; each is a grave injustice.
RAZI-FULL:v23p35/r8.anchor: فبين تعالى ظلمهم لهم بهذين الوجهين

RAZI-FULL:v23p35/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p35/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p35/r9.claim: The exception means they were expelled with no cause other than affirming God's oneness, which should warrant acceptance and protection, not expulsion and banishment.
RAZI-FULL:v23p35/r9.anchor: التوحيد الذي ينبغي أن يكون موجب الإقرار والتمكين

RAZI-FULL:v23p35/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p35/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p35/r10.claim: Rāzī compares the wording with 5:59, where believers are challenged for nothing except that they believed in God.
RAZI-FULL:v23p35/r10.anchor: ومثله { هل تنقمون منا إلا أن ءامنا بالله }

RAZI-FULL:v23p35/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p35/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p35/r11.claim: God's established practice is to preserve his religion by having some people repel others.
RAZI-FULL:v23p35/r11.anchor: أن عادته جل جلاله أن يحفظ دينه بهذا الأمر

RAZI-FULL:v23p35/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p35/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p35/r12.claim: Nāfiʿ reads لهدمت with a light consonant; the other readers use the doubled consonant.

RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r1.claim: Rāzī explains defense as God permitting his people to fight unbelievers; otherwise polytheists would dominate religious communities and destroy worship places, while the command lets believers worship and build.
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r1.anchor: هو إذنه لأهل دينه بمجاهدة الكفار

RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r2.claim: Non-Muslim worship sites are included because the defense preserves places of worship for communities beyond the Muslims.
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r2.anchor: ولكنه دفع عن هؤلاء بأن أمر بقتال أعداء الدين

RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r3.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī says God protects believers through prophets and protects those who do not fight through those who fight.
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r3.anchor: قال الكلبي يدفع الله بالنبيين عن المؤمنين

RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r4.claim: Abū al-Jawzāʾ reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that good-doers protect wrongdoers, and those who pray, give alms, and perform pilgrimage protect those who do not.
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r4.anchor: روى أبو الجوزاء عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that the Prophet said God protects a hundred members of a righteous Muslim's household and neighbors through him, then recited this verse; no grading is stated.
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r6.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reports Ibn ʿAbbās's view that Islam and its adherents protect the protected non-Muslim communities.
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r6.anchor: قال الضحاك عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r7.claim: Mujāhid says witnesses protect people's rights and legal retaliation protects lives.
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r7.anchor: قال مجاهد يدفع عن الحقوق بالشهود

RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes all these terms to mean places of worship used by believers, with different expressions for them.
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r8.anchor: قال الحسن المراد بهذه المواضع أجمع مواضع المؤمنين

RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r9.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r9.claim: Al-Zajjāj says each prophet's lawful prayer place was protected in its era: churches under Moses, monasteries under Jesus, and mosques under Muhammad, before distortion and abrogation.
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r9.anchor: فلولا ذلك الدفع لهدم في زمن موسى الكنائس

RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r10.claim: Another explanation includes the sites because God's name continued to be remembered in them in the Prophet's time, so they were unlike idol worship.
RAZI-FULL:v23p35#2/r10.anchor: يجري فيها ذكر الله تعالى فليست بمنزلة عبادة الأوثان

RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r1.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya assigns monasteries to Christians, churches to Jews, prayer houses to Sabians, and mosques to Muslims.

RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r2.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says monasteries are Christian desert buildings, churches Christian buildings in towns, and prayer houses belong to Jews; ṣalawāt is Hebrew ṣəlōṯā.
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r2.anchor: الصوامع للنصارى وهي التي بنوها في الصحارى

RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r3.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r3.claim: Qatāda assigns monasteries to Sabians, churches to Christians, and prayer houses to Jews.
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r3.anchor: الصوامع للصابئين والبيع للنصارى والصلوات لليهود عن قتادة

RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r4.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says all four terms denote mosques: Muslims may use monasteries, churches is a comparison for mosques, and prayer houses refers to prayer and mosques being preserved.
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r4.anchor: أنها بأسرها أسماء المساجد عن الحسن

RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r5.claim: One figurative explanation of destroying prayers is invalidating them and eliminating their performers, as when someone's kindness is destroyed by answering it with ingratitude.
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r5.anchor: المراد بهدم الصلاة إبطالها وإهلاك من يفعلها

RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r6.claim: Another explanation takes صلوات as the place of prayer, as 'ask the town' means ask its people.

RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r7.claim: A third view allows an item that cannot be destroyed to join a list whose other items can, like saying someone carries a sword and a spear.

RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r8.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r8.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil take the frequent remembrance of God's name to refer to all the listed worship places.
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r8.anchor: قال الكلبي ومقاتل عائد إلى الكل

RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r9.claim: Rāzī says the phrase more likely refers only to mosques, honoring them as places where God is frequently remembered.
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r9.anchor: والأقرب أنه مختص بالمساجد تشريفا لها

RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p36/r10.claim: The other worship sites precede mosques because they existed earlier; another explanation says the last-mentioned were last historically, though first in intention, since Muhammad and his community were best and last, as in the Prophet's saying, 'we are the last and the foremost'.

RAZI-FULL:v23p37/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p37/r1.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v23p37/r1.claim: One view says aiding God means accepting jihad and thereby supporting God's religion.
RAZI-FULL:v23p37/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم من ينصره بتلقى الجهاد بالقبول

RAZI-FULL:v23p37/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p37/r2.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v23p37/r2.claim: Another view understands aiding God as upholding all his religion; God cannot literally be aided, so the expression means aiding his religion, as with being God's ally or enemy.
RAZI-FULL:v23p37/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون : بل المراد من يقوم بسائر دينه

RAZI-FULL:v23p37/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p37/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p37/r3.claim: The promise aids those who support God's religion: he strengthens them against enemies until they prevail, helps them explain proofs, and assists them in knowledge and obedience, encouraging jihad.
RAZI-FULL:v23p37/r3.anchor: وعد بالنصر لمن هذه حاله ونصر الله تعالى للعبد

RAZI-FULL:v23p37/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p37/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p37/r4.claim: God's strength assures his promised aid; his might means he cannot be wronged or prevented from what he wills.
RAZI-FULL:v23p37/r4.anchor: قوي على هذه النصرة التي وعدها المؤمنين

RAZI-FULL:v23p37/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p37/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p37/r6.claim: The people empowered are the Muhājirūn: 22:41 describes those expelled from their homes, while the Anṣār were not expelled.

STUDYQURAN:22:40/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r1.claim: The verse recalls believers expelled from Makkah for their faith, a frequently cited grievance of the Muslim community against Quraysh.
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r1.anchor: The expulsion of the believers from their homes in Makkah, mentioned also in 2:191, 217, 246; 3:195

STUDYQURAN:22:40/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r2.claim: Believers were permitted to use force in response to persecution and expulsion for professing that God is their Lord.
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r2.anchor: The believers were given permission to use force because of the wrongs committed against them: persecution and being forced to leave because of their faith

STUDYQURAN:22:40/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r3.claim: Repelling force is justified because it prevents destruction of different houses of worship; by implication, defense applies in similar future circumstances involving actual expulsion and potential destruction.
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r3.anchor: By implication, such defense or “repelling” should take place in the future under similar conditions

STUDYQURAN:22:40/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r4.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r4.claim: Monasteries are usually understood as houses of Christian monks.
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r4.anchor: Monasteries renders ṣawāmiʿ, usually understood to be houses of Christian monks

STUDYQURAN:22:40/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r5.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r5.claim: Some also associate the monasteries with the Sabeans.
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r5.anchor: but also associated by some with the Sabeans

STUDYQURAN:22:40/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r6.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r6.claim: Churches are generally understood to be Christian houses of worship.
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r6.anchor: churches renders biyaʿ, which most have understood to refer to Christian houses of worship

STUDYQURAN:22:40/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r7.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r7.claim: Churches may alternatively refer to Jewish temples.
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r7.anchor: but which may also refer to Jewish temples

STUDYQURAN:22:40/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r8.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r8.claim: Synagogues are usually understood as Jewish houses of worship.
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r8.anchor: synagogues renders ṣalawāt, usually understood to mean Jewish houses of worship

STUDYQURAN:22:40/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r9.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r9.claim: Some link the synagogues with the Sabeans.
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r9.anchor: but linked by some with the Sabeans (see 2:62)

STUDYQURAN:22:40/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r10.claim: Masājid literally means places of prostration and is generally associated with Muslim houses of worship.
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r10.anchor: mosques renders masājid, a word meaning “place of prostrations” and associated by most commentators with the houses of worship of Muslims themselves

STUDYQURAN:22:40/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r11.speaker: another opinion
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r11.claim: An alternate view takes masājid as a general term for the three preceding kinds of houses of worship.
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r11.anchor: although another opinion sees masājid as a general term referring to the previous three types of houses of worship (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:22:40/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r12.speaker: many commentators and jurists
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r12.claim: Commentators and jurists who hold Islam supersedes earlier religions take the verse to concern pre-Islamic houses of worship.
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r12.anchor: For many commentators and jurists, in keeping with their general theory of Islam’s supersession

STUDYQURAN:22:40/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r13.claim: Muslims are prohibited from damaging or destroying treaty communities' houses of worship both within and beyond Islamic lands.
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r13.anchor: Muslims, however, are prohibited from damaging or destroying the houses of worship belonging to peoples with whom there is a treaty

STUDYQURAN:22:40/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r14.speaker: Q, R
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r14.claim: Those who help God are understood to be those who help God's religion and His Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:22:40/r14.anchor: Those who help Him is understood to mean those who help God’s religion and His Prophet (Q, R).

TAB-FULL:v16p574/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p574/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v16p574/r1.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reports that when the Prophet left Mecca, a man said they had expelled their Prophet; the permission-to-fight verses followed, and the expelled were Muhammad and his companions.
TAB-FULL:v16p574/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، قال: " لما خرج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v16p574/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p574/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p574/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that when the Prophet left Mecca, Abū Bakr feared their destruction; after permission to fight was revealed, he knew fighting would occur, and the report calls it the first verse revealed.
TAB-FULL:v16p574/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " لما خرج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v16p574/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p574/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p574/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says permission to fight was given after the believers had been spared for ten years; those expelled were the believers.
TAB-FULL:v16p574/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {أذن للذين يقاتلون بأنهم ظلموا}

TAB-FULL:v16p577/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p577/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p577/r1.claim: The second relative pronoun ‘those’ resumes the first, identifying the people who were given permission to fight.

TAB-FULL:v16p577/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p577/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p577/r2.claim: The expelled people are the believers whom Quraysh drove from Mecca.
TAB-FULL:v16p577/r2.anchor: وعنى بالمخرجين من دورهم: المؤمنين الذين أخرجهم كفار قريش من مكة.

TAB-FULL:v16p577/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p577/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p577/r3.claim: Quraysh tortured some believers for their faith, insulted and threatened them until they had to leave; the expulsion was unjust because Quraysh were false and the believers right.
TAB-FULL:v16p577/r3.anchor: وكان فعلهم ذلك بهم بغير حق؛ لأنهم كانوا على باطل، والمؤمنون على الحق،

TAB-FULL:v16p578/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p578/r1.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v16p578/r1.claim: Ibn Jurayj explains the mutual دفع as God repelling the polytheists through the Muslims.
TAB-FULL:v16p578/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قوله: {ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض} [البقرة: 251] «دفع المشركين بالمسلمين»

TAB-FULL:v16p578/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p578/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p578/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets the mutual دفع as fighting and jihad in God’s path.
TAB-FULL:v16p578/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض} [البقرة: 251] قال «لولا القتال والجهاد»

TAB-FULL:v16p578/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p578/r3.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v16p578/r3.claim: Ali says God protects later Successors from harm through the Companions of Muhammad; without that defense, the monasteries and other worship places would have been demolished.
TAB-FULL:v16p578/r3.anchor: أن عليا رضي الله عنه قال: " إنما أنزلت هذه الآية في أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v16p578/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p578/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p578/r4.claim: Mujahid explains this defense through testimony and the securing of rights; without it, the named worship places would be destroyed.
TAB-FULL:v16p578/r4.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: {ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض} [البقرة: 251] يقول: " دفع بعضهم بعضا في الشهادة، وفي الحق،

TAB-FULL:v16p578/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p578/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p578/r5.claim: The wording is general: God restrains people through one another in many ways, including Muslims checking polytheists, rulers checking oppression, and witnesses preserving rights; no reason or binding report narrows it.
TAB-FULL:v16p578/r5.anchor: فذلك على الظاهر والعموم، على ما قد بينته قبل، لعموم ظاهر ذلك جميع ما ذكرنا

TAB-FULL:v16p581/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p581/r1.speaker: رفيع، مجاهد، ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p581/r1.claim: Rafi, Mujahid, and Ibn Zayd identify the ṣawāmiʿ as monks’ hermitages.
TAB-FULL:v16p581/r1.anchor: عن رفيع، في هذه الآية: {لهدمت صوامع} [الحج: 40] قال: «صوامع الرهبان»

TAB-FULL:v16p581/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p581/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v16p581/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak describes them as small ṣawāmiʿ that people build.

TAB-FULL:v16p581/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p581/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p581/r3.claim: Qatada identifies the ṣawāmiʿ as places belonging to the Sabians.

TAB-FULL:v16p581/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p581/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p581/r4.claim: Medinan readers read the verb without gemination; most Kufan and Basran readers geminate it to indicate repeated demolition, which al-Tabari prefers as fitting the repeated actions of disbelievers.
TAB-FULL:v16p581/r4.anchor: والتشديد في ذلك أعجب القراءتين إلي. لأن ذلك من أفعال أهل الكفر بذلك

TAB-FULL:v16p583/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p583/r1.speaker: رفيع، قتادة، الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v16p583/r1.claim: Rafi, Qatada, and al-Dahhak identify the biyaʿ as Christian churches.

TAB-FULL:v16p583/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p583/r2.speaker: مجاهد، ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p583/r2.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Zayd identify the biyaʿ as Jewish synagogues.
TAB-FULL:v16p583/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قال: {وبيع} [الحج: 40] قال: «وكنائس»

TAB-FULL:v16p584/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p584/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p584/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says ṣalawāt refers to churches.
TAB-FULL:v16p584/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {وصلوات} [التوبة: 99] قال: " يعني بالصلوات: الكنائس "

TAB-FULL:v16p584/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p584/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v16p584/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says these are Jewish synagogues, called ṣalōtā in their language.
TAB-FULL:v16p584/r2.anchor: الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {وصلوات "} [التوبة: 99] كنائس اليهود، ويسمون الكنيسة صلوتا "

TAB-FULL:v16p584/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p584/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p584/r3.claim: Qatada identifies ṣalawāt as Jewish synagogues.

TAB-FULL:v16p584/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p584/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v16p584/r4.claim: Abu al-Aliya says ṣalawāt means Sabian temples.
TAB-FULL:v16p584/r4.anchor: سألت أبا العالية عن الصلوات،، قال: «هي مساجد الصابئين»

TAB-FULL:v16p584/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p584/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p584/r5.claim: Mujahid identifies them as worship places of the People of the Book and Muslims along roads.
TAB-FULL:v16p584/r5.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قوله: {وصلوات} [التوبة: 99] قال: «مساجد لأهل الكتاب، ولأهل الإسلام بالطرق»

TAB-FULL:v16p584/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p584/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p584/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says these are Muslim prayers, interrupted when enemies enter, leaving worship stopped and mosques liable to destruction as under Nebuchadnezzar.
TAB-FULL:v16p584/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {وصلوات} [التوبة: 99] قال: «الصلوات صلوات أهل الإسلام، تنقطع إذا دخل العدو عليهم،

TAB-FULL:v16p586/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p586/r1.speaker: رفيع، قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p586/r1.claim: Rafi and Qatada identify the masājid as Muslim mosques, where God’s name is often invoked.

TAB-FULL:v16p586/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p586/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v16p586/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says God’s name is often invoked in all the places listed, so the phrase is not limited to mosques.
TAB-FULL:v16p586/r2.anchor: الضحاك يقول في قوله: {ومساجد} [الحج: 40] «يقول في كل هذا يذكر اسم الله كثيرا، ولم يخص المساجد»

TAB-FULL:v16p586/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p586/r3.speaker: بعض أهل العربية من أهل البصرة
TAB-FULL:v16p586/r3.claim: Some Basran grammarians say prayers cannot be demolished, so an omitted verb is understood: prayers were left behind.
TAB-FULL:v16p586/r3.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العربية من أهل البصرة يقول: الصلوات لا تهدم، ولكن حمله على فعل آخر، كأنه قال: وتركت صلوات.

TAB-FULL:v16p586/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p586/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v16p586/r4.claim: Another explanation takes ṣalawāt to mean places where prayers are performed.
TAB-FULL:v16p586/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم: إنما يعني: مواضع الصلوات.

TAB-FULL:v16p586/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p586/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v16p586/r5.claim: Another explanation takes the word literally as prayers, identifying them as Jewish synagogues called ṣalōtā in Hebrew.
TAB-FULL:v16p586/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم: إنما هي صلوات، وهي كنائس اليهود، تدعى بالعبرانية: صلوتا.

TAB-FULL:v16p586/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p586/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p586/r6.claim: Al-Tabari identifies the four places as monks’ hermitages, Christian churches, Jewish synagogues, and Muslim mosques; these are the established Arabic senses, while alternatives are possible but not ordinarily used for their proposed referents.
TAB-FULL:v16p586/r6.anchor: وأولى هذه الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب قول من قال: معنى ذلك: لهدمت صوامع الرهبان، وبيع النصارى، وصلوات اليهود، وهي كنائسهم،

TAB-FULL:v16p638/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p638/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p638/r1.claim: God is powerful and invincible, unlike the idols, which cannot create a fly or stop it taking something from them; this shows their weakness and humiliation.
TAB-FULL:v16p638/r1.anchor: من الذباب إذا استلبها شيئا ضعفا ومهانة

TABATABAI:22:39-40/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:39-40/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:39-40/r6.claim: The believers were driven from their homes in Mecca by polytheist abuse, torture, and persecution that forced some to Abyssinia and others to Medina; “expelled” means compelled to leave, not physically deported.
TABATABAI:22:39-40/r6.anchor: ولم يخرجوهم بحمل وتسفير بل آذوهم وبالغوا في إيذائهم وشددوا بالتعذيب والتفتين

TABATABAI:22:39-40/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:39-40/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:39-40/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī takes the exception as disconnected: they were expelled, but only because they said “Our Lord is God,” exposing the polytheists’ perverse treatment of truth as grounds for eviction.
TABATABAI:22:39-40/r7.anchor: استثناء منقطع معناه ولكن أخرجوا بسبب أن يقولوا ربنا الله

TABATABAI:22:39-40/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:39-40/r8.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:22:39-40/r8.claim: An alternative takes the exception as connected, with “the right” as the excepted element: their profession of God was the only right involved; the author rejects this as contrary to the verse’s point that they had no lawful cause for expulsion.
TABATABAI:22:39-40/r8.anchor: وقيل الاستثناء متصل والمستثنى منه هو الحق والمعنى أخرجوا بغير حق إلا الحق

TABATABAI:22:39-40/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:39-40/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:39-40/r9.claim: The passage describes all believers by the experience of some—the emigrants—because believers form one united community; the Qur'an often attributes some members’ qualities to the whole.

TABATABAI:22:40/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:40/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:40/r1.claim: Ṣawāmiʿ are taper-topped structures in mountains or wilderness where ascetics and recluses worship; biyaʿ are Jewish and Christian temples, and masājid are Muslim mosques.
TABATABAI:22:40/r1.anchor: الصوامع جمع صومعة وهي بناء في أعلاه حدة كان يتخذ في الجبال والبراري

TABATABAI:22:40/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:40/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:40/r2.claim: Ṣalawāt refers to Jewish prayer houses, naming the place by the act performed there, as al-ṣalāt means a mosque in 4:43.
TABATABAI:22:40/r2.anchor: والصلوات جمع صلاة وهي مصلى اليهود سمي بها تسمية للمحل باسم الحال

TABATABAI:22:40/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:40/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:22:40/r3.claim: Another explanation derives ṣalawāt from the Aramaic or Syriac ṣlotha, meaning a place of prayer.
TABATABAI:22:40/r3.anchor: وقيل هي معرب صلوثا بالثاء المثلثة والقصر وهي بالعبرانية المصلى

TABATABAI:22:40/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:40/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:40/r4.claim: As a rationale for combat, the verse says fighting protects religious society from enemies seeking to extinguish God's light; without it, worship sites and rites would be erased.
TABATABAI:22:40/r4.anchor: ومحصلها أن تشريع القتال إنما هو لحفظ المجتمع الديني من شر أعداء الدين

TABATABAI:22:40/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:40/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:40/r5.claim: God's pushing people against one another is broader than battle: mutual defense of life's interests is an innate social law, ultimately grounded in God.
TABATABAI:22:40/r5.anchor: لكن المراد بدفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض أعم من القتال

TABATABAI:22:40/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:40/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:40/r6.claim: People are equipped with physical powers and reason to devise means of self-defense and protect the conditions of a good life; fighting is a last resort, like cautery, accepting some loss so others may live.
TABATABAI:22:40/r6.anchor: ويشهد به تجهيز الإنسان كسائر الموجودات بأدوات وقوى تسهل له البطش

TABATABAI:22:40/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:40/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:40/r7.claim: Worship sites are singled out because they are the visible signs of religion that remind people of it and preserve its image in their minds, although religion's broader existence is at stake.
TABATABAI:22:40/r7.anchor: لأن هذه المعابد والمعاهد هي الشعائر والأعلام الدالة على الدين المذكرة له الحافظة لصورته

TABATABAI:22:40/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:40/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:40/r8.claim: The emphatic oath promises aid to those who fight in defense of divine religion; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says God fulfilled it by supporting Muslim campaigns and raising the religion's name as they supported it.
TABATABAI:22:40/r8.anchor: قسم مع تأكيد بالغ على نصره تعالى من ينصره بالقتال ذبا عن الدين الإلهي

TABATABAI:22:40/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:40/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:40/r9.claim: God is powerful, whom none can weaken or prevent from acting, and mighty, inaccessible in His sovereignty and unmatched in dominion.
TABATABAI:22:40/r9.anchor: إن الله لقوي لا يضعفه أحد ولا يمنعه شيء عما أراد عزيز منيع الجانب

TABATABAI:22:40/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:40/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:40/r10.claim: The verse suggests that earlier religious laws also contained a defensive rule, though it does not explain its form.
TABATABAI:22:40/r10.anchor: ويظهر من الآية أنه كان في الشرائع السابقة حكم دفاعي في الجمله وإن لم يبين كيفيته

TABRISI:22:39-40/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:39-40/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:39-40/r4.claim: One possibility is that the expelled believers went to Medina, making the verse Medinan.
TABRISI:22:39-40/r4.anchor: يحتمل معناه أن يكون أراد أخرجوا إلى المدينة فتكون الآية مدنية

TABRISI:22:39-40/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:39-40/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:39-40/r5.claim: Alternatively, the expulsion was to Abyssinia, which would make the verse Meccan; persecution forced them to leave.
TABRISI:22:39-40/r5.anchor: ويحتمل إلى الحبشة فتكون الآية مكية وذلك بأنهم تعرضوا لهم بالأذى حتى اضطروا إلى الخروج

TABRISI:22:39-40/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:39-40/r6.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:22:39-40/r6.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī explains “without right” as meaning they had done nothing to deserve expulsion.
TABRISI:22:39-40/r6.anchor: وقوله بغير حق معناه من غير أن استحقوا ذلك عن الجبائي

TABRISI:22:39-40/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:39-40/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:39-40/r7.claim: They were expelled solely because they professed that God alone is their Lord.
TABRISI:22:39-40/r7.anchor: أي لم يخرجوا من ديارهم إلى لقولهم ربنا الله وحده

TABRISI:22:39-40/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:39-40/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABRISI:22:39-40/r8.claim: Abū Jaʿfar says the verse was revealed about the Emigrants and also applies to the family of Muhammad, who were expelled and intimidated.
TABRISI:22:39-40/r8.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر ع: نزلت في المهاجرين وجرت في آل محمد عليهم السلام

TABRISI:22:39-40/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:39-40/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:39-40/r9.claim: The author refers readers to his earlier discussion of God’s repelling some people by means of others.

TABRISI:22:39-40/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:39-40/r10.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:22:39-40/r10.claim: Al-Zajjāj assigns monasteries to Jesus’ dispensation, churches to Moses’ dispensation, and mosques to Muhammad’s; without divine restraint, prayer places in every dispensation would be demolished.
TABRISI:22:39-40/r10.anchor: عن الزجاج، والمعنى ولولا أن دفع الله بعض الناس ببعض لهدم في كل شريعة

TABRISI:22:39-40/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:39-40/r11.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:22:39-40/r11.claim: Abū Muslim says churches are in villages, monasteries in mountains and deserts and shared by three communities, mosques belong to Muslims, and ṣalawāt are Jewish synagogues.
TABRISI:22:39-40/r11.anchor: وقيل: البيع للنصارى في القرى والصوامع في الجبال والبراري ويشترك فيها الفرق الثلاث

TABRISI:22:39-40/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:39-40/r12.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك وقتادة
TABRISI:22:39-40/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and Qatāda identify ṣalawāt as Jewish synagogues, whose name was Arabized from their term ṣalawt.
TABRISI:22:39-40/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والضحاك وقتادة: الصلوات كنائس اليهود يسمونها صلوة فعربت

TABRISI:22:39-40/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:39-40/r13.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:22:39-40/r13.claim: Al-Hasan takes ṣalawāt to mean the prayer itself, destroyed by killing those who perform it or preventing them from praying.
TABRISI:22:39-40/r13.anchor: وقال الحسن: أراد بذلك عين الصلاة وهدم الصلاة بقتل فاعليها

TABRISI:22:39-40/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:39-40/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:39-40/r14.claim: Another view takes ṣalawāt as prayer places, as in the command not to approach prayer while intoxicated, meaning mosques.
TABRISI:22:39-40/r14.anchor: وقيل: أراد بالصلوات المصليات كما قال: لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى

TABRISI:22:39-40/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:39-40/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:39-40/r15.claim: The pronoun “in them” may refer only to mosques, or to all the previously named worship places, where God is generally remembered.
TABRISI:22:39-40/r15.anchor: الهاء تعود إلى المساجد. وقيل: إلى جميع المواضع التي تقدمت لأن الغالب فيها ذكر الله

TABRISI:22:39-40/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:39-40/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:39-40/r16.claim: God promises to support whoever supports His religion and religious law.
TABRISI:22:39-40/r16.anchor: هذا وعد من الله بأنه سينصر من ينصر دينه وشريعته

TABRISI:22:39-40/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:39-40/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:39-40/r17.anchor: إن لقوي عزيز } أي قادر قاهر

THALABI:v7p25#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p25#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p25#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that when the Prophet was expelled from Mecca, Abū Bakr feared that the people would be destroyed; after the permission to fight was revealed, he realized fighting would occur.
THALABI:v7p25#2/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: لما أخرج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من مكة قال أبو بكر:

THALABI:v7p25#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p25#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v7p25#2/r2.claim: Mujāhid says the verse was revealed about specific Meccan emigrants prevented from migrating to Medina, and permits fighting those unbelievers who blocked their migration.
THALABI:v7p25#2/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد: نزلت هذه الآية في قوم بأعيانهم خرجوا مهاجرين من مكة إلى المدينة

THALABI:v7p25#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p25#2/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p25#2/r3.claim: The phrase describing those expelled is an appositive replacement for the earlier phrase al-ladhīna.
THALABI:v7p25#2/r3.anchor: الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم بغير حق بدل من الذين الأولى

THALABI:v7p25#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p25#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p25#2/r4.claim: They were expelled for no reason except saying that God alone is their Lord.
THALABI:v7p25#2/r4.anchor: إلا أن يقولوا ربنا الله يعني لم يخرجوا من ديارهم إلا لقولهم ربنا الله وحده

THALABI:v7p25#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p25#2/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p25#2/r5.claim: The clause may be genitive, governed by the bāʾ in bi-ghayri ḥaqq, or accusative as an exception.
THALABI:v7p25#2/r5.anchor: فيكون أن في موضع الخفض ردا على الباء في قوله بغير حق ويجوز أن يكون في موضع نصب

THALABI:v7p25#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p25#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p25#2/r6.claim: God's repelling of people by others occurs through jihad, enforcing legal limits, and restraining injustice.
THALABI:v7p25#2/r6.anchor: ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض بالجهاد وإقامة الحدود وكف الظلم

THALABI:v7p25#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p25#2/r7.speaker: الحجازيون والباقون
THALABI:v7p25#2/r7.claim: The people of the Ḥijāz read the verb with a light dāl; the others double it with kasrah, meaning the places would be destroyed.
THALABI:v7p25#2/r7.anchor: قرأ الحجازيون بتخفيف الدال، والباقون بالتشديد على الكسر أي تخربت

THALABI:v7p25#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p25#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك وقتادة
THALABI:v7p25#2/r8.claim: Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk identify the ṣawāmiʿ as monks' hermitages; Qatādah says they are the Sabians' hermitages.
THALABI:v7p25#2/r8.anchor: صوامع قال مجاهد والضحاك: يعني صوامع الرهبان، قتادة: صوامع الصابئين.

THALABI:v7p25#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p25#2/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p25#2/r9.claim: The churches are the Christians' places of worship.

THALABI:v7p25#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p25#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
THALABI:v7p25#2/r10.claim: Ibn Abī Najīḥ reports from Mujāhid, and Ibn Zayd agrees, that the word means Jewish synagogues.
THALABI:v7p25#2/r10.anchor: ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد: البيع: كنائس اليهود، وبه قال ابن زيد

THALABI:v7p25#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p25#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والضحاك
THALABI:v7p25#2/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatādah, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say ṣalawāt are Jewish synagogues, called ṣalūtā.
THALABI:v7p25#2/r11.anchor: صلوات قال ابن عباس وقتادة والضحاك: يعني كنائس اليهود ويسمونها صلوتا.

THALABI:v7p25#2/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p25#2/r12.speaker: أبو العالية
THALABI:v7p25#2/r12.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliyah identifies the ṣalawāt as Sabian temples.

THALABI:v7p25#2/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p25#2/r13.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v7p25#2/r13.claim: Ibn Abī Najīḥ reports from Mujāhid that these are places of worship for scriptural communities and Muslims along roads; on these interpretations, enemy attack would interrupt worship and destroy mosques, as happened under Nebuchadnezzar.
THALABI:v7p25#2/r13.anchor: ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد: هي مساجد لأهل الكتاب ولأهل الإسلام بالطريق،

THALABI:v7p25#2/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p25#2/r14.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v7p25#2/r14.claim: Another explanation assigns hermitages and churches to Jesus' dispensation, synagogues to Moses' dispensation, and mosques to Muhammad's dispensation.
THALABI:v7p25#2/r14.anchor: وقيل: تأويلها: لهدمت صوامع وبيع في أيام شريعة عيسى،

THALABI:v7p25#2/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p25#2/r15.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v7p25#2/r15.claim: Al-Hasan says believers protect the worship places of protected non-Muslims from being destroyed.
THALABI:v7p25#2/r15.anchor: وقال الحسن: يدفع عن هدم مصليات أهل الذمة بالمؤمنين،

THALABI:v7p25#2/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p25#2/r16.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p25#2/r16.claim: Non-Muslim worship places precede mosques because they are older, or because they are nearer to destruction while mosques are nearer to remembrance; the author compares the ordering with 35:32.
THALABI:v7p25#2/r16.anchor: فإن قيل: لم قدم مصليات الكافرين على مساجد المسلمين؟

THALABI:v7p26/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p26/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p26/r1.claim: God will help whoever helps His religion and His Prophet.
THALABI:v7p26/r1.anchor: ولينصرن الله من ينصره أي ينصر دينه ونبيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p426#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p426#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p426#2/r1.claim: The relative pronoun is genitive, with the sense ‘permission was given to those expelled from their homes,’ continuing the preceding verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p426#2/r1.anchor: المعنى: أذن للذين أخرجوا من ديارهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p426#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p426#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p426#2/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj say the monotheists were expelled by idolaters because they proclaimed God’s oneness; ‘they were expelled’ is understood from the opening and the exception.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p426#2/r2.anchor: الزجاج (¬4): أي لم يخرجوا إلا بأن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p426#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p426#2/r3.speaker: سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p426#2/r3.claim: Sībawayh treats the exception as disconnected: the sense is ‘but because they say, Our Lord is God,’ meaning they were expelled for monotheism; al-Farrāʾ also records this option.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p426#2/r3.anchor: وقال سيبويه: هذا من الاستثناء المنقطع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p426#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p426#2/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p426#2/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ also permits construing أن as an exception, as in 92:20.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p426#2/r4.anchor: وذكر الفراء هذا القول أيضا، فقال: وإن شئت جعلت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p426#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p426#2/r5.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p426#2/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad reports another view: they were expelled on the pretext that their saying ‘Our Lord is God’ entitled them to expulsion, an injustice expressed as a connected exception.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p426#2/r5.anchor: وحكى المبرد عن بعضهم قولا آخر، وهو: أن المعنى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p426#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p426#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p426#2/r6.claim: The connected exception excludes monotheism from wrongdoing for emphatic effect, like al-Nābigha’s ironic exception of sword nicks from a list of faults: these exiles had no real offense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p426#2/r6.anchor: وعلى هذا الاستثناء متصل، واستثنى التوحيد من الباطل لضرب من المبالغة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r1.claim: The phrase is also read difāʿ Allāh, ‘God’s defense’; the author refers readers to the discussion in the preceding verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r1.anchor: وقوله: {ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض} وقرئ:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r2.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r2.claim: Abū ʿAlī allows difāʿ as a verbal noun from triliteral dafaʿa, like kitāb from kataba, rather than a Form III verbal noun; examples include qiyām and ghiyāth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r2.anchor: قال أبو علي: ويجوز أن يكون الدفاع من دفع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r3.claim: Hadm means demolishing a structure; the noun can also mean what has been demolished.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r3.anchor: وقوله: {لهدمت} الهدم: مصدر هدمت البناء، إذا نقضته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r4.claim: The verb is read with a light or doubled dāl: the light form can cover little or much demolition, while the doubled form is specific to extensive demolition.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r4.anchor: فالتخفيف يكون للكثير والقليل، يدلك على ذلك أنك تقول

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r5.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r5.claim: Al-Azharī defines ṣawāmiʿ as hermits’ monasteries, named for their tapered tops; ṣamaʿa a dish means raising and sharpening its top, and aṣmaʿ describes a keen-witted man.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r5.anchor: قال الأزهري: الصومعة من البناء سميت صومعة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r6.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r6.claim: Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk identify the ṣawāmiʿ as monks’ monasteries.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r7.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r7.claim: Qatāda says the ṣawāmiʿ belong to the Ṣābians.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r8.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r8.claim: Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān identifies them as buildings beside roads.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p429/r8.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن حيان: هي البيوت التي على الطرق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r1.speaker: أهل اللغة والمفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r1.anchor: وهي كنيسة النصارى في قول أهل اللغة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق وأبو العباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r2.claim: Ṣalawāt are Jewish synagogues; their Hebrew name is ṣalotā.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r2.anchor: هي كنائس اليهود، وهي بالعبرانية صلوتا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة، الضحاك، مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and Muqātil also identify ṣalawāt as synagogues.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r3.anchor: وهذا قول ابن عباس، وقتادة، والضحاك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r4.claim: The mosques are those of the Muslim community of Muhammad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r4.anchor: يعني مساجد المسلمين من أمة محمد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r5.claim: Without divine repelling, each prophetic dispensation's prayer places would have been demolished in its own era.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r5.anchor: لولا أن الله دفع بعض الناس ببعض لهدم في كل شريعة نبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r6.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r6.claim: God's repelling people through others protects every community's worship places from corruption.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r6.anchor: أخبر الله جل ثناؤه أنه لولا دفعه الناس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r7.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r7.claim: The list is chronological: Israelite prayer places predated the Qurʾān, while mosques took their name later, so the oldest are named first.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r7.anchor: فبدأ بذكر البيع لأن صلوات من تقدم من أنبياء بني إسرائيل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r8.claim: This is the view of most exegetes: God averts destruction of each religious community's worship places.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r8.anchor: وهذا مذهب أكثر أهل التأويل في هذه الآية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r9.claim: Ṣalawāt means Muslim prayers, which cease if an enemy enters upon them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r9.anchor: الصلوات: صلوات أهل الإسلام تنقطع إذا دخل عليهم العدو

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r10.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r10.claim: On Ibn Zayd's reading, prayers are not demolished; an omitted phrase means that prayers are abandoned.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r10.anchor: وعلى هذا فالصلوات لا تهدم، ولكن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r11.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r11.claim: The intended referents are places where prayers are performed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r11.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: إنما يعني مواضع الصلوات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r12.claim: The first, era-by-era explanation is preferable.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r13.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r13.claim: Believers protect the worship places of protected non-Muslims from demolition.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r14.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r14.claim: The first view is preferable because the worship places were protected before their owners became dhimmīs; the alternative would list mosques first for their merit, while churches and synagogues were invalidated in Islam.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p431/r14.anchor: لأنهم قبل أن صاروا أهل الذمة حين كانوا على الحق كانت متعبداتهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p434/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p434/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p434/r1.claim: God helps the one who supports His religion, law, and messenger.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p434/r1.anchor: وهذا وعد من الله بنصر من ينصر دينه وشريعته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p434/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p434/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p434/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد ينصر محمدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p434/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p434/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p434/r3.claim: God fulfilled the promise by helping Muhammad and his religious community.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p434/r3.anchor: قال مقاتل: وقد فعل، نصر محمدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p434/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p434/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p434/r4.claim: Whoever establishes one of God's laws is helped to establish it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p434/r4.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: أي: من أقام شريعة من شرائعه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p434/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p434/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p434/r5.claim: God is powerful over His creation and invincible in His dominion and power.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p434/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: على خلقه {عزيز} منيع في سلطانه وقدرته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p434/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p434/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p434/r6.claim: God is mighty in taking vengeance on His enemy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p434/r6.anchor: وقال مقاتل: {عزيز} في انتقامه من عدوه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r6.claim: Those expelled unjustly from their homes are the Emigrants.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r7.claim: They were driven out only because they professed God’s oneness.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r7.anchor: لم يخرجوا إلا بأن وحدوا الله تعالى

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r8.claim: God’s restraining some people through others prevents the demolition of places of worship.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r8.anchor: لولا أن دفع الله بعض الناس ببعض

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r9.claim: The monasteries and churches named here belong to the era of Jesus.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r9.anchor: صوامع وبيع } في زمان عيسى عليه السلام

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r10.claim: The ṣalawāt are the churches or synagogues of Moses’ law, called ṣalota in Aramaic.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r10.anchor: في أيام شريعة موسى عليه السلام، يعني: كنائسهم وهي بالعبرانية صلوتا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r11.claim: The mosques named here belong to the law of Muhammad.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r11.anchor: في أيام شريعة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r12.claim: God will help whoever supports His religion.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r12.anchor: من نصر دين الله نصره الله على ذلك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r13.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r13.claim: God is powerful over creation and invincible in His dominion.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:38-40/r13.anchor: على خلقه { عزيز } منيع في سلطانه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p380#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p380#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p380#2/r1.claim: Qatāda says polytheists objected when Muslims professed God's oneness, and Satan and his troops were distressed by it.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p380#2/r1.anchor: قال قتادة: لما قال المسلمون: لا إله إلا الله، أنكرها المشركون وضاقها إبليس وجنوده.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p380#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p380#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p380#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says they had shed no blood, taken no property, or severed kinship; they were expelled only for professing God, as in 85:8.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p380#2/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن: ما سفكوا لهم من دم، ولا أخذوا لهم من مال، ولا قطعوا لهم من رحم وإنما أخرجوهم لأنهم قالوا: ربنا الله

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p380#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p380#2/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p380#2/r3.claim: God protects believers through their religion and protects unbelievers through believers.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p380#2/r3.anchor: يدفع عن المؤمنين بدينهم ويدفع عن الكافرين بالمؤمنين.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p380#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p380#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p380#2/r4.claim: Qatāda says the believer is tested by the unbeliever, while the unbeliever is spared through the believer.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p380#2/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: يبتلى المؤمن بالكافر، ويعافى الكافر بالمؤمن.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p380#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p380#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p380#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid identifies ṣawāmiʿ as monks' cells.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p380#2/r5.anchor: لهدمت صوامع} [الحج: 40] قال مجاهد: صوامع للرهبان.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p380#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p380#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p380#2/r6.claim: Qatāda identifies them as places of worship belonging to the Sabians.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p381/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p381/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p381/r2.claim: The mosques are those of the Muslims.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p381/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p381/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p381/r3.claim: The places where God's name is much mentioned are the mosques.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p381/r3.anchor: قوله: {يذكر فيها اسم الله كثيرا} [الحج: 40] يعني المساجد.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p381/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p381/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p381/r4.claim: God aids those who aid His religion.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p381/r4.anchor: قوله: {ولينصرن الله من ينصره} [الحج: 40] يعني من ينصر دينه.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p381/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p381/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p381/r5.claim: The aid is victory in this world and a proof in the Hereafter.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p381/r5.anchor: النصر في الدنيا والحجة في الآخرة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p381/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p381/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p381/r6.claim: God is mighty in His retribution.

QASHANI:22:40-41/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:22:40-41/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:22:40-41/r1.claim: God's counteraction among psychic powers includes desire against anger; more generally, spirit opposes psyche and intellect opposes fancy.
QASHANI:22:40-41/r1.anchor: { ولولا دفع الله } ناس القوى النفسانية { بعضهم ببعض } كدفع الشهوانية بالغضبية وبالعكس

QASHANI:22:40-41/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:22:40-41/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:22:40-41/r2.claim: Alternatively, faculties counteract one another generally, such as spiritual powers against psychic powers and intellect against fancy.
QASHANI:22:40-41/r2.anchor: أو ناس القوى مطلقا كدفع النفسانية بالروحانية ودفع الوهمية بالعقلية والنفسانية بعضها ببعض كما ذكر

QASHANI:22:40-41/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:22:40-41/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:22:40-41/r3.claim: Monasteries signify the secret's retreats, churches the heart's places of manifestation, synagogues the breast's worship places, and mosques the spirit's stations of witnessing and annihilation in God.
QASHANI:22:40-41/r3.anchor: { لهدمت صوامع } رهبان السر وخلواتهم { وبيع } نصارى القلب ومحال تجلياتهم { وصلوات } يهود الصدور ومتعبداتهم { ومساجد } مؤمني الروح ومقامات مشاهداتهم

QASHANI:22:40-41/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:22:40-41/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:22:40-41/r4.claim: Remembering God's greatest name is realized by embodying His character and attributes, attaining His mysteries, and being annihilated in His Essence.
QASHANI:22:40-41/r4.anchor: { يذكر فيها اسم الله } الأعظم بالتخلق بأخلاقه والاتصاف بصفاته والتحقق بأسراره والفناء في ذاته

QASHANI:22:40-41/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:22:40-41/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:22:40-41/r5.claim: God overcomes with His light whoever confronts Him through self-existence and manifestation, prevailing over those who match Him in self-exaltation.
QASHANI:22:40-41/r5.anchor: { ولينصرن الله } يقهر بنوره من بارزه بوجوده وظهوره

ELMALILI:22:39-41/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r6.claim: The wronged believers were expelled from their property and homes without just cause except that they said their Lord is Allah.

ELMALILI:22:39-41/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r7.claim: God repels aggressive oppressors, corrupters, and unbelievers through just people, the righteous, and believers.
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r7.anchor: mütecâviz zâlimleri, müfsidleri, kâfirleri âdillerle, sâlihlerle, mü’minlerle def‘etmesi olmasa idi

ELMALILI:22:39-41/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r8.claim: Sawami originally means a tall, pointed building, used before Islam for Christian monks' monasteries and Sabaean ascetics' retreats, and later for Muslim minarets; here it means the monasteries or retreats.
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r8.anchor: “Savma‘a” esasen tepesi sivri mürtefi‘binâ demektir ki İslâm’dan evvel Nasârâ râhiplerinin manastırlarına

ELMALILI:22:39-41/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r9.claim: Biya refers to churches, the places of worship of Christians.

ELMALILI:22:39-41/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r10.claim: Salawat here is the Arabicized Hebrew saluta and means Jewish prayer houses, or synagogues.
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r10.anchor: “Salât” burada İbrânice “saluta” mu‘arrebidir ki Yahudîlerin namazgâhı, yani havra demektir

ELMALILI:22:39-41/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r11.claim: Describing mosques as places where God's name is often mentioned both states frequent remembrance as Islam's primary worship aim and signals that other institutions have departed from their original purpose of remembrance.
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r11.anchor: Birisi İslâm ibadetinde ismullâhın çok zikredilmesi maksûd-ı aslî olduğunu tasrih, ikincisi de diğerlerinin vaz‘-ı aslî olan zikrullahtan udûl ile başka maksatlarda isti‘mâl olunduğuna işarettir

ELMALILI:22:39-41/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r12.claim: Without God moving religious people to repel aggressors and authorizing believers to fight, all these sanctuaries would be destroyed; irreligious attackers would spare none.
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r12.anchor: ehl-i imana harp hakk u salâhiyeti vermese idi manastırlar ve zâviyeler, kiliseler ve havralar ve içinde Allah ismi kesîren zikredilen mescidler bütün hedm olunurdu; dinsizlerin taarruzu hiçbirini bırakmaz

ELMALILI:22:39-41/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r13.claim: Elmalılı links the destruction prevented by repelling aggressors to the corruption of the earth mentioned in al-Baqara.
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r13.anchor: Sûre-i Bakara’da geçtiği üzere Arz fâsid olurdu

ELMALILI:22:39-41/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r14.claim: The preservation and safety of the religious institutions is proportionate to their defense, so Islam's right of defense is all the more established.
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r14.anchor: ve selâmeti müdafaalarıyla mütenâsibdir. O hâlde bütün bunların himâyesini istihdaf eden İslâm’ın hakk-ı müdafaası evleviyetle sâbittir

ELMALILI:22:39-41/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r15.claim: Aiding God means aiding His religion.

ELMALILI:22:39-41/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r16.speaker: author
