ELMALILI:22:39-41/r16.claim: Because religion concerns voluntary acts, the realization of divine will in this matter is contingent on the servant's partial will; human effort becomes a means to divine accomplishment, hence is called aid.
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r16.anchor: din ef‘âl-i ihtiyâriyeye ta‘alluk ettiği cihetle ol babda maksûdun husûlü için irâde-i ilâhiyenin ta‘alluku abdin irâde-i cüz’iyesine mu‘allak olduğundan kulların irâde-i cüz’iyelerini sarf ile sa‘yleri irâde-i ilâhiyenin incâzına vesile olmak itibariyle bir nusret gibidir

ELMALILI:22:39-41/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r17.claim: God makes the certainty of victory depend on believers' aid, meaning their effort.
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r17.anchor: nusretinin kat‘î tahakkukunu onların nusretine, yani çalışmalarına rabt eylemiştir

ELMALILI:22:39-41/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r18.claim: God is strong and mighty and needs no aid; those He aids are honored and cannot be overcome.
ELMALILI:22:39-41/r18.anchor: Nusrete ihtiyâcı yoktur. Ve nusret ettiği muazzez ve gayr-i mağlubdur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r6.claim: Together, verses 39–40 make protecting freedom of belief and the ability to practice religion a leading justification for defensive preparations.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r6.anchor: 39 ve 40. âyetler birlikte değerlendirildiğinde, inanç özgürlüğünü ve dinin icaplarını yaşama serbestisini sağlama hedefinin, savunma hazırlıklarını haklı kılan sebeplerin başında geldiği söylenebilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r7.claim: Following the broadly accepted translation, these terms mean monastic retreats, Christian churches, and Jewish synagogues, respectively.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r7.anchor: 40. âyette geçen ve sırasıyla “manastırlar, kiliseler, havralar” şeklinde tercüme edilen kelimeler genel kabul esas alınarak çevrilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r8.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r8.claim: Commentaries also differ over which religious communities' places of worship the three terms designate.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r8.anchor: Tefsirlerde, bunların hangi din mensuplarına ait mâbedler olduğu hususunda farklı görüşler de bulunmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r9.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r9.claim: Some exegetes read the clause about frequent remembrance of God as describing mosques alone.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r9.anchor: Bu âyetin “ki oralarda Allah’ın adı bol bol anılır” şeklinde çevrilen kısmını sadece mescidlerin sıfatı olarak yorumlayan müfessirler de vardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r10.speaker: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r10.claim: On the mosque-only reading, Elmalılı says the verse highlights remembrance of God as Islam's worship goal and suggests other faiths' shrines were diverted to different purposes.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r10.anchor: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi, burada bir taraftan İslâm’daki ibadetlerde Allah’ı çokça anmanın temel hedef olduğuna

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r11.claim: Frequent remembrance of God is the central aim of worship in all revealed religions.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r11.anchor: Bütün ilâhî dinlerdeki ibadetlerde Allah’ı çokça anmanın temel hedef olduğunda kuşku yoktur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r12.claim: The author finds it unsound to infer that other religions' places of worship had abandoned remembrance of God as their original aim.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r12.anchor: âyette diğer din mensuplarına ait mâbedlerde bu aslî amaçtan uzaklaşıldığına dair bir işaret bulunduğunu söylemek de isabetli görünmemektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r13.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r13.claim: Since the verse specifies no particular case, Tabari favors a comprehensive reading of God's preventing people from harming one another.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r13.anchor: Taberî bu konudaki başlıca yorumları aktardıktan sonra, burada özel bir durumun kastedildiğine dair bir açıklama bulunmadığına göre âyeti kapsamlı biçimde anlamanın uygun olacağını belirtir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r14.claim: This broad reading includes empowering monotheists against idolaters, granting governance that restrains injustice, and providing legal means such as testimony to protect rights.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:39/r14.anchor: Allah’ın, O’nun birliğine inananlara, putperestlere karşı mücadele gücü vermesi, topluma bireylerinin birbirlerine haksızlık etmelerini önleyen bir yönetim nasip etmesi

QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r1.claim: The wrongfully expelled are ultimately vindicated: truth prevails over falsehood, and oppression brings the oppressor swift punishment.
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r1.anchor: المظلوم منصور ولو بعد حين ، ودولة الحق تغلب دولة الباطل

QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r2.claim: For the spiritually discerning ascetic, renouncing worldly goods to earn compensation in the next life is a betrayal; ordinary righteous people may regard that motive as sincerity.
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r2.anchor: وهذا إخلاص الصالحين . ولكنه عند خواص الزهاد خيانة ؛ لأنهم تركوا دنياهم لا لله ولكن لوجود العوض

QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r3.claim: Worshippers betray their aspiration when they abandon desires and then retreat to legal concessions; sincerity would keep them from descending after rising beyond them.
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r3.anchor: وخيانة العابدين أن يدعوا شهواتهم ثم يرجعون إلى الرخص ، فلو صدقوا في مرماهم لما انحطوا

QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r4.claim: Gnostics betray their way by leaning toward a spiritual station or seeking rank, honor, and a measure of nearness from God.
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r4.anchor: وخيانة العارفين جنوحهم إلى وجود مقام ، وتطلعهم لمنال منزلة وإكرام من الحق

QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r5.claim: Lovers betray their way when they seek relief from the pain of ecstatic experience, estrangement, overpowering longing, or prolonged separation.
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r5.anchor: وخيانة المحبين روم فرحة مما يمسهم من برحاء المواجيد ، وابتغاء خرجه مما يشتد عليهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r6.claim: Those devoted to divine unity betray it if even a trace of choice stirs in them and they return from effacement to some distinction, unless this occurs while they are absent from themselves.
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r6.anchor: وخيانة أرباب التوحيد أن يتحرك لهم للاختيار عرق ، وروجوعهم - بعد امتحائهم عنهم - إلى شظية من أحكام الفرق

QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r7.claim: When enemies apparently humiliate the saints, the saints remain surrendered while God avenges them, destroys their opponents, and turns fortune against them.
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r7.anchor: فالحق - سبحانه - ينتقم من أعدائهم لأجلهم ، فهم بنعت التسليم والسكون في أغلب الأحوال

QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r8.claim: At times God gives the saints victory and power over their opponents; in every case divine aid comes, for God prevails in His affair.
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r8.anchor: وفي بعض الأحايين ينصبهم الحق سبحانه بنعت الغلبة والتمكين من نزولهم بساحات من يناوئهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r9.claim: The soul and its whisperings can corrupt hearts, displacing pure states through settled heedlessness; God defeats vile promptings with turning toward Him and supports realization with unveilings.
QUSHAYRI:v2p323/r9.anchor: فتعمل في القلوب بالفساد بسبب استيطان الغفلة حتى تتداعى القلوب للخراب من طوارق الحقائق

QUSHAYRI:v2p324/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p324/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p324/r1.claim: God overlooks lesser people for the sake of the great and pardons the common for the honor of the elect, preserving places of worship and refining sources of gnosis.
QUSHAYRI:v2p324/r1.anchor: يتجاوز عن الأصاغر لقدر الأكابر ، ويعفو عن العوام لاحترام الكرام

QUSHAYRI:v2p324/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p324/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p324/r2.claim: This is a lasting divine custom that will not be changed.
QUSHAYRI:v2p324/r2.anchor: ولا تحويل لسنته ، ولا تبديل لكريم عادته

BURHAN:v1p108/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p108/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p108/r5.claim: Ṣalāh generally denotes worship or mercy; in the phrase ṣalawāt wa-masājid it means houses of worship.
BURHAN:v1p108/r5.anchor: وكل صلاة فى القرآن فهى عبادة ورحمة إلا قوله تعالى ﴿ وصلوات ومساجد ﴾ فإنه يريد بيوت عبادتهم

BURHAN:v3p123/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p123/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p123/r7.claim: A second verb is implicit for prayers, which cannot literally be demolished: the churches and sanctuaries would be torn down and prayers abandoned.
BURHAN:v3p123/r7.anchor: والصلوات لا تهدم فالتقدير ولتركت صلوات

BURHAN:v4p237/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p237/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p237/r1.claim: The believers' saying “Our Lord is God” is no legitimate ground for expelling them from their homes.
BURHAN:v4p237/r1.anchor: فقولهم ﴿ ربنا الله ﴾ ليس بحق يوجب اخراجهم

BURHAN:v1p133/r17.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p133/r17.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p133/r17.claim: The wording إن الله لقوي عزيز, with an added lām, occurs twice in al-Ḥajj.
BURHAN:v1p133/r17.anchor: ﴿ إن الله لقوي عزيز ﴾ بزيادة اللام حرفان فى الحج

ITQAN:v2p418/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p418/r7.speaker: ابن فارس
ITQAN:v2p418/r7.claim: Ṣalāt usually means worship or mercy, but in the list with monasteries, churches, and mosques it means places of worship.
ITQAN:v2p418/r7.anchor: وكل صلاة فيه عبادة ورحمة إلا ﴿ وصلوات ومساجد ﴾ فهي الأماكن

ITQAN:v2p412/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p412/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p412/r9.claim: Al-ṣalah can refer to places of prayer.
ITQAN:v2p412/r9.anchor: 9 ومواضع الصلاة ﴿ وصلوات ومساجد ﴾ ﴿ لا تقربوا الصلاة ﴾

ITQAN:v1p254/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p254/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p254/r4.claim: The feminine tāʾ has disputed assimilation before six consonants, including ṣād in la-huddimat ṣawāmiʿ.
ITQAN:v1p254/r4.anchor: وتاء التأنيث اختلف فيها عند ستة أحرف الثاء ﴿ بعدت ثمود ﴾ والجيم ﴿ نضجت جلودهم ﴾ والزاي ﴿ خبت زدناهم ﴾ والسين ﴿ أنبتت سبع سنابل ﴾ والصاد ﴿ لهدمت صوامع ﴾

ITQAN:v3p239#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p239#2/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p239#2/r2.claim: Al-Suyūṭī gives the expulsion verse as another instance: the exception seems to state grounds for expulsion, but confessing God merits honor and strengthens the praise.
ITQAN:v3p239#2/r2.anchor: قلت ونظيرها قوله ﴿ وما نقموا إلا أن أغناهم الله ورسوله من فضله ﴾

ITQAN:v2p397/r18.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p397/r18.speaker: الجواليقي
ITQAN:v2p397/r18.claim: Al-Jawaliqi says some scholars considered biʿa, a church, an Arabized Persian word.
ITQAN:v2p397/r18.anchor: قال الجواليقي في كتاب المعرب البيعة والكنيسة جعلهما بعض العلماء

DAMGHANI:v1p231/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p231/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p231/r7.claim: Masājid can mean all the mosques where God's name is often remembered.
DAMGHANI:v1p231/r7.anchor: لهدمت صوامع وبيع وصلوات ومساجد يذكر فيها اسمه الله كثيرا

DAMGHANI:v1p282/r14.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p282/r14.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p282/r14.claim: Ṣalawāt can refer to houses of prayer.
DAMGHANI:v1p282/r14.anchor: الرابع الصلوات بيوت الصلاة قوله تعالى في سورة الحج لهدمت جوامع وبيع وصلوات ومساجد

DAMGHANI:v1p82/r13.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p82/r13.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p82/r13.claim: بيع can mean Christian churches; this is the sense in the verse listing churches, prayer houses, and mosques.
DAMGHANI:v1p82/r13.anchor: الرابع : البيعة بيعة النصارى . قوله تعالى في سورة الحج

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r13.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r13.claim: Ṣalawāt refers to Jewish places of worship.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p393/r13.anchor: والسابع : موضع الصلاة . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحج :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p586/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p586/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p586/r1.claim: Naṣr means help; intişār means taking revenge. Naṣr can also mean rain or coming to a place, as in the cited verse.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p586/r1.anchor: النصر : العون وانتصر فلان : انتقم . والنصر : المطر . والنصر : الإتيان

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p586/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p586/r2.speaker: الشاعر
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p586/r2.claim: The cited poem uses unṣurī to mean come to or visit a land.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p586/r2.anchor: إذا ودع الشهر الحرام فودعي … بلاد تميم وانصري أرض عامر

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p586/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p586/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p586/r4.claim: Naṣr can mean aid, including God’s support for those who support His cause.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p586/r4.anchor: والثاني : العون . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحج

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p293#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p293#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p293#4/r1.claim: Ṣawāmiʿ are the places of worship belonging to the Ṣābiʾūn.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p293#4/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p293#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p293#4/r2.claim: Biʿ are the churches of Christians.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p293#4/r2.anchor:
{وبيع} للنصارى.
{وصلوات} يريد بيوت صلوات، يعني كنائس اليهود.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p293#4/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p293#4/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p293#4/r3.claim: Ṣalawāt means the prayer houses of the Jews, that is, their synagogues.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p293#4/r3.anchor: {وصلوات} يريد بيوت صلوات، يعني كنائس اليهود.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p293#4/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p293#4/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p293#4/r5.claim: Qatāda says there are six religions, five belonging to Satan and one to the Merciful, and describes the Ṣābiʾūn, Magians, polytheists, Jews, and Christians.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p293#4/r5.anchor: هذا قول قتادة (4) وقال: الأديان ستة: خمسة للشيطان، وواحد للرحمن، فالصابئون: قوم يعبدون الملائكة

MAJAZ:v2p52/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p52/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p52/r1.claim: The exception is elliptical, with a pronoun understood: “except that they say the truth,” meaning “except that they say, ‘Our Lord is God.’”
MAJAZ:v2p52/r1.anchor: «الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم بغير حق إلا أن يقولوا ربنا الله» (40) مجازه مجاز المختصر الذي فيه ضمير

MAJAZ:v2p52/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p52/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p52/r2.claim: Ṣalawāt here means prayer places or chapels.

NAHHAS:v3p99/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p99/r8.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v3p99/r8.claim: On Sibawayh's analysis the accusative إلا أن يقولوا is an exception not drawn from the preceding class.
NAHHAS:v3p99/r8.anchor: على مذهب سيبويه استثناء ليس من الأول

NAHHAS:v3p99/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p99/r9.speaker: الفراء وأبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p99/r9.claim: Al-Farra and Abu Ishaq allow أن to be genitive through an understood ب; Abu Ishaq explains that the idolaters expelled them for professing God's oneness.
NAHHAS:v3p99/r9.anchor: وقال الفراء يجوز أن تكون أن في موضع خفض يقدرها مردودة على الباء

NAHHAS:v3p99/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p99/r10.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p99/r10.claim: Abu Ishaq paraphrases the exception as their being expelled because they said our Lord is God; idolaters drove them out for monotheism.
NAHHAS:v3p99/r10.anchor: والمعنى عنده الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم بغير حق إلا بأن يقولوا ربنا الله

NAHHAS:v3p99/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p99/r11.speaker: أبو الدرداء
NAHHAS:v3p99/r11.claim: Abu al-Darda says God wards off punishment through mosque-goers on behalf of those outside mosques and through fighters on behalf of those who do not fight.
NAHHAS:v3p99/r11.anchor: روي عن أبي الدرداء أنه قال لولا أن الله جل وعز يدفع بمن في المساجد

NAHHAS:v3p99/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p99/r12.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v3p99/r12.claim: Mujahid explains the divine defense as occurring through the recovery of rights by testimony.
NAHHAS:v3p99/r12.anchor: وروى ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد لولا أن الله جل وعز يدفع بأخذ الحقوق بالشهادات

NAHHAS:v3p99/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p99/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p99/r13.claim: صوامع and مساجد are diptotes because they are maximal plural forms, as are plurals with an alif after the third consonant followed by two or three letters.
NAHHAS:v3p99/r13.anchor: ولم ينصرف صوامع ومساجد لأنهما جمعان وهما نهاية الجموع فثقلا فمنعا الصرف

NAHHAS:v3p99/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p99/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p99/r14.claim: The closest grammatical antecedent makes فيها refer to mosques; it can also refer to all listed worship places, meaning their rites and the upholding of justice.
NAHHAS:v3p99/r14.anchor: أن يكون يذكر فيها اسم الله عائد على المساجد لا على غيرها لأن الضمير يليها

SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r1.claim: الذين أخرجوا may be genitive as an adjective, explanatory apposition, or substitute for the preceding relative expression.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r1.anchor: قوله: { الذين أخرجوا }: يجوز أن يكون في محل جر، نعتا للموصول الأول أو بيانا له، أو بدلا منه،

SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r2.claim: It may instead be accusative as an expression of praise or nominative after an implied subject.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r2.anchor: وأن يكون في محل نصب على المدح، وأن يكون في محل رفع على إضمار مبتدأ.

SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r3.claim: إلا أن يقولوا can be an accusative of disconnected exception; when the governor cannot apply, Arabs agree on accusative, as in ما زاد إلا ما نقص.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r3.anchor: قوله: { إلا أن يقولوا } فيه وجهان، أحدهما: أنه منصوب على الاستثناء المنقطع

SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r4.claim: When the governor can apply, both accusative Hijazi usage and an attached accusative or apposition are possible; here it cannot, since the phrase fails when بغير حق is omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r4.anchor: فلو توجه العامل جاز فيه لغتان: النصب وهو لغة الحجاز، وأن يكون كالمتصل في النصب والبدل

SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari and al-Zajjāj take the phrase as a genitive appositive to حق, meaning the sole cause was tawḥīd, which should warrant acknowledgment rather than expulsion; they compare 5:59.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r5.anchor: الثاني: أنه في محل جر بدلا من " حق " قال الزمخشري: " أي بغير موجب سوى التوحيد الذي ينبغي أن يكون موجب الإقرار

SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r6.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r6.claim: The Shaykh rejects the proposed genitive apposition: apposition requires a preceding negation, prohibition, or negative question and a governing element that can reach it; apposition to حق after غير yields an impossible construction.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r6.anchor: إلا أن الشيخ قد رد ذلك فقال: " ما أجازاه من البدل لا يجوز؛ لأن البدل لا يجوز إلا حيث سبقه نفي أو نهي

SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r7.claim: The author endorses the distinction between apposition and a descriptive construction where إلا means سوى, which al-Zamakhshari's illustration actually exemplifies.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40/r7.anchor: ثم إن الزمخشري حيث مثل البدل قدره: بغير موجب سوى التوحيد، وهذا تمثيل للصفة جعل [إلا] بمعنى سوى

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r1.claim: The author refers to an earlier discussion of the readings of ولولا دفع الله in 2:251.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r1.anchor: قوله: { ولولا دفع الله } قد تقدم الخلاف فيه في البقرة وتوجيه القراءتين.

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r2.speaker: نافع
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r2.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr read لهدمت with a light dāl; the others double it, signaling the many different places, though the light reading can bear that sense too.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ " لهدمت " بالتخفيف نافع وابن كثير. والباقون بالتثقيل الدال على التكثير؛ لأن المواضع كثيرة متعددة

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r3.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r3.claim: The general reading is صلوات with fatḥa on ṣād and lām.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r3.anchor: والعامة على " صلوات " بفتح الصاد واللام جمع صلاة.

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r4.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r4.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad reads with ḍamma on both letters; another report from him has ṣād kasra and lām sukūn.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ جعفر ابن محمد " وصلوات " بضمهما. وروي عنه أيضا بكسر الصاد وسكون اللام.

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r5.speaker: الجحدري
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r5.claim: Al-Jaḥdarī reads with ḍamma on ṣād and fatḥa on lām; Abū al-ʿĀliya reads with fatḥa on ṣād and sukūn on lām.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري بضم الصاد وفتح اللام. وأبو العالية بفتح الصاد وسكون اللام.

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r6.speaker: الجحدري
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r6.claim: Al-Jaḥdarī also reads صَلُوت, with ḍamma on ṣād and lām and a quiescent wāw.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r6.anchor: والجحدري أيضا " وصلوت " بضمهما وسكون الواو، بعدها تاء مثناة من فوق

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r7.speaker: الكلبي
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r7.claim: Al-Kalbī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read the same form with ث rather than ت.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r7.anchor: والكلبي والضحاك كذلك، إلا أنهما أعجما التاء بثلاث من فوقها.

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r8.speaker: الجحدري
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r8.claim: Al-Jaḥdarī, Abū al-ʿĀliya, Abū Rajāʾ, and Mujāhid add an alif after ث, reading صلوثا.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r8.anchor: والجحدري أيضا وأبو العالية وأبو رجاء ومجاهد كذلك، إلا أنهم جعلوا بعد الثاء المثلثة ألفا فقرؤوا " صلوثا "

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r9.speaker: مجاهد
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r9.claim: A further report from Mujāhid has the form with the two-dot tāʾ rather than ث.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r9.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد في هذه التاء المثناة من فوق أيضا.

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r10.speaker: الجحدري
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r10.claim: Al-Jaḥdarī also reads صلواث with ḍamma on ṣād, sukūn on lām, and an alif after wāw before ث.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r10.anchor: وروي عن الجحدري أيضا " صلواث " بضم الصاد وسكون اللام وألف بعد الواو والثاء مثلثة.

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r11.speaker: عكرمة
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r11.claim: ʿIkrima reads صلويثى with ṣād kasra, lām sukūn, a kasra on wāw, then yāʾ and ث.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة " صلويثى " بكسر الصاد وسكون اللام، وبعدها واو مكسورة

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r12.speaker: ابن مجاهد
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r12.claim: Ibn Mujāhid records صلواث with ṣād kasra, lām sukūn, and an alif after wāw before ث.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r12.anchor: وحكى ابن مجاهد أنه قرىء " صلواث " بكسر الصاد وسكون اللام. بعدها واو، بعدها ألف،

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r13.speaker: الجحدري
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r13.claim: Al-Jaḥdarī reads صلوب, like كعوب, as an anomalous plural of صليب on the فعول pattern.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r13.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري " وصلوب " مثل كعوب بالباء الموحدة وهو جمع " صليب "

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r14.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r14.claim: A report from Abū ʿAmr has the common form without tanwīn, treating it as a proper foreign place-name.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r14.anchor: وروي عن أبي عمرو " صلوات " كالعامة، إلا أنه لم ينون، منعه الصرف للعلمية والعجمة

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r15.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r15.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r15.claim: The author counts fourteen readings in all and says only the familiar prayer-word reading is well known.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r15.anchor: فهذه أربع عشرة قراءة، المشهور منها واحدة، وهي هذه الصلاة المعهودة.

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r16.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r16.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r16.claim: A deleted مضاف is needed for buildings to be demolished: مواضع صلوات.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r16.anchor: ولا بد من حذف مضاف ليصح تسلط الهدم عليها أي: مواضع صلوات،

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r17.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r17.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r17.claim: Alternatively هدمت means made inactive, applicable to both places and acts.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r17.anchor: أو يضمن " هدمت " معنى " عطلت " فيكون قدرا مشتركا بين المواضع والأفعال

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r18.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r18.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r18.claim: In different communities, the prayers or worship named صلوات vary according to each community's practice.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r18.anchor: والصلوات في الأمم...... صلاة كل ملة بحسبها.

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r19.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r19.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r19.claim: The mosques come last because they arose later, or because the sequence moves to the noblest place of worship.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r19.anchor: وأخر المساجد لحدوثها في الوجود، أو الانتقال إلى الأشرف.

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r20.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r20.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r20.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats صلوات itself as a place-name for a synagogue because prayer is performed there; another account derives it from Hebrew صلوثا.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#2/r20.anchor: وظاهر كلام الزمخشري أنها بنفسها اسم مكان فإنه قال: " وسميت الكنسية صلاة لأنه يصلى فيها.

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#3/r1.claim: The uncommon forms are said to be Syriac or Hebrew words that entered Arabic, accounting for their many variant forms.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#3/r1.anchor: وأما غيرها من القراءات فقيل: هي سريانية أو عبرانية دخلت في لسان العرب.

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#3/r2.claim: صوامع are tall buildings with narrow, pointed tops; the word relates to أصمع, sharp or keen in speech, and follows the فوعلة pattern.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#3/r2.anchor: والصوامع: جمع صومعة وهي البناء المرتفع الحديد الأعلى، من قولهم رجل أصمع،

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#3/r3.claim: صوامع are identified as monks' places of worship because monks withdraw there, or alternatively as Sabaean temples.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#3/r3.anchor: وهي متعبد الرهبان لأنهم ينفردون. وقيل: متعبد الصابئين.

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#3/r4.claim: البيع is the plural of بيعة, a Christian place of worship; another view identifies them as Jewish churches.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#3/r4.anchor: والبيع: جمع بيعة، وهي متعبد النصارى. وقيل: كنائس اليهود.

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#3/r5.claim: The more widely accepted mapping is monasteries for monks, churches for Christians, prayer-houses for Jews, and mosques for Muslims.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#3/r5.anchor: والأشهر أن الصوامع للرهبان والبيع للنصارى، والصلوات لليهود، والمساجد للمسلمين.

SAMIN-DURR:22:40#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#3/r6.claim: يذكر فيها may modify all the listed places if فيها refers to them all, or only the mosques if its pronoun is restricted; the first reading is more apparent.
SAMIN-DURR:22:40#3/r6.anchor: أو صفة للمساجد فقط، إن خصصنا الضمير في " فيها " بها، والأول أظهر.

ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r1.claim: الذين is genitive under an omitted أذن, meaning permission was given to those expelled from their homes.
ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r1.anchor: أذن للذين أخرجوا من ديارهم بغير حق

ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r2.claim: أن is genitive after the exception: they were expelled for no just cause except professing that God is their Lord.
ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r2.anchor: أخرجوا بلا حق، إلا بقولهم ربنا الله

ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r3.claim: Idol worshippers expelled the believers because they affirmed God's oneness.
ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r3.anchor: أي لم يخرجوا إلا بأن وحدوا الله

ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r4.claim: The implicit construction is لو لا أن دفع الله بعض الناس ببعض, had God not caused some people to repel others.
ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r4.anchor: ولولا أن دفع الله بعض الناس ببعض

ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r5.claim: The passage also has a reading لهدمت; صوامع are monks' monasteries, بيع Christian churches, and صلوات Jewish synagogues, called ṣəlōtā in Hebrew.

ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r6.claim: Another reading has the singular صلاة; one explanation identifies the prayer sites as places of worship belonging to the Sabians.
ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r6.anchor: وقرئت صلاة ومساجد، وقيل إنها موضع

ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r7.claim: Without mutual defense, every prophet's community would have seen its worship place demolished: synagogues in Moses' era, monasteries and churches in Jesus' era, and mosques in Muhammad's era.
ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r7.anchor: فكان لولا الدفع لهدم في زمن موسى عليه السلام

ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r8.claim: God supports whoever upholds one of His revealed laws, while each prophet's law permits only what that prophet brought and forbids what he prohibited.
ZAJJAJ:v3p430/r8.anchor: أي من أقام شريعة من شرائعه، نصر على إقامة ذلك

ASAD-NOTES:22:39#n58/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:22:39#n58/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:22:39#n58/r1.claim: Asad glosses God's repelling some people by means of others and links the phrase to 2:251.
ASAD-NOTES:22:39#n58/r1.anchor: Lit., "were it not that God repels some people by means of others" (cf. the identical phrase in the second paragraph of 2:251).

ASAD-NOTES:22:39#n59/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:22:39#n59/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:22:39#n59/r1.claim: Defending religious freedom is the foremost cause for which arms may and must be taken up; without it corruption would overwhelm the earth.
ASAD-NOTES:22:39#n59/r1.anchor: The implication is that the defence of religious freedom is the foremost cause for which arms may and, indeed, must - be taken up

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#2/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#2/r2.claim: Strength precedes might because being strong leads to being victorious and mighty.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#2/r2.anchor: ومنه تقديم القوة على العزة لأنه قوي فعزّ أي غلب فالقوة أول

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p30/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p30/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p30/r2.claim: Power precedes might because God conquers through power.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p30/r2.anchor: تقديم القوة على العزة لأنه قوي فعزّ أي غلب بالقوة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p481/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p481/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p481/r2.claim: Power precedes might because strength enables domination: He is powerful, so He prevails.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p481/r2.anchor: ومنه تقديم القوة على العزة لأنه قوي فعزّ أي غلب بالقوة فالقوة أول قال تعالى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p618/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p618/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p618/r2.claim: Qur’anic and Arabic fronting does not always signal greater merit: mosques are best in this list, yet the context warrants listing them last; Moses and Aaron also change order by context.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p618/r2.anchor: هي أفضل المذكور في الآية لكن أحياناً يُقدّم ما هو أقل تفضيلاً

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r1.claim: The idolaters and their People of the Book supporters delude themselves that they are Abraham’s true custodians and may bar the Prophet and followers from the House.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r1.anchor: they think that it is they who are the real custodians of Abraham’s religion and the House of God and hence have the right to close its doors

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r2.claim: Abraham built the House for worship of the one God and pilgrimage, not for idolatry and polytheism.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r2.anchor: Abraham (sws) never built this House for idolatry and polytheism. On the other hand, they have precisely done this.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r3.claim: Attention to the real essence of animal sacrifice and Hajj rituals urges Abraham’s legacy claimants to reevaluate their beliefs.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r3.anchor: attention is directed to the real essence of animal sacrifice and other rituals of ḥajj

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r4.claim: The claimants have distorted Abraham’s legacy and are bent on expelling those who seek to revive it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r4.anchor: they have totally distorted his legacy and his teachings. To make matters worse, they are bent upon expelling those who are trying to revive this legacy.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r5.claim: Verses 38–41 are Medinan; after migration, Muslims faced the question of what to do if Quraysh blocked their pilgrimage.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r5.anchor: the question arose as to what they should do if they go for ḥajj and the disbelievers try to stop them?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r6.claim: Although fighting in sacred months near the House was prohibited even in jāhiliyyah, Quraysh used that sanctity as a shield and Muslims would not breach it without God’s permission.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r6.anchor: waging war in the sacred months and that too within the vicinity of the House of God was regarded as prohibited even in the times of jāhiliyyah.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r7.claim: If war becomes inevitable, Muslims may retaliate; this does not violate sacred months but is a holy war to cleanse the House and, if able, liberate it from usurpers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r7.anchor: This war does not violate the sanctity of the sacred months; in fact, it is a holy war for the cleansing of the House of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r8.claim: Treating such war as impious would leave monotheistic houses of worship to enemies who could destroy them or turn them into idol centers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r8.anchor: all houses of worship that have been built for the One God are being consigned to the disbelievers and their accomplices.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r9.claim: Muslims should not hesitate at war or heed opponents’ accusations; despite their small numbers and scarce resources, God will grant them authority in Makkah.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r9.anchor: in spite of their small number and scarcity of resources, God will help them to grant them authority in the land of Makkah.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r10.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r10.claim: Once empowered, Muslims should cleanse the Ḥaram of polytheism and disbelief and restore the purpose for which Abraham settled the land.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r10.anchor: they should cleanse the Ḥaram from the filth of polytheism and disbelief and revive the objectives

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r11.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r11.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r11.claim: Though Medinan, these verses are placed in a Makkan sūrah because Quraysh’s illegitimate occupation follows the prior argument and this permission answers prevailing circumstances.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p164/r11.anchor: they were placed here in a Makkan sūrah so that it becomes evident that this permission was given because of the prevailing circumstances.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p204/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p204/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p204/r1.claim: The preceding account of the House and its rites shows that Quraysh violated its sanctity and therefore had no right to remain its occupants.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p204/r1.anchor: it is shown that the Quraysh have totally

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p204/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p204/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p204/r2.claim: The preceding verses imply that Muslims, rather than Quraysh, are the House's true custodians, but they were powerless in Makkah; after migration they formed a community and sought its blessings.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p204/r2.anchor: the real custodians of the House of God are the Muslims and not the Quraysh. However, in Makkah, they were utterly helpless

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p204/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p204/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p204/r3.claim: The expelled Muslims could expect Quraysh to deny them pilgrimage; attempting ḥajj or ʿumrah could bring war within the Ḥaram during sacred months, forbidden in both jāhiliyyah custom and Islam.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p204/r3.anchor: within the precincts of the Ḥaram in the sacred months, something regarded to be forbidden both in the jāhiliyyah customs and in Islam

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p204/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p204/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p204/r4.claim: Quraysh and its People of the Book allies used the issue to accuse Muslims of violating sacred places; the following verses answer the questions this raised.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p204/r4.anchor: In the following verses, these questions have been answered

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p206/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p206/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p206/r7.claim: The description explains the oppression in the previous verse: Muslims were expelled without committing a crime, and the wording evokes the hardship of leaving one's homeland under compulsion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p206/r7.anchor: no one leaves his house and homeland unless he is utterly compelled

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p206/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p206/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p206/r8.claim: The sentence is highly eloquent: the only alleged offence was declaring God their Lord, so their greatest virtue and truth was made their greatest sin.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p206/r8.anchor: their greatest virtue and the greatest truth they preached became their greatest sin

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p206/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p206/r9.speaker: Some people
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p206/r9.claim: Some interpreters take the monotheistic declaration to mean that belief in one God is no offence and Quraysh harassed Muslims over an innocuous belief.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p206/r9.anchor: Some people have interpreted this last sentence to refer to the fact that here the Qur’ān is presenting this declaration of monotheism

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r1.claim: Islahi rejects the view that Quraysh dismissed monotheism as harmless: they understood its far-reaching implications and opposed the greatest truth, a folly the Qur'an subtly exposes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r1.anchor: They knew its far reaching consequences and hence they were its enemies

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r2.claim: Ṣawāmiʿ is the plural of ṣawmaʿah, used primarily for lofty structures where Christian monks lived in seclusion; monasteries is an apt translation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r2.anchor: It is primarily used for the lofty mountains and buildings in which Christian monks would live in seclusion

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r3.claim: Biyaʿ is the plural of biʿah and denotes Jewish and Christian worship places; because ṣalawāt separately names Jewish prayer places, he takes biyaʿ here to mean Christian churches.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r3.anchor: this word must be considered specific to Christian places of worship

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r4.claim: Churches and monasteries held equal importance for Christians because of their system of monasticism.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r4.anchor: both churches and monastries held equal importance to them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r5.claim: Ṣalawāt means places where Jews prayed; their word for prayer, ṣalwota, is Aramaic.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r6.claim: Masājid is the common word for Muslims' mosques.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r6.anchor: is commonly used for the mosques of Muslims

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r7.claim: God permits believers to fight even within the Ḥaram to defend themselves and protect religious values and symbols; prophets and messengers were likewise allowed jihad for this purpose, and Muslims received this permission to protect the Ḥaram.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r7.anchor: God has always allowed His prophets and messengers to wage jihād and they have waged it to protect their religious values and symbols

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r8.claim: If the House's deceitful current custodians obstruct Muslims from defending it, Islahi says they should be repaid in kind.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r8.anchor: If its current deceitful and fraudulent claimants to custodianship imepede them in any way, they should be paid back in their own coin

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r9.claim: Quraysh accused Muslims of disregarding the Ḥaram's sanctity, joined in this campaign by Jews and Christians, who portrayed Muslim jihad as contrary to religious sentiment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r9.anchor: The Jews and Christians too joined them in this vicious campaign and regarded the attitude of the Muslims to be against sentiments of religiosity

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r10.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r10.claim: The Qur'an answers that if jihad for God meant violating religiosity, evil would have free rein to destroy religion itself.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r10.anchor: it would mean that evil is given full freedom to wreck havoc and obliterate religion itself

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r11.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r11.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r11.claim: Christian monasteries and churches are named first because Christians were the strongest critics of Muslim jihad, with their concept of monasticism contributing greatly to their opposition.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p207/r11.anchor: The reason for this foremost mention is that they it was they who were the most critical of the Muslim spirit of jihād

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r1.claim: Those who call jihad irreligious should recognize that without it none of God's places of worship would have survived.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r1.anchor: if this concept pre-existed, none of God’s worship places on earth would have survived

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r2.claim: Jewish and Christian worship places originally had the same standing as Muslim mosques; deviation arose when the People of the Book embraced polytheism and religious innovations.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r2.anchor: the worship places of the Jews and the Christians mentioned here primarily had the same status as mosques of the Muslims

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r3.claim: The promise of divine help is reiterated: those who protect God's symbols are helping their Lord, so God in turn will help them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r3.anchor: those who strive to protect the symbols of God, in fact help their Lord

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r4.claim: Only people who fulfil their duty to the cause of truth merit God's help; He does not grant effortless comfort to those demanding it, as the Israelites did.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r4.anchor: He does not help those, who like the Israelites demand that God should provide them with a bed of roses without any effort from their own side

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r5.claim: God is powerful and needs no one's help; those who help Him are opening the way for His help to reach themselves.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r5.anchor: Since God is mighty and powerful, He does not need the help of anyone

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r6.claim: Muslims should not fear being few against many enemies, since the majestic God promising their help is powerful and dominant.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r6.anchor: Muslims should not feel scared because of their own small number and the large number of their enemies

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r7.claim: Disbelievers should not infer that a small Muslim group can achieve nothing: with God behind them, these drops will become a storm.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p208/r7.anchor: These drops will now become a storm because God is behind them and God is mighty and powerful

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p278#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p278#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p278#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read يدفع and دفع without alif; دفع is the verbal noun of دفع.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p278#2/r1.anchor: قراءة ابن كثير وأبي عمرو: (إن الله يدفع) ولولا دفع الله جعلوا الدفع مصدر دفع،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p278#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p278#2/r2.speaker: نافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p278#2/r2.claim: Nafi reads both forms with alif, treating دفاع as the verbal noun of دافع, like قتال from قاتل.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p278#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع: إن الله يدافع عن الذين آمنوا، (ولولا دفاع الله) بألف.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p278#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p278#2/r3.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p278#2/r3.claim: These readers combine يدافع with دفع; the author allows فاعل here to carry the sense of فعل.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p278#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي: إن الله يدافع بألف، ولولا دفع الله بغير ألف .

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p278#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p278#2/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p278#2/r5.claim: With يدفع, دفاع can be a verbal noun of triliteral دفع, like كتاب from كتب, rather than a noun of دافع.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p278#2/r5.anchor: ولو قرأ قارئ: (ولولا دفاع الله الناس) وقرأ: (إن الله يدفع) لجاز أن يكون الدفاع من دفع، كالكتاب من كتب

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p279/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p279/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p279/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir and Nafi read لهدمت with a light د; the other readers read it with a doubled د.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p279/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع: (لهدمت صوامع) خفيفة الدال وقرأ الباقون: لهدمت مشددة الدال .

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p279/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p279/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p279/r2.claim: The light form هدمت applies to little or much, while the doubled form is specific to extensive demolition.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p279/r2.anchor: هدمت يكون للقليل والكثير، يدلك على ذلك أنك تقول: ضربت زيدا ضربة، وضربته ألف ضربة

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p279/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p279/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p279/r3.claim: The doubled form is supported by Quranic وغلقت and a poet's repeated opening and closing of doors.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p279/r3.anchor: وأغلقها ... حتى أتيت أبا عمرو بن عمار

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p253#2/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p253#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p253#2/r2.claim: Doubling dāl conveys repeated demolition; light dāl conveys a single act. Both forms are common Arabic usage.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p253#2/r2.anchor: يقرأ بتشديد الدال وتخفيفها فالحجة لمن شدد أنه أراد تكرير الفعل

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p253#2/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p253#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p253#2/r3.claim: “Dafʿ Allāh” and “yudāfiʿ” have readings with fatḥa on dāl and no alif or kasra with alif; the author refers to his earlier explanation in al-Baqara.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p253#2/r3.anchor: يقرآن بفتح الدال من غير ألف وبكسرها وإثبات الألف وقد ذكرت علته في البقرة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p437/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p437/r5.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p437/r5.claim: These readers use light dāl in لهدمت; Abu ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim, Hamza, and al-Kisāʾī geminate it.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p437/r5.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع ﴿ لهدمت ﴾ خفيفة وقرأ أبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائى

NASHR:v2p4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p4/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p4/r1.claim: In the preceding, partly omitted consonant section, al-Shadhāʾī alone reports a choice for Ibn al-Akhram before shīn; Warsh assimilates before ḍād and ẓāʾ, while special routes vary elsewhere.
NASHR:v2p4/r1.anchor: وانفرد الشذائي بحكاية التخيير في الشين عن ابن الأخرم وأدغمها ورش في الضاد والظاء

NASHR:v2p4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p4/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي
NASHR:v2p4/r2.claim: The feminine tāʾ assimilates before thāʾ, jīm, ẓāʾ, and the sibilants; Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī assimilate it across all six letters.
NASHR:v2p4/r2.anchor: فأدغمها في الحروف الستة أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي

NASHR:v2p4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p4/r3.speaker: الأزرق عن ورش
NASHR:v2p4/r3.claim: Al-Azraq’s Warsh route assimilates the feminine tāʾ only before ẓāʾ; Khalaf displays before thāʾ, while Ibn ʿĀmir and Hishām have their stated assimilation sets.
NASHR:v2p4/r3.anchor: وأدغمها الأزرق عن ورش في الظاء فقط

NASHR:v2p4/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p4/r4.speaker: هشام
NASHR:v2p4/r4.claim: Hishām differs on sīn, jīm, and zāy: al-Dājūnī’s and selected al-Ḥulwānī routes assimilate, while al-Ḥulwānī’s other routes display.
NASHR:v2p4/r4.anchor: وأدغمها هشام في الثاء. واختلف عنه في حروف (سجز)

NASHR:v2p4/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p4/r5.speaker: الحلواني
NASHR:v2p4/r5.claim: For لهدمت صوامع, most al-Ḥulwānī transmitters display, as in major manuals; al-Kāfī records both, while some assimilation routes exempt this word, outside the author’s routes.
NASHR:v2p4/r5.anchor: واختلف عن الحلواني في لهدمت صوامع فروى الجمهور عنه إظهارها

NASHR:v2p4/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p4/r6.speaker: صاحب التجريد
NASHR:v2p4/r6.claim: Some authorities who transmit al-Ḥulwānī’s assimilation exempt لهدمت صوامع and sometimes نضجت جلودهم; al-Tajrīd adds jīm and ṣād exceptions on a specific route, not the known Jamāl route.
NASHR:v2p4/r6.anchor: وأضاف بعضهم إليها نضجت جلودهم فاستثناها أيضا كصاحب المستنير والغاية والتجريد

NASHR:v2p4/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p4/r7.speaker: ابن ذكوان
NASHR:v2p4/r7.claim: Ibn Dhakwān displays before sīn, jīm, and zāy; on thāʾ al-Ṣūrī displays while al-Akhfash assimilates, which the author identifies as correct despite inconsistent manuals.
NASHR:v2p4/r7.anchor: وأظهرها ابن ذكوان عند حروف (سجز) المتقدمة

NASHR:v2p4/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p4/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p4/r9.claim: The author rejects as mistaken Abū al-ʿAlāʾ’s unique report that al-Ṣūrī displays before ḍād.
NASHR:v2p4/r9.anchor: وانفرد الحافظ أبو العلاء بالإظهار عن الصوري عند الضاد وهو وهم

NASHR:v2p326/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p326/r1.speaker: ابن كثير، والبصريان
NASHR:v2p326/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir and the Basrans read يدفع without an alif; the remaining readers read يدافع with an alif.
NASHR:v2p326/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير، والبصريان (يدفع) بفتح الياء والفاء

NASHR:v2p326/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p326/r2.speaker: الباقون
NASHR:v2p326/r2.claim: The remaining readers read يدافع, with ḍamma on yāʾ, fatḥa on dāl, an alif, and kasra on fāʾ.
NASHR:v2p326/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بضم الياء وفتح الدال وألف بعدها مع كسر الفاء

NASHR:v2p326/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p326/r7.speaker: المدنيان، وابن كثير
NASHR:v2p326/r7.claim: The two Medinans and Ibn Kathir read لهدمت with a light dāl; the others read it with a doubled dāl. The author refers to an earlier discussion of tāʾ assimilation.
NASHR:v2p326/r7.anchor: قرأ المدنيان، وابن كثير بتخفيف الدال، وقرأ الباقون بتشديدها

QIRAAT-ER:22:40:15#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:22:40:15#1/r1.speaker: Lvw
QIRAAT-ER:22:40:15#1/r1.claim: Form III difāʿ suggests sustained or reciprocal defense, while Form I dafʿ can indicate a single act of pushing.
QIRAAT-ER:22:40:15#1/r1.anchor: difāʿ (Form III verbal noun) vs. dafʿ (Form I) — difāʿ implies sustained/reciprocal defense; dafʿ implies single-act pushing

QIRAAT-ER:22:40:22#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:22:40:22#1/r1.speaker: Vr
QIRAAT-ER:22:40:22#1/r1.claim: Form I passive indicates simple demolition, whereas standard Form II suggests thorough or repeated destruction.
QIRAAT-ER:22:40:22#1/r1.anchor: Form I passive hudimat (simple demolition) vs. standard Form II huddimat (intensive demolition) — both canonical

IBNHISHAM:v1p467#2/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p467#2/r1.speaker: عروة بن الزبير وغيره من العلماء
IBNHISHAM:v1p467#2/r1.claim: Before the Aqaba pledge, Muslims had no permission to fight and were told to call to God, endure harm, and pardon; after Quraysh persecuted and expelled them, this passage was the first permission to fight, according to reports from Urwa and other scholars.
IBNHISHAM:v1p467#2/r1.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل بيعة العقبة لم يؤذن له في الحرب ولم تحلل له الدماء

IBNHISHAM:v1p467#2/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p467#2/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p467#2/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq says fighting was permitted because the Muslims were wronged and had committed no offense against people except worshipping God alone.
IBNHISHAM:v1p467#2/r2.anchor: أي أني إنما أحللت لهم القتال لأنهم ظلموا، ولم يكن لهم ذنب فيما بينهم وبين الناس، إلا أن يعبدوا الله

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p39#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p39#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p39#2/r1.claim: Qatāda identifies the hermitages as belonging to the Ṣābiʾūn.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p39#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ لهدمت صوامع ﴾ قال هي للصابئين

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p39#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p39#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p39#2/r2.claim: Qatāda identifies the churches as belonging to the Christians.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p39#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ لهدمت صوامع ﴾ قال هي للصابئين ﴿ وبيع ﴾ للنصارى

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p39#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p39#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p39#2/r3.claim: Qatāda identifies ṣalawāt as Jewish synagogues.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p39#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ لهدمت صوامع ﴾ قال هي للصابئين ﴿ وبيع ﴾ للنصارى ﴿ وصلوات ﴾ قال كنائس اليهود

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p39#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p39#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p39#2/r4.claim: Qatāda identifies the mosques as Muslim mosques.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p39#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ لهدمت صوامع ﴾ قال هي للصابئين ﴿ وبيع ﴾ للنصارى ﴿ وصلوات ﴾ قال كنائس اليهود والمساجد مساجد المسلمين

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولهتعالى@QB@لاعاصماليومم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولهتعالى@QB@لاعاصماليومم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولهتعالى@QB@لاعاصماليومم.claim: Sībawayh glosses the exception in 22:40 as adversative لكن: they were expelled without right, but they say, 'Our Lord is God'; he gives three parallel Qur'anic examples.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولهتعالى@QB@لاعاصماليومم.anchor: أخرجوا من ديارهم بغير حق إلا أن يقولوا ربنا الله

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولهتعالى@QB@لاعاصماليومم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولهتعالى@QB@لاعاصماليومم.speaker: أبو الخطاب
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولهتعالى@QB@لاعاصماليومم.claim: Abū al-Khaṭṭāb reports idioms like ما زاد إلا ما نقص; ما with a verb functions as a noun or verbal noun, allowing this construction after إلا.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولهتعالى@QB@لاعاصماليومم.anchor: الخطاب ما زاد إلا ما نقص وما نفع إلا ما ضر

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولهتعالى@QB@لاعاصماليومم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولهتعالى@QB@لاعاصماليومم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولهتعالى@QB@لاعاصماليومم.claim: Nabigha and Nabigha al-Jaʿdī use غير أن with the same corrective force as لكن, introducing a qualification rather than a true exception.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولهتعالى@QB@لاعاصماليومم.anchor: ومثل ذلك من الشعر قول النابغة

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولهتعالى@QB@لاعاصماليومم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولهتعالى@QB@لاعاصماليومم.speaker: الفرزدق
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولهتعالى@QB@لاعاصماليومم.claim: Al-Farazdaq's غير أني ابن غالب is another poetic example of the corrective sense 'but I am the son of Ghālib.'
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولهتعالى@QB@لاعاصماليومم.anchor: قول الفرزدق # % وما سجنوني غير أني ابن غالب

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولهتعالى@QB@لاعاصماليومم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولهتعالى@QB@لاعاصماليومم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولهتعالى@QB@لاعاصماليومم.claim: The Banu Mazin line attributed to ʿAnz ibn Dujāja gives another example of إلا in the corrective sense 'but'.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولهتعالى@QB@لاعاصماليومم.anchor: إلا كناشرة الذي ضيعتم % % كالغصن في غلوائه المتنبت

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولهتعالى@QB@لاعاصماليومم.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولهتعالى@QB@لاعاصماليومم.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولهتعالى@QB@لاعاصماليومم.claim: The closing poetic example also uses إلا adversatively after a negative construction, with the sense 'but like the camel handler who deliberately abuses me.'
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولهتعالى@QB@لاعاصماليومم.anchor: إلا كمعرض المحسر بكره % % عمدا يسببنى على الظلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p515/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p515/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p515/r4.claim: الذين أخرجوا may be a genitive adjective to the preceding relative, an appositive, an accusative explanatory phrase, or a nominative phrase with an implied subject.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p515/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p515/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p515/r5.claim: إلا أن يقولوا is a disconnected exception in the accusative, semantically approximating لكن, because the governing verb cannot reach it; Arabs unanimously use accusative in this construction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p515/r5.anchor: وإلا أن يقولوا استثناء منقطع فإن يقولوا في موضع نصب لأنه منقطع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p515/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p515/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق والزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p515/r6.claim: Abu Ishaq and al-Zamakhshari allow a genitive appositive after بغير حق, interpreting the sole cause of expulsion as confessing God’s oneness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p515/r6.anchor: وأجاز أبو إسحاق فيه الجر على البدل واتبعه الزمخشري فقال أن يقولوا في محل الجر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p515/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p515/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p515/r7.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects that apposition: badal requires prior negation, prohibition or a negative question, and here the positive العامل cannot govern the exception; al-Zamakhshari also confuses badal with description by سوى.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p515/r7.anchor: وما أجازاه من البدل لا يجوز لأن البدل لا يكون إلا إذا سبقه نفي أو نهي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r1.claim: The clause urges the fighting just permitted: God customarily uses it to maintain order and religious law, protect places of worship from demolition and their people from killing and dispersal.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r1.anchor: الآية فيها تحريض على القتال المأذون فيه قبل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r2.claim: Abu Hayyan links this wording to the account of David killing Goliath after Saul’s fighting; without such defense, the earth would be corrupted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r2.anchor: وانظر إلى مجيء قوله ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض لفسدت الأرض إثر قتال طالوت لجالوت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r3.claim: ‘Ali says God’s defense through Muhammad’s Companions kept disbelievers from overrunning later generations.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r3.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب: ولولا دفع الله بأصحاب محمد الكفار عن التابعين فمن بعدهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains defense as God empowering believers to overcome disbelievers through striving; otherwise polytheists would dominate religious communities and demolish their sanctuaries, including those of Muslims and protected People of Scripture.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r4.anchor: دفع الله بعض الناس ببعض إظهاره وتسليط المؤمنين منهم على الكافرين بالمجاهدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r5.claim: Mujahid interprets the defense as stopping a people’s injustice through just witnesses and similar means.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: ولولا دفع الله ظلم قوم بشهادات العدول ونحو هذا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r6.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r6.claim: Some say rulers’ justice averts the injustice of oppressors.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r6.anchor: وقال قوم دفع ظلم الظلمة بعدل الولاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r7.speaker: فرقة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r7.claim: Another group interprets the defense as punishment averted through the prayers of righteous people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r7.anchor: وقالت فرقة دفع العذاب بدعاء الأخيار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r8.speaker: قطرب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r8.claim: Qutrub says retaliation preserves people from one another’s violence.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r9.claim: Another view takes the defense to be prophets protecting believers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r9.anchor: بالقصاص عن النفوس. وقيل: بالنبيين عن المؤمنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r10.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r10.claim: Al-Hasan says that without Islam’s security, the worship places of protected non-Muslims would be destroyed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r10.anchor: وقال الحسن: لولا أمان الإسلام لخربت متعبدات أهل الذمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r11.claim: The meaning of defense through fighting best fits this verse and most effectively prevents corruption.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r11.anchor: ومعنى الدفع بالقتال أليق بالآية وأمكن في دفع الفساد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r12.speaker: الحرميان وأيوب وقتادة وطلحة وزائدة عن الأعمش والزعفراني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r12.claim: The Two Sanctuary readers, Ayyub, Qatadah, Talhah, Zaidah from al-A‘mash and al-Za‘farani read فهدمت without gemination; the remaining Seven and others geminate, fitting repeated demolition of many sites.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r12.anchor: وقرأ الحرميان وأيوب وقتادة وطلحة وزائدة عن الأعمش والزعفراني فهدمت مخففا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r13.speaker: الجمهور وجعفر بن محمد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r13.claim: The majority read وصلوات as the plural of صلاة; Ja‘far ibn Muhammad reads it with ḍamma on both ṣād and lām.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r14.speaker: ابن خالويه والجحدري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r14.claim: Ibn Khalawayh reports from Ja‘far a form with kasra on ṣād and a still lām; al-Jahdari also has ḍamma on ṣād and fatḥa on lām.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r14.anchor: وحكى عنه ابن خالويه صلوات بسكون اللام وكسر الصاد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r15.speaker: الكلبي وأبو العالية والحجاج بن يوسف ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r15.claim: Al-Kalbi and Abu al-‘Aliya have fatḥa on ṣād and a still lām; al-Hajjaj and al-Jahdari read وصلوت without alif, while Mujahid adds alif after tā’.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r15.anchor: وحكيت عن الكلبي وأبي العالية بفتح الصاد وسكون اللام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r16.speaker: الضحاك والكلبي وأبو رجاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r16.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi read وصلوث without alif; Abu Raja‘, al-Jahdari, Abu al-‘Aliya and Mujahid are also reported with the variant that adds alif after tha.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r16.anchor: والضحاك والكلبي وصلوث بضمتين من غير ألف وبثاء منقوطة بثلاث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r17.speaker: عكرمة والجحدري وابن مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r17.claim: ‘Ikrima reads وصلويثا with kasra on ṣād, a still lām and kasra on wāw; al-Jahdari has a form with wāw and tha, and Ibn Mujahid reports it with kasra on ṣād.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r17.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة: وصلويثا بكسر الصاد وإسكان اللام وواو مكسورة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r18.speaker: الحجاج والجحدري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r18.claim: Al-Hajjaj and al-Jahdari are also reported to read صلوب with one ba, a rare plural of صليب on the pattern فعيل فعول; Abu Hayyan counts thirteen readings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p516/r18.anchor: وحكى ابن خالويه وابن عطية عن الحجاج والجحدري صلوب بالباء بواحدة على وزن كعوب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r1.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r1.claim: Some say the word denotes Jewish synagogues and is borrowed from Syriac; another says it is Hebrew.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r1.anchor: قيل: هي مساجد اليهود هي بالسريانية مما دخل في كلام العرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r2.claim: Ibn ‘Atiyya says the majority reading means the customary prayers of the religious communities; altered foreign forms should be explained from the source language.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r2.anchor: وينبغي أن تكون قراءة الجمهور يراد بها الصلوات المعهودة في الملل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r3.speaker: خصيف
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r3.claim: Khasif assigns monasteries to monks or Sabians, churches to Christians, synagogues to Jews and mosques to Muslims.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r3.anchor: والأظهر في تعداد هذه المواضع أن ذلك بحسب معتقدات الأمم فالصوامع للرهبان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r4.claim: Ibn ‘Atiyya prefers a rhetorical abundance of worship places: most names are shared across nations, while bay‘a is conventionally Christian; Zoroastrians and polytheists are omitted because their sanctuaries lack protection and divine remembrance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r4.anchor: قال ابن عطية: والأظهر أنه قصد بها المبالغة في ذكر المتعبدات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r5.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil take فيها to refer collectively to all the named places, making يذكر a modifier of the whole list.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r5.anchor: والظاهر عود الضمير في قوله يذكر فيها على المواضع كلها جميعها وقاله الكلبي ومقاتل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r6.claim: If صلوات means acts of prayer, either supply an omitted مضاف meaning prayer places or understand demolition to include disabling, common to buildings and acts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r6.anchor: وإذا حملنا الصلوات على الأفعال التي يصليها أهل الشرائع كان ذلك إما على حذف مضاف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r7.claim: The mosques come last either because the earlier sanctuaries are old and mosques later, or because the list rises from noble to more noble.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r7.anchor: وتأخير المساجد إما لأجل قدم تلك وحدوث هذه، وإما لانتقال من شريف إلى أشرف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r8.claim: Helping God means helping His religion and allies; His help makes them defeat enemies in combat and argument, encouraging fighting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r8.anchor: أي ينصر دينه وأولياءه، ونصره تعالى هو أن يظفر أولياءه بأعدائهم جلادا وجدالا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r9.claim: God is powerful to support the believers and invincible against any opponent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p517/r9.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى أنه قوي على نصرهم عزيز لا يغالب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p525/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p525/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p525/r1.claim: After recalling permission to fight and the believers' expulsion from their homes, the author presents the account of earlier messengers as a second consolation for Muhammad.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p525/r1.anchor: وأنهم كانوا أخرجوا من ديارهم وذكر مسلاة رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم بتكذيب من تقدم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.claim: In augmented triliteral verbs, when the consonant before a weak letter was originally vowelless and is not alif, wāw, or yāʾ, the weak letter is made vowelless and its vowel shifts back.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.anchor: فإذا كان الحرف الذي قبل الحرف المعتل ساكنا في الأصل ولم يكن

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.claim: This shift lets the added form undergo the same weakening as its unaugmented counterpart, while avoiding a change to a form absent from Arabic; the preceding consonant has already changed.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.anchor: وإنما دعاهم إلى ذلك أنهم أرادوا أن تعتل وما قبلها

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.claim: Forms such as fāʿala, tafāʿala, faʿʿala, and tafaʿʿala do not undergo this weakening: applying it would delete the long vowel or both letters, causing excessive loss and ambiguity.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.anchor: ولا يعتل في فاعلت لأنهم لو أسكنوا حذفوا الألف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.claim: Some verbs preserve the original weak letter despite the preceding sukūn, by analogy with fāʿala; this preservation is exceptional rather than a general rule.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.anchor: وقد جاءت حروف على الأصل غير معتلة مما أسكن ما قبله

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.claim: Al-Khalil explains that اجتوروا and similar forms retain wāw because they mean the equivalent tafāʿala forms, where wāw remains; shared meaning with sound triliteral forms also supports retention.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.claim: A form such as اجتاروا would follow regular weakening if built directly from the triliteral root; اجتوروا is possible when construed on the meaning and pattern of تفاعلوا.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.anchor: لقلت فيها اجتاروا إلا أن يقول ابنه على معنى تفاعلوا فتقول اجتوروا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.claim: If the preceding consonant was originally vowelled, it keeps its vowel and the weak letter follows the normal pattern, as in اختار and اعتاد; in أفتعل forms the kasra shifts to the tāʾ, as in أختير and أنقيد.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.anchor: وإذا كان الحرف قبل المعتل متحركا في الأصل لم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.claim: Wāw and yāʾ that are sound in the base root remain sound through augmentation and inflection, like the wāw of شويت and yāʾ of حييت.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمالحقتهالزوائدمنهذهالأفع.anchor: فإن الواو والياء لا تعتلان إذا لحق الأفعال الزيادة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.claim: Weak triliteral nouns whose pattern matches a verb generally undergo the same weakening as that verb; nouns often preserve the original form, though weakening is more common.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.anchor: اعلم أن كل اسم منها كان على ما ذكرت لك إن كان يكون مثاله وبناؤه فعلا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.claim: Some nouns preserve the underlying form, including القود and الخونة, just as a few augmented verbs do; the usual outcome remains sukūn and weakening.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.anchor: وربما جاء على الأصل كما يجيء فعل من المضاعف على

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.claim: Al-Khalil analyzes خاف, مال, and راح on the فعِل pattern, comparing them to adjectives like فرق and نزق; forms such as روع and حول also preserve the original pattern.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.anchor: فعلت كقولهم فرق وهو رجل فرق ونزق

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.claim: The فُعُل pattern is not used in its underlying form for these weak roots, because ḍamma on wāw is disliked and would lead to vowel adjustment or hamza, as with أدؤر and خون.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.anchor: وأما فعل فلم يجيئوا به على الأصل كراهية

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.claim: Patterns that are not themselves weak retain their original form; examples include نوم and سولة, while حول, صير, بيع, and ديم follow their stated patterns.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.anchor: قولهم رجل نوم ورجل سولة ولومة وعيبة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.author: Sībawayh
