SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.claim: In فُعُل forms with wāw, the wāw is made vowelless to avoid two adjacent ḍammas and the heaviness of wāw; this is preferred to hamza and parallels vowelless nonweak forms such as رسل.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.anchor: فأما فعل فإن الواو تسكن لاجتماع الضمتين والواو فجعلوا الإسكان

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.claim: Poetry may restore a heavy or lengthened form that ordinary speech avoids; Sībawayh quotes ʿAdī ibn Zayd’s line with سور as an example.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.claim: The corresponding pattern with yāʾ is treated like a sound form because yāʾ followed by wāw is lighter; غيور and غير illustrate this, with analogous lightening in بيض.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءفيأسماءهذاالمعتلعلى.anchor: وأما فعل من بنات الياء فبمنزلة غير المعتل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.claim: Indefinite and definite nouns on the مفاعل and مفاعيل patterns do not decline because these are plural patterns, less basic than the singular; the verse’s مساجد exemplifies the form.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.anchor: اعلم أنه ليس شيء يكون على هذا المثال إلا لم ينصرف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.claim: مقاتل and عذافر decline because their pattern can also be singular, unlike the exclusively plural مفاعل and مفاعيل forms.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.claim: The yāʾ of ثماني and رباع is an added nisba-like suffix on فعال, so these forms decline; Sībawayh compares it to يماني and شآم.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.anchor: في ثماني ياء الإضافة أدخلتها على فعال كما أدخلتها

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.claim: صياقلة declines because its tāʾ is appended after the مفاعل pattern is complete, as with feminine singulars; the suffix transforms the word from its plural pattern.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.anchor: من قبل أن هذه الهاء إنما ضمت إلى صياقل كما ضمت موت إلى حضر

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.claim: When a suffix creates a form like a singular or compound name, the resulting word declines; مدائني and مساجدي have moved out of the original plural pattern through the added yāʾ.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.anchor: فقد أخرجت هذه الياء مفاعيل ومفاعل إلى باب تميمي كما

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.claim: Some speakers shorten جنادل and ذلاذل to جندل and ذلذل and add nunation as compensation for the deleted alif.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.anchor: ويقول بعضهم جندل وذلذل يحذف ألف جنادل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.claim: Proper names based on plural patterns decline when diminutivized because the diminutive changes the form; حضاجر is itself a collective plural used as a name for the hyena.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.anchor: مساجد ثم حقرته صرفته لأنك قد حولت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.claim: حضاجر names the hyena because the plural evokes its broad belly; Sībawayh cites the Arabic expression أوطب حضاجر as evidence for its collective use.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.anchor: وإنما جعل هذا اسما للضبع لسعة بطنها

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.claim: سراويل is one Arabicized foreign garment name, but resembles indeclinable forms; as a man’s name it remains indeclinable when diminutivized, like عناق.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.anchor: أعرب كما أعرب الآجر إلا أن سراويل أشبه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.claim: شراحيل declines in the diminutive because it is Arabic and used only as a plural.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.anchor: وأما شراحيل فتحقيره ينصرف لأنه عربي

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.claim: أجمال and فلوس decline because they are close to singular patterns and can form further broken plurals, as in أقوال/أقاويل and أعراب/أعاريب; resemblance to a singular explains the case treatment.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.anchor: وأما أجمال وفلوس فإنها تنصرف وما أشبهها لأنها ضارعت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.claim: مفاعل and مفاعيل are terminal plural patterns and cannot be broken into a further pattern; unlike them, فعول can yield فعائل, as in جدود/جدائد and ركوب/ركائب.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.anchor: وأما مفاعل ومفاعيل فلا يكسر فيخرج الجمع إلى بناء غير هذا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.claim: أفعال can be singular for some Arabs; Sībawayh cites الأنعام and the Qur’anic wording نسقيكم مما في بطونه, plus ثوب أكياش and سدوس for the form’s uses.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.anchor: من العرب من يقول هو الأنعام وقال الله عز وجل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.claim: The yāʾ in بخاتي belongs to the plural formation, unlike the suffixal yāʾ in مدائني; it is part of the pattern just as the dāl is part of مساجد.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.anchor: فليس بمنزلة مدائني لأنك لم تلحق هذه الياء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.claim: Abū al-Khaṭṭāb reports a poetic use of ثماني without nunation; diminutives such as بخاتي and صحار decline after the plural pattern is changed, while ثمان as a singular proper name does not.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.anchor: بمنزلة حذار حدثني أبو الخطاب أنه سمع العرب ينشدون

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.claim: ثَمَان is indeclinable as a singular name, whereas صحار is a declinable plural; the yāʾ of ثمان resembles the suffix in قمري, يماني, and شآم.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.anchor: وأما ثمان إذا سميت به رجلا فلا تصرف لأنها واحدة كعناق

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانعلىمثالمفاعلومفاعيل.claim: رباع and حواري pattern with related forms such as سداسي; عواري, عوادي, and حوالي are broken plurals of حولي, عادي, and عارية, not forms with a newly attached yāʾ.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.claim: After إن, a following noun may be raised as a new subject because إن only emphasizes the preceding clause; Sībawayh prefers this analysis over raising it on a hidden pronoun in the predicate.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.anchor: يكون محمولا على الابتداء لأن معنى إن زيدا منطلق

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.claim: The weaker alternative raises the following noun on the implicit pronoun in the predicate; he recommends making that pronoun explicit, as in منطلق هو وعمرو.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.anchor: واما الوجه الآخر الضعيف فأن يكون محمولا على الاسم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.claim: He cites the Qur’anic phrase إن الله برئ من المشركين ورسوله for the preferred nominative analysis of a noun following an إن clause.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.claim: After a prepositional predicate such as فيها, a following noun can be raised like one after an adjective because فيها contains an implicit nominative pronoun.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.anchor: وإذا قلت إن زيدا فيها وعمرو جرى عمر

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.claim: The line by Jarīr supports the analysis of coordination after a prepositional predicate containing an implicit pronoun.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.claim: After a repeated إن clause, a following نفسه is preferably accusative; if it attaches to the hidden pronoun instead, use هو نفسه.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.claim: Negated coordination with لا follows the same case analyses as coordination with waw: عمرا is accusative when coordinated with the first noun.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.anchor: وإذا قلت إن زيدا منطلق لا عمرو

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.claim: لعل, كأن, and ليت allow the same coordination options as إن, but do not permit an independent raised noun; accusative after ليت is preferred because its wish meaning should not be mixed with an assertion.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.anchor: واعلم أن لعل وكأن وليت ثلاثتهن

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.claim: With إن زيدا فيها لا بل عمرو, عمرو may be raised or accusative because لا بل behaves like waw.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايكونمحمولاعلىإن)#271/r.anchor: وتقول إن زيدا فيها لا بل عمرو

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r3.claim: الذين may be a genitive adjective or clarification/apposition to the preceding relative pronoun, an accusative of praise, or a nominative sentence with an omitted subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r3.anchor: في حيز الجر على أنه صفة للموصول قبل أو بيان له أو بدل منه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r4.claim: The believers were expelled by the polytheists from Mecca.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r4.anchor: والمراد الذين أخرجهم المشركون من مكة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r5.claim: بغير حق attaches to the expulsion and means there was no cause that justified their removal.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r5.anchor: أي أخرجوا بغير ما يوجب إخراجهم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r6.speaker: الطبرسي
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī allows بغير حق to be circumstantial, describing them as having no cause that warranted expulsion.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r6.anchor: واختار الطبرسكونه في موضع الحال أي كائنين بغير حق مترتب عليهم يوجب إخراجهم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r7.claim: The exception is connected to حق; the phrase is a verbal noun apposed to حق, making monotheism the only alleged cause of expulsion.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r7.anchor: استثناء متصل من ( حق ) وأن وما بعدها في تأويل مصدر بدل منه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r8.claim: Their monotheism was the sole supposed reason for expulsion, though not a real justification; al-Ālūsī illustrates the construction with al-Nābigha's poetic exception.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r8.anchor: وحاصل المعنى لا موجب لإخراجهم إلا التوحيد وهو إذا أريد بالموجب النفس الأمري

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r9.claim: Another parse makes the exception appositive to غير, meaning they were not kept in their homes except by professing faith; al-Ālūsī finds it weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r9.anchor: وجوز أن يكون الإبدال من غير وفي أخرجوا معنى النفي أي لم يقرروا في ديارهم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r10.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r10.claim: Abū Ḥayyān requires a disconnected exception, meaning they were expelled because they said their Lord is God, with the post-exception phrase in the accusative.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r10.anchor: وأوجبه أبو حيان أي ولكن أخرجوا بقولهم ربنا وأوجب نصب ما بعد إلا

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r11.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the objections to a connected exception and apposition to حق as sophistical.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r11.anchor: كونه متصلا وكون ما بعد إلا بدلا من ( حق ) بما هو أشبه شيء بالمغالطة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r12.claim: The author also allows إلا to mean سوى as an adjective of حق, so monotheism was their only purported ground for expulsion.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162/r12.anchor: ويفهم من كلامهم جواز أن تكون إلا بمعنى سوى صفة لحق

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r1.claim: The clause encourages authorized fighting: God has historically enabled people to restrain one another so order, religious law, and worship places endure.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r1.anchor: تحريض على القتال المأذون فيه بإفادة أنه تعالى أجرى العادة بذلك في الأمم الماضية

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r2.claim: Without fighting and God's empowering believers against polytheists, worship sites would be demolished and people scattered.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r2.anchor: فلو لا القتال وتسليط الله تعالى المؤمنين على المشركين في كل عصر وزمان لهدمت متعبداتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r3.speaker: unnamed commentators
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r3.claim: Another view limits the reference to this community's believers overcoming unbelievers, preserving some places for Muslims and others for protected non-Muslims; al-Ālūsī says this is unpersuasive.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r3.anchor: بتسليط مؤمني هذه الأمة على كفارها لهدمت المتعبدات المذكورة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r4.claim: Mujāhid interprets restraint as stopping a people's oppression through testimony by just witnesses and similar means.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد : أي لو لا دفع ظلم قوم بشهادة العدول ونحو ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r5.speaker: قوم
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r5.claim: Another group says rulers' justice restrains the oppression of wrongdoers.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r5.anchor: وقال قوم : أي لو لا دفع ظلم الظلمة بعدل الولاة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r6.speaker: فرقة
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r6.claim: Another group interprets the clause as God averting punishment from the wicked through the prayers of the righteous.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r6.anchor: وقالت فرقة : أي لو لا دفع العذاب عن الأشرار بدعاء الأخيار

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r7.speaker: قطرب
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r7.claim: Quṭrub explains the restraint as retaliation protecting lives.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r7.anchor: وقال قطرب : أي لو لا الدفع بالقصاص عن النفوس

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r8.speaker: unnamed commentators
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r8.claim: Another view says prophets protect believers; al-Ālūsī finds these alternative readings unsupported by the context and unconvincing.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r8.anchor: وقيل بالنبيين عليهم السلام عن المؤمنين والكل مما لا يقتضيه المقام

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r9.claim: صوامع is the plural of صومعة, a tall building with a narrow pointed top; أصمع describes a man sharp in speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r9.anchor: والصوامع جمع صومعة بوزن فعولة وهي بناء مرتفع حديد الأعلى

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r10.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r10.claim: Al-Rāghib defines a صومعة as a building with a compressed top, comparing it to an ear close against the head.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r10.anchor: وقال الراغب : هي كل بناء متصمع الرأس أي متلاصقه والأصمع اللاصقة أذنه برأسه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r11.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r11.claim: Qatāda says ṣawāmiʿ before Islam were associated with Christian monks and Sabian worshippers; al-Ālūsī objects to the Sabian reference because he considers their religion never to have been true.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r11.anchor: وكانت قبل الإسلام كما قال قتادة مختصة برهبان النصارى وبعباد الصابئة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r12.speaker: أبو العالية
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r12.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya identifies the ṣawāmiʿ here as worship places of monks.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r12.anchor: والمراد بها هنا متعبد الرهبان عن أبي العالية

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r13.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r13.claim: Qatāda identifies the ṣawāmiʿ here as Sabian worship places, an identification al-Ālūsī says should not be intended.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r13.anchor: ومتعبد الصابئة عند قتادة ولا يخفى أنه لا ينبغي إرادة ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r14.claim: The term was later used for Muslim minarets.

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r15.claim: A بيعة is a Christian prayer house and, unlike a monk's hermitage, is not restricted to monks.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r15.anchor: والبيع واحدها بيعة بوزن فعلة وهي مصلى النصارى ولا تختص برهبانهم كالصومعة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r16.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r16.claim: Al-Rāghib suggests that if بيعة is originally Arabic, its name may allude to God purchasing believers' lives and property.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r16.anchor: وقال الراغب : فإن يكن ذلك عربيا في الأصل فوجه التسمية به لما قال سبحانه ( إن الله اشترى من المؤمنين

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r17.claim: Another reported identification of a بيعة is a Jewish synagogue.

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r18.speaker: أهل المدينة ويعقوب
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r18.claim: The people of Medina and Yaʿqūb read دفاع with an added alif.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r18.anchor: وقرأ أهل المدينة ويعقوب ( ولو لا دفاع ) بالألف

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r19.speaker: الحرميان وأيوب وقتادة وطلحة وزائدة والزعفراني
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r19.claim: The two Meccan readers, Ayyūb, Qatāda, Ṭalḥa, Zāʾida from al-Aʿmash, and al-Zaʿfarānī read هدمت with lightening or doubling, reflecting the many sites.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r19.anchor: وقرأ الحرميان وأيوب وقتادة وطلحة وزائدة عن الأعمش والزعفراني ( لهدمت ) بالتخفيف والتضعيف

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r20.claim: Ṣalawāt most commonly refers to a Jewish synagogue; another view makes it a Christian place of worship distinct from a بيعة.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r20.anchor: وصلوات ( جمع صلاة وهي كنيسة اليهود وقيل : معبد للنصارى دون البيعة والأول أشهر

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r21.claim: The synagogue is named ṣalāt by naming the place for the prayer performed there.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r21.anchor: وسميت الكنيسة بذلك لأنها يصلي فيها فهي مجاز من تسمية المحل باسم الحال

ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r22.claim: A literal reading of ṣalawāt would require هدمت to mean rendered inactive or an omitted word to be supplied; the author says this is unpersuasive.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p162#2/r22.anchor: وقيل : هي بمعناها الحقيقي وهدمت بمعنى عطلت أو في الكلام مضاف مقدر وليس بذاك

ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r1.claim: Ṣalawāt is an Arabized form of Syriac ṣlotha, meaning a place of prayer in Hebrew; the ordinary form is apparently a generic noun, not a proper name.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r1.anchor: معرب صلوثا بالثاء المثلثة والقصر ومعناها بالعبرانية المصلى

ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r2.speaker: أبو رجاء والجحدري وأبو العالية ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r2.claim: They read ṣalawāt in the Syriac-like form ṣlotha, with thāʾ and a shortened ending.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r2.anchor: وروي عن أبي رجاء والجحدري وأبي العالية ومجاهد أنهم قرأوا بذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r3.claim: Hārūn's report from Abū ʿAmr of an uninflected, diptote form suggests a generic proper name; a specific place-name is unlikely, and the usual-reading explanation by resemblance to a plural is strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r3.anchor: ما رواه هارون عن أبي عمرو من عدم تنوينه ومنع صرفه للعلمية والعجمية

ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r4.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r4.claim: Jaʿfar read the word with ḍamma on both ṣād and lām; Ibn Khalawayh also reports a kasra on ṣād with a still lām, attributed as well to al-Jahdari.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r4.anchor: وقرأ جعفر بن محمد رضي الله تعالى عنهما ( صلوات ) بضم الصاد واللام وحكى عنه ابن خالويه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r5.speaker: الكلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r5.claim: Ibn Khalawayh reports a form with ḍamma on ṣād and fatḥa on lām, attributed to al-Kalbi.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r5.anchor: وحكى عنه أيضا ( صلوات ) بضم الصاد وفتح اللام وحكيت عن الكلبي

ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r6.speaker: أبو العالية
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r6.claim: In one transmission, Abū al-ʿĀliya read the word with fatḥa on ṣād and sukūn on lām.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو العالية في رواية ( صلوات ) بفتح الصاد وسكون اللام

ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r7.speaker: الحجاج بن يوسف والجحدري
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r7.claim: Al-Ḥajjāj read with ḍamma on both consonants and no alif; the same reading is also attributed to al-Jahdari.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r7.anchor: وقرأ الحجاج بن يوسف ( صلوات ) بضم الصاد واللام من غير ألف وحكيت عن الجحدري

ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r8.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r8.claim: Mujāhid read ṣalūta, with two ḍammas, a tāʾ, and a following alif.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r8.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد ( صلوتا ) بضمتين وتاء مثناة بعدها ألف

ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r9.speaker: الضحاك والكلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r9.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Kalbi read ṣalūth with two ḍammas, no alif, and the three-dotted thāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r9.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك والكلبي ( صلوث ) بضمتين من غير ألف وبثاء مثلثة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r10.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r10.claim: ʿIkrima read ṣalwīthā with kasra on ṣād, a still lām, kasra on wāw, then yāʾ, thāʾ, and alif.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r10.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة ( صلويثا ) بكسر الصاد وإسكان اللام وواو مكسورة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r11.speaker: الجحدري ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r11.claim: Al-Jahdari read ṣalwāth with ḍamma on ṣād and fatḥa on wāw; Mujāhid is also reported with that form but a kasra on ṣād.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r11.anchor: وحكي عن الجحدري أيضا ( صلواث ) بضم الصاد وسكون اللام وواو مفتوحة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r12.speaker: الحجاج والجحدري
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r12.claim: Al-Ḥajjāj and al-Jahdari are reported to read ṣulūb, treating it as the irregular plural of ṣalīb on the fuʿūl pattern.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r12.anchor: وحكى ابن خالوية وابن عطية عن الحجاج والجحدري ( صلوب ) بضمتين وباء موحدة على أنه جمع صليب

ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r13.claim: The word has an unusually large number of variant readings.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r13.anchor: فهذه عدة قراآت قلما يوجد مثلها في كلمة واحدة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r14.claim: Masājid are the familiar Muslim places of worship; the name honors them because prostration brings a servant closest to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r14.anchor: وهو معبد معروف للمسلمين وخص بهذا الاسم اعتناء بشأنه من حيث أن السجود أقرب ما يكون العبد فيه إلى ربه عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r15.claim: The claim that the name is exclusive because prostration in prayer belongs only to Muslims is refuted by Mary being commanded to prostrate; taking her prostration only lexically is far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r15.anchor: لاختصاص السجود في الصلاة بالمسليمن ورد بقوله تعالى ( يا مريم اقنتي لربك واسجدي واركعي ) مع الراكعين

ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r16.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r16.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the named worship places occur across communities, except that biʿa is specifically Christian in the customary usage of each language.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r16.anchor: الأسماء المذكورة تشترك الأمم في مسمياتها لا البيعة فإنها مختصة بالنصارى في عرف كل لغة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r17.speaker: الأكثرون
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r17.claim: Most commentators identify monasteries with monks, churches with Christians, synagogues with Jews, and mosques with Muslims.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r17.anchor: والأكثرون على أن الصوامع للرهبان والبيع للنصارى والصلوات لليهود والمساجد للمسلمين

ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r18.claim: The delayed mention of mosques may follow the historical order of the institutions, place them beside praise of their worshippers, or distance them from the mention of demolition; ṣalawāt may be delayed to pair it with mosques.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r18.anchor: ولعل تأخير ذكرها مع أن الظاهر تقديمها لشرفها لأن الترتيب الوجودي كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r19.claim: Another proposed ordering rises in dignity: churches exceed monk-only cells in worshippers, Jewish synagogues are older, and mosques are highest because they host forms of worship absent elsewhere.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r19.anchor: وقيل إنما جيء المتعبدات على هذا النسق للانتقال من شريف إلى أشرف

ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r20.claim: The threatened demolition is hyperbole for widespread corruption and disruption among people if God did not empower the righteous against the wicked, rather than merely destruction of religious buildings.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r20.anchor: المبالغة في ظهور الفساد ووقوع الاختلال في أمر العباد لو لا تسليط الله تعالى المحقين على المبطلين

ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r21.claim: The clause about frequent remembrance is an adjective specifically describing mosques.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r21.anchor: في موضع الصفة لمساجد وقال الضحاك ومقاتل والكلبي

ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r22.speaker: الضحاك ومقاتل والكلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r22.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Muqātil, and al-Kalbi take the remembrance clause as describing all the worship places; Abū Ḥayyān favors this scope.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r22.anchor: وقال الضحاك ومقاتل والكلبي : في موضع الصفة للجميع واستظهره أبو حيان

ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r23.claim: The abrogation of earlier laws does not preclude God's name continuing to be remembered in those places; the verse also applies generally to the period before abrogation.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r23.anchor: لأن الانتساخ لا ينافي بقاءها ببركة ذكر الله تعالى فيها مع أن معنى الآية عام

ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r24.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r24.claim: God promises help to whoever supports His religion or His allies, and fulfilled this by giving the Emigrants and Helpers victory over Arab, Persian, and Roman powers and their lands.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r24.anchor: وبالله لينصرن الله تعالى من ينصر دينه أو من ينصر أولياءه ولقد أنجز الله تعالى وعده

ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r25.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r25.claim: God is powerful to accomplish His purposes, including granting them victory.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p163/r25.anchor: على ما يريده من مراداته التي من جملتها نصرهم ( عزيز

ALUSI-FULL:v17p164/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p164/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p164/r1.claim: God is mighty: nothing can resist or oppose Him.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p377/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p377/r1.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن سابط
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p377/r1.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sābiṭ says that when pilgrims came to Mecca, no Meccan was more entitled to his own house than they were; ʿUmar forbade residents to shut their doors during the season.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p377/r1.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن سابط: كان الحجاج إذا قدموا مكة لم يكن أحد من أهل مكة بأحق بمنزله منهم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p377/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p377/r2.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p377/r2.claim: On the view associated with ʿUmar’s rule that residents could not restrict access during pilgrimage, selling or renting Meccan houses is impermissible.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p377/r2.anchor: وكان عمر بن الخطاب ينهى الناس أن يغلقوا أبوابهم في الموسم، وعلى هذا القول لا يجوز بيع دور مكة وإجارتها،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p377/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p377/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p377/r3.claim: Baghawī prefers the opposing view, which permits sale and lease: the verse attributes homes to their expelled owners, and reports show ownership and sale in Mecca.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p377/r3.anchor: وعلى القول الأول -وهو الأقرب إلى الصواب -يجوز، لأن الله تعالى قال: {الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم} (الحج: 40) ،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p377/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p377/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p377/r4.claim: The Prophet declared that whoever entered Abū Sufyān’s house was safe at the conquest of Mecca, attributing the house to its owner; ʿUmar also bought a Meccan house for a prison for four thousand dirhams.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p377/r4.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم فتح مكة: "من دخل دار أبي سفيان فهو آمن" (2) فنسب الدار إليه نسب ملك،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p377/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p377/r5.speaker: طاووس وعمرو بن دينار والشافعي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p377/r5.claim: Permitting sale of Meccan houses is the view of Ṭāwūs, ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, and al-Shāfiʿī.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p377/r5.anchor: وهذا قول طاوس وعمرو بن دينار، وبه قال الشافعي.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r1.claim: “Those who were expelled” is a substitute for the earlier “those” in the passage.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r1.anchor: {الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم بغير حق} بدل "عن الذين" الأولى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r2.claim: They were expelled from their homes for no reason except saying that God alone is their Lord.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r2.anchor: أي: لم يخرجوا من ديارهم إلا لقولهم ربنا الله وحده.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r3.claim: God’s repelling of some people by others occurs through jihad and enforcement of legal penalties.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r3.anchor: {ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض} بالجهاد وإقامة الحدود،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r4.speaker: أهل الحجاز
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r4.claim: The people of the Ḥijāz read the verb with a light dāl; the other readers double it, a form specific to extensive demolition.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r4.anchor: قرأ أهل الحجاز بتخفيف الدال، وقرأ الآخرون بالتشديد على التكثير،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r5.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r5.claim: Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk identify the ṣawāmiʿ as monks’ hermitages.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r5.anchor: قال مجاهد والضحاك: يعني: صوامع الرهبان.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r6.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r6.claim: Qatādah identifies the ṣawāmiʿ as hermitages of the Ṣābiʾans.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r7.claim: Buyūʿ is the plural of biʿah, a Christian church.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r7.anchor: بيع النصارى جمع "بيعة" وهي كنيسة النصارى،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r8.claim: Ṣalawāt refers to Jewish synagogues, called ṣalōtā in Hebrew.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r8.anchor: يعني كنائس اليهود، ويسمونها بالعبرانية صلوتا،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r9.claim: The mosques are those of the Muslim community of Muhammad.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r9.anchor: يعني مساجد المسلمين من أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r10.claim: The worship places of each prophetic community would have been demolished in its own era: synagogues in Moses’ time, churches and hermitages in Jesus’ time, and mosques in Muhammad’s time.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r10.anchor: ومعنى الآية: ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض لهدم في شريعة كل نبي مكان صلاتهم،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r11.speaker: ابن زيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r11.claim: Ibn Zayd instead identifies ṣalawāt as Muslim prayers, which would cease if an enemy entered upon them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389/r11.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: أراد بالصلوات صلوات أهل الإسلام، فإنها تنقطع إذا دخل العدو عليهم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389#2/r1.claim: God will aid whoever aids His religion and His Prophet.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389#2/r1.anchor: {ولينصرن الله من ينصره} أي: ينصر دينه ونبيه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p389#2/r2.anchor: {ولينصرن الله من ينصره} أي: ينصر دينه ونبيه، {إن الله لقوي عزيز}

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r1.claim: Those expelled from their homes are the Muslims driven from Mecca.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r1.anchor: الذين أخرجوا من ديرهم } يعني مكة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r2.claim: They were expelled without any cause that could make them deserve it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r2.anchor: بغير حق } بغير موجب استحقوه به.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r3.claim: The exception may be rhetorically connected, like al-Nābigha’s line denying any fault except swords nicked in battle; another view treats it as disconnected.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r3.anchor: ربنا الله } على طريقة قول النابغة: ولا عيب فيهم غير أن سيوفهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r4.claim: Another view construes the exception as disconnected.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r4.anchor: وقيل منقطع. { ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض } بتسليط

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r5.claim: God’s repelling people through one another means empowering believers over unbelievers.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r6.claim: Without this check, polytheists would prevail over religious communities and destroy their places of worship.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r6.anchor: لخربت باستيلاء المشركين على أهل الملل،

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r7.claim: Nāfiʿ reads دفاع in place of دفع.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r7.anchor: وقرأ نافع { دفاع } وقرأ نافع وابن كثير { لهدمت } بالتخفيف.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r8.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr read لهدمت with a light rather than doubled consonant.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r8.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن كثير { لهدمت } بالتخفيف.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r9.claim: Ṣawāmiʿ are monks’ monasteries, biyaʿ Christian churches, ṣalawāt Jewish synagogues, and masājid Muslim mosques.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r9.anchor: صومع } صوامع الرهبانية. { وبيع } بيع النصارى. { وصلوت } كنائس اليهود

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r10.claim: Synagogues are called ṣalawāt because prayer is performed there; alternatively, the word comes from Aramaic ṣalōtā and was Arabized.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r10.anchor: سميت بها لأنها يصلى فيها، وقيل أصلها صلوتا بالعبرانية فعربت.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r11.claim: This phrase may describe all four kinds of worship place, or only mosques to give them special distinction.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r11.anchor: صفة للأربع أو لمساجد خصت بها تفضيلا.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r12.claim: Those who help God help His religion; the promise was fulfilled when emigrants and helpers overcame Arab chiefs, Persian kings, and Byzantine emperors, inheriting their lands.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r12.anchor: من ينصر دينه، وقد أنجز وعده بأن سلط المهاجرين والأنصار على صناديد العرب

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r13.claim: God is strong enough to aid them and mighty, with nothing able to resist Him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:40/r13.anchor: على نصرهم. { عزيز } لا يمانعه شيء.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r6.claim: The expelled believers were driven to the mountain valley, Abyssinia, and Medina.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r6.anchor: الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم } إلى الشعب والحبشة والمدينة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r7.claim: Their only alleged offense was professing God as Lord, a statement that should instead have secured their residence, love, praise, and emulation.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r7.anchor: الموجب لإقرارهم في ديارهم , وحبهم ومدحهم واقتفاء آثارهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r8.claim: The exception may be parsed as disconnected, meaning they had no offense apart from their confession, or as an ordinary exception; either way it frames their confession as the sole pretext for expulsion.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r8.anchor: فهو من باب : ولا عيب فيهم غير أن سيوفهم بهن فلول من قراع الكتائب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r9.claim: The cited poetic example feigns criticism of swords blunted in battle while actually praising their owners’ valor.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r9.anchor: ولا عيب فيهم غير أن سيوفهم بهن فلول من قراع الكتائب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r10.claim: Those who are sincerely devoted to God attract people’s arrows of intrigue and every effort to harm them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r10.anchor: من أخلص لله , صوب الناس إليه سهام مكرهم , ولم يدعوا في أذاه شيئا من جهدهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r11.claim: Repelling people through others operates in every religious law and in the era of every prophet; the permission for these believers illustrates that wider principle.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r11.anchor: في كل شريعة , وفي زمن كل ني أرسله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r12.claim: Without this repulsion, polytheism would remain openly dominant and ignorant people would seize the pilgrimage sites.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r12.anchor: لا ستمر الشرك ظاهرا , والباطل - باستيلاء الجهلة على مواطن الحج - قاهرا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r13.claim: The list names elevated small retreats of monks, Christian churches, Jewish synagogues, and Muslim mosques, respectively.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r13.anchor: صوامع } وهي معابد صغار مرتفعة للرهبان { وبيع } للنصارى { وصلوات } اي كنائس اليهود

BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r14.claim: Mosques come last in the list so that they are farthest from demolition and nearest in the wording to mention of God’s name.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r14.anchor: أخرها لتكون بعيدة من الهدم قريبة من الذكر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r15.claim: Using God’s name explicitly instead of a pronoun may signal that the groups invoke Him differently in these places, with varying degrees of sincerity.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r15.anchor: ولعل العدول عن الإضمار إلى الإظهار للإشارة إلى اختلاف ذكره تعالى في الأماكن المذكورة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r16.claim: God averts destruction because each religious group may seek to ruin another group’s sanctuaries, and even members of one faith may attack one another’s places of worship.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r16.anchor: لأن كل فرقة تريد هدم ما للأخرى , بل ربما أراد بعض أهل ملة إخراب بعض معلبد أهل ملته

BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r17.claim: God counters the corruption He wills among most people by placing opposing forces among them, which reduces much of their stubbornness.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p156/r17.anchor: فإنه تعالى لما أراد بأكثر الناس الفساد , نصب لهم من الأضداد , ما يخفف كثيرا من العناد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p157/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p157/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p157/r1.claim: He attaches the promise of divine aid either to the implied statement that the places were not demolished because God repelled some people by others, or to the earlier permission to fight.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p157/r1.anchor: عطف عليه أو على قوله { أذن } قوله : { ولينصرون الله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p157/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p157/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p157/r2.claim: Naming God instead of using a pronoun universalizes the rule and ties it to the quality of whoever supports Him, from among Muslims or others.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p157/r2.anchor: وأظهر ولم يضمر تعميما وتعليقا للحكم بالوصف فقال : { من ينصره

BIQAI-FULL:v5p157/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p157/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p157/r3.claim: God arranges support through ordinary causes or extraordinary breaches of custom, as in early Muslim conquests and miraculous crossings and victories.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p157/r3.anchor: بما يهيىء له من الأسباب , إجراء له على الأمر المعتاد , وبغير أسباب خرقا للعادةن كما وقع في كثير من الفتوحاتن

BIQAI-FULL:v5p157/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p157/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p157/r4.claim: God is powerful over whatever He wills and cannot be overcome; whoever has Him as helper is victorious, while that person's enemy is subdued, even if the supported party is weak.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p157/r4.anchor: ثم علل نصره وإن ضعف المنصور , بقوله : { إن الله } أي الذي لا كفوء له { لقوي * } أي على ما يريد { عزيز

DURR-FULL:v6p58/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies those expelled from their homes as Muhammad and his companions, driven from Mecca to Medina without right.
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس {الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم} أي من مكة إلى المدينة {بغير حق} يعني محمدا - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وأصحابه

DURR-FULL:v6p58/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r2.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r2.claim: Uthman says this verse and the next concern him and his companions: expelled unjustly, they later gained power, prayed, gave alms, and commanded right and forbade wrong.
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r2.anchor: عن عثمان بن عفان قال: فينا نزلت هذه الآية {الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم بغير حق} والآية بعدها أخرجنا من ديارنا

DURR-FULL:v6p58/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r3.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r3.claim: Ali says the verse concerns Muhammad's companions: God used them to repel attackers from their followers, or places of worship would have been demolished.
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r3.anchor: أن عليا قال: إنما نزلت هذه الآية في أصحاب محمد {ولولا دفع الله الناس} قال: لولا دفع الله بأصحاب محمد عن التابعين

DURR-FULL:v6p58/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r4.speaker: عاصم
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r4.claim: Asim recited دفع الله without the alif found in the alternate form دفاع.
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r4.anchor: عن عاصم أنه قرأ {ولولا دفع الله الناس} بغير الألف

DURR-FULL:v6p58/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets God's repelling people as warfare and jihad.
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r5.anchor: عن ابن زيد {ولولا دفع الله الناس} قال: لولا القتال والجهاد

DURR-FULL:v6p58/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r6.claim: Mujahid says the Muslims repel the polytheists.
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد في الآية قال: دفع المشركون بالمسلمين

DURR-FULL:v6p58/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r7.claim: Mujahid also explains mutual repelling as people restraining one another through testimony, truth, and similar means, preserving the listed sanctuaries.
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد في الآية قال: منع بعضهم ببعض في الشهادة وفي الحق وفيما يكون مثل هذا

DURR-FULL:v6p58/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies monasteries as monks' houses, biyaʿ as Jewish synagogues, ṣalawat as Christian churches, and mosques as Muslim mosques.
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {لهدمت صوامع} قال: الصوامع التي تكون فيها الرهبان والبيع مساجد اليهود

DURR-FULL:v6p58/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r9.claim: In another report, Ibn Abbas identifies biyaʿ as Christian churches and ṣalawat as Jewish synagogues.
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: البيع بيع النصارى وصلوات كنائس اليهود

DURR-FULL:v6p58/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r10.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak says Jewish synagogues are called ṣalawat.
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r10.anchor: عن الضحاك قال: صلوات كنائس اليهود يسمون الكنيسة صلاة

DURR-FULL:v6p58/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r11.speaker: عاصم الجحدري
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r11.claim: Asim al-Jahdari reads the word ṣalawat and treats it as prayer, asking how prayer itself could be demolished.
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r11.anchor: عن عاصم الجحدري أنه قرأ {وصلوات} قال: الصلوات دون الصوامع قال: وكيف تهدم الصلاة

DURR-FULL:v6p58/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r12.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r12.claim: Abu al-Aliya calls biyaʿ Christian churches and ṣalawat small Christian churches.
DURR-FULL:v6p58/r12.anchor: عن أبي العالية قال: البيع بيع النصارى والصلوات: بيع صغار للنصارى

DURR-FULL:v6p60/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p60/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v6p60/r1.claim: Abu al-Aliya identifies monasteries as monks' retreats, biyaʿ as Christian churches, and ṣalawat as Sabian places of worship.
DURR-FULL:v6p60/r1.anchor: عن أبي العالية في الآية قال: صوامع الرهبان وبيع النصارى وصلوات مساجد الصابئين

DURR-FULL:v6p60/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p60/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p60/r2.claim: Qatada assigns monasteries to Sabians, churches to Christians, ṣalawat to Jewish synagogues, and mosques to Muslims.
DURR-FULL:v6p60/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {صوامع} قال: هي للصابئين وبيع للنصارى وصلوات كنائس اليهود ومساجد للمسلمين

DURR-FULL:v6p60/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p60/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p60/r3.claim: Mujahid describes monasteries, churches, ṣalawat, and mosques as worship places of scriptural communities and Muslims along roads.
DURR-FULL:v6p60/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد في الآية قال: الصوامع صوامع الرهبان وبيع كنائس وصلوات ومساجد لأهل الكتاب ولأهل الإسلام بالطرق

DURR-FULL:v6p60/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p60/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v6p60/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says that if an enemy entered, Islamic worship would cease in the mosques.
DURR-FULL:v6p60/r4.anchor: عن ابن زيد في قوله: وصلوات أهل الإسلام تنقطع إذا دخل عليهم العدو

DURR-FULL:v6p60/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p60/r5.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v6p60/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says God's name is remembered often in every place listed, not only in mosques.
DURR-FULL:v6p60/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله: {يذكر فيها اسم الله كثيرا} يعني في كل مما ذكر من الصوامع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r1.claim: The phrase is appositional to ‘those who fight’ in 22:39; it shows that their fighting began as persecution, whose gravest form was expulsion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r1.anchor: بدل من { الذين يقاتلون } ( الحج : 39 ) ، وفي إجراء هذه الصلة عليهم إيماء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r2.claim: Bi-ghayri ḥaqq is circumstantial: the expelled people were in a state of having no valid ground on which expulsion could be imposed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r2.anchor: أي أخرجوا متلبسين بعدم الحق عليهم الموجب إخراجهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r3.claim: People have a natural right to remain in their homeland and among their people, on equal terms with the established community, whether rooted in long settlement or conquest.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r3.anchor: فإن للمرء حقا في وطنه ومعاشرة قومه ، وهذا الحق ثابت بالفطرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r4.claim: That right ends only under a basis set by religious law or established pre-religious custom; legal exile and banishment and pre-Islamic expulsion were penalties for wrongdoing when lesser restraint failed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r4.anchor: ولا يزول ذلك الحق إلا بموجب قرره الشرع أو العوائد قبل الشرع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r5.speaker: زهير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r5.claim: Zuhayr’s verse lists an oath, a contest or departure as the three ways a right may be brought to an end.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r5.anchor: كما قال زهير : فإن الحق مقطعه ثلاث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r6.claim: Faith in God entails no aggression against others, and merely declaring it harms no one; expulsion for that reason is blatant injustice enforced by force.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r6.anchor: فإن إيمانهم بالله لا ينجر منه اعتداء على غيرهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r7.claim: The exception ironically treats professing God as the sole supposed ground for expulsion, thereby reinforcing that no real ground exists; it praises by seeming to blame.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r7.anchor: وهذا من تأكيد الشيء بما يوهم نقضه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r8.claim: The exception is rhetorically drawn from the general idea of a valid ground, while the intended ground is one that would justify expelling them; its ironic force surveys and dismisses any imagined justification.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p274#2/r8.anchor: والاستثناء في قوله : { إلا أن يقولوا ربنا الله } استثناء من عموم الحق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r1.speaker: النابغة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r1.claim: Al-Nābigha’s couplet illustrates praise framed to resemble blame: the only supposed flaw is that swords have battle nicks.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r1.anchor: ولا عيب فيهم غير أن سيوفهم بهن فلول من قراع الكتائب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r2.claim: The verse was certainly revealed in Medina.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r2.anchor: وهذه الآية لا محالة نزلت بالمدينة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r3.claim: This parenthesis explains and honors the permission to defend in 22:39; that defense protects the worship of Muslims, Jews and Christians, benefiting all monotheists rather than Muslims alone.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r3.anchor: فلما تضمنت جملة { أذن للذين يقاتلون } ( الحج : 39 ) الخ الإذن للمسلمين بدفاع المشركين عنهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r4.claim: The wāw introduces a parenthetical, resumptive clause that explains the content of the permission to fight in 22:39.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r4.anchor: والواو في قوله { ولولا دفاع الله الناس } إلى آخره ، اعتراضية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r5.claim: Lawlā is a counterfactual conditional: its consequent is withheld because the condition stated in its clause exists.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r5.anchor: حرف امتناع لوجود ، أي حرف يدل على امتناع جوابه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r6.claim: Without defense of Muslim worship places, polytheists would have overcome the Muslims, attacked neighboring non-polytheist communities and destroyed their temples to erase monotheism; naming other temples also urges support for Muslims.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r6.anchor: ولهدموا معابدهم من صوامع ، وبيعع ، وصلوات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r7.claim: On this interpretation, al-nās is context-specific: the people fighting one another are the Muslims and Meccan polytheists.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r8.claim: He also allows a general historical reading: before Islam, God permitted earlier monotheists to fight, as in David’s victory over Goliath and Solomon’s rule, to prevent polytheists from erasing signs of monotheism as Nebuchadnezzar erased Solomon’s temple.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد : لولا ما سبق قبل الإسلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r9.claim: In that alternative, al-nās is generic and the clause concludes the permission in 22:39: earlier permission to fight kept polytheists from oppressing monotheists as they had done before.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p275/r9.anchor: فتكون هذه الجملة تذييلا لجملة { أذن للذين يقاتلون بأنهم ظلموا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r1.claim: Attributing the defense directly to God is a figurative causal attribution: His permission caused people to defend their temples, urging religious communities to unite against polytheism.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r1.anchor: وإضافة الدفاع إلى الله إسناد مجازي عقلي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r2.speaker: نافع
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r2.claim: Nāfiʿ, Abū Jaʿfar and Yaʿqūb read difāʿ, with an alif.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع ، وأبو جعفر ، ويعقوب { دفاع . }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r3.claim: Baʿḍahum is a partitive apposition to al-nās, and bi-baʿḍin attaches to difāʿ with bāʾ of instrument.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r4.claim: Hadm means demolishing a structure and bringing it down.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r5.speaker: نافع
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r5.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Abū Jaʿfar read the verb with a light dāl; the other readers double it to intensify the destruction, as if rage left no trace.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r5.anchor: وقرأ نافع ، وابن كثير ، وأبو جعفر { لهدمت } بتخفيف الدال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r6.claim: Ṣawāmiʿ are tall, narrow buildings reached by stairs, with an upper chamber used by monks for secluded worship; lamps aided night prayer and travelers, hence the related name manāra.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r7.speaker: امرؤ القيس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r7.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays’s image of a monk’s lantern-like tower at evening illustrates the meaning of manāra.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r7.anchor: تضيء الظلام بالعشي كأنها منارة ممسى راهب متبتل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r8.claim: Biyaʿ are Christian places of worship; the word’s etymology is unknown and may be borrowed from another language.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r8.anchor: والبيع : جمع بيعة بكسر الباء وسكون التحتية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r9.claim: Ṣalawāt here means Jewish synagogues, borrowed from Syriac ṣlōthā and adapted into Arabic.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r9.anchor: والصلوات : جمع صلاة وهي هنا مراد بها كنائس اليهود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r10.speaker: مجاهد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r10.claim: Mujāhid, al-Jaḥdarī, Abū al-ʿĀliya and Abū Rajāʾ are reported to read the word with a final thāʾ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r10.anchor: أنهم قرأوها هنا { وصلواث } بمثلثة في آخره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r11.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya reports that ʿIkrima and Mujāhid read ṣalwaythā with the stated vowel pattern and a shortened alif.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : قرأ عكرمة ، ومجاهد { صلويثا بكسر الصاد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r12.claim: He remarks that the lexicographers’ failure to record this word or material is astonishing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r12.anchor: وهذه المادة قد فاتت أهل اللغة وهي غفلة عجيبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r13.claim: Masājid here denotes places of prostration not among the three preceding kinds of worship buildings; the passage applies as Muslims build the mosques of Qubāʾ and Medina at the start of the Hijra.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p277/r13.anchor: والمساجد : اسم لمحل السجود من كل موضع عبادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r1.claim: The adjectival clause most naturally modifies all four preceding places of worship, since a description after coordinated phrases ordinarily returns to their shared described nouns.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r1.anchor: يذكر فيها اسم الله كثيرا } صفة والغالب في الصفة الواردة بعد جمل متعاطفة فيها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r2.claim: The description hints that these places are destroyed because they preserve frequent remembrance of God rather than idols; the expelled Muslims were persecuted for saying their Lord is God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r2.anchor: وفائدة هذا الوصف الإيماء إلى أن سبب هدمها أنها يذكر فيها اسم الله كثيرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r3.claim: Here frequent remembrance means continuous remembrance across all times, and it signals a religious benefit of these places.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r3.anchor: في هذا إيماء إلى أن في هذه المواضع فائدة دينية وهي ذكر اسم الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r4.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r4.claim: Ibn Khuyz Mindad says the verse forbids demolishing the churches, synagogues, and fire temples of protected non-Muslims.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r4.anchor: قال ابن خويز منداد من أيمة المالكية ( من أهل أواخر القرن الرابع ) تضمنت هذه الآية المنع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r5.claim: The verse does not itself forbid destroying fire temples, where God is not remembered; their protection instead follows from the dhimma covenant with Muslims.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r5.anchor: أما بيوت النار فلا تتضمن هذه الآية منع هدمها فإنها لا يذكر فيها اسم الله وإنما منع هدمها عقد الذمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r6.claim: An alternative view makes the description of places where God is remembered refer only to mosques.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r6.anchor: وقيل الصفة راجعة إلى مساجد خاصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r7.claim: Monasteries come first because they were common and familiar in Arabia, serving travelers as beacons and shelter; churches follow by analogy, then prayer houses, with general mosques last.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r7.anchor: وتقديم الصوامع في الذكر على ما بعده لأن صوامع الرهبان كانت أكثر في بلاد العرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r8.claim: The promise explains that God commands Muslims to defend their faith and guarantees victory: defending God’s religion is figuratively helping Him; the oath lām and emphatic nūn stress the promise, which concludes generally for the expelled Muslims.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p278/r8.anchor: لأنهم بدفاعهم ينصرون دين الله ، فكأنهم نصروا الله ، ولذلك أكد الجملة بلام القسم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p279/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p279/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p279/r1.claim: God being strong and mighty grounds the promised aid: strength means power, while might literally means invulnerability to anyone’s domination.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p279/r1.anchor: العزة هنا حقيقة لأن العزة هي المنعة ، أي عدم تسلط غير صاحبها على صاحبها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p123#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p123#2/r3.speaker: نافع والحسن وأبو جعفر وأبو عمرو وابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p123#2/r3.claim: Nafi, Hasan, and Abu Ja'far read yudāfiʿ and difāʿ; Abu Amr and Ibn Kathir read yadfaʿ and dafʿ; the remaining readers combine yudāfiʿ with dafʿ.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p123#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p123#2/r4.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p123#2/r4.claim: Abu Ali says this reading treats dāfaʿ like dafaʿ, as in ʿāqaba and ṭābaqa, so the verbal noun is dafʿ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p123#2/r4.anchor: قال أبو علي أجريت «دافع» في هذه القراءة مجرى «دفع» كعاقبت اللص وطابقت النعل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya rejects the gloss that God averts punishment through the prayer of the virtuous: the verse requires one group of people to be repelled from another.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r1.anchor: وهذا وما شاكله مفسد لمعنى الآية وذلك أن الآية تقتضي ولا بد مدفوعا من الناس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r2.speaker: نافع وابن كثير والباقون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r2.claim: Nafi and Ibn Kathir lighten the dal in lahuddimat; the other readers double it, fitting the repeated destruction of many places of worship.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن كثير «لهدمت» مخففة الدال، وقرأ الباقون «لهدمت» مشددة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r3.claim: Doubling suits many monasteries being repeatedly destroyed, as plural towers are described as reinforced; the singular palace is lighter, with similar contrasts in other verses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r3.anchor: فثقل الياء وقال قصر مشيد [الحج: 45] فخفف لكونه فردا وغلقت الأبواب [يوسف: 43]

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r4.claim: A ṣawmaʿa is a place of worship, a tall isolated building with a hard or pointed top; the word follows fawʿala and is associated with a sharp-spoken man.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r4.anchor: موضع العبادة وزنها فوعلة وهي بناء مرتفع منفرد حديد الأعلى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r5.claim: Qatada says monasteries were particular to Christian monks and Sabian worshippers before Islam; the word was later used for Muslim minarets.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r5.anchor: وكانت قبل الإسلام مختصة برهبان النصارى وبعباد الصابئين، قاله قتادة، ثم استعمل في مئذنة المسلمين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r6.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r6.claim: Al-Tabari says biyaʿ are Christian churches; another view calls them Jewish churches, but Ibn Atiyya says the material attributed to Mujahid does not establish that.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r6.anchor: والبيع كنائس النصارى واحدتها بيعة قال الطبري: وقيل هي كنائس اليهود ثم أدخل عن مجاهد ما لا يقتضي ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r7.claim: Ṣalawāt can mean worship places shared by religions, or prayers whose destruction is figuratively their disabling; some say the term means Jewish synagogues and is an Aramaic loan.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r7.anchor: مشتركة لكل ملة واستعير الهدم للصلوات من حيث تعطل، أو أراد وموضع صلوات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r8.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r8.claim: Abu al-Aliya identifies the ṣalawāt as Sabian worship places.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r8.anchor: وقال أبو العالية الصلوات مساجد الصابئين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r9.speaker: جمهور الناس وجعفر بن محمد وابن جني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r9.claim: The majority read ṣalawāt with both first consonants open; Ja'far ibn Muhammad and groups reported by Ibn Jinni vary the vowels, including kasra or ḍamma on ṣad and a silent lam.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r9.anchor: واختلفت القراءة فيها فقرأ جمهور الناس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r10.speaker: الجحدري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r10.claim: Al-Jahdari reads wa-ṣalawāt with ḍamma on both consonants, on the fuʿūl pattern, and says it denotes Christian churches.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r10.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري فيما روي عنه «وصلوات» بتاء بنقطتين من فوق وبضم الصاد واللام على وزن فعول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r11.speaker: الجحدري والحجاج بن يوسف
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r11.claim: Al-Jahdari and al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf read wa-ṣalūb with bāʾ, treating it as the plural of cross.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r11.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري والحجاج بن يوسف «وصلوب» بضم الصاد واللام وبالباء على أنه جمع صليب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r12.speaker: الضحاك والكلبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r12.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi read wa-ṣalūth with thāʾ and say it means Jewish worship places.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r12.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك والكلبي «وصلوث» بضم الصاد واللام وبالثاء منقوطة ثلاثا قالوا وهي مساجد اليهود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r13.speaker: فرقة وابن جني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r13.claim: Other groups read ṣalawāt with a silent lam and either open or doubled vowels; Ibn Jinni also records ṣalūthā and ṣalūt as forms associated with Christian burial houses near Mosul.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r13.anchor: وقرأت فرقة «صلوات» بفتح الصاد وسكون اللام، وقرأت فرقة «صلوات» بضم الصاد واللام حكاها ابن جني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r14.speaker: ابن جني وعكرمة ومجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r14.claim: Ibn Jinni mentions Christian burial houses outside Mosul called ṣalūt; Ikrima and Mujahid read ṣalūythā with kasra ṣad and waw.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r15.speaker: خصيف
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r15.claim: Kusayf says each name designates a worship place of a different community: monks or Sabians, Christians, Jews, and Muslims respectively.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r15.anchor: وذهب خصيف إلى أن هذه الأسماء قصد بها متعبدات الأمم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r16.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers that the list broadly emphasizes worship places shared among scriptural communities; in Arab usage, only biyaʿ is specifically Christian.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r16.anchor: والأظهر أنها قصد بها المبالغة بذكر المتعبدات وهذه الأسماء تشترك الأمم في مسمياتها إلا البيعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r17.claim: These worship institutions belong to scriptural communities from antiquity; Zoroastrians and polytheists are not named because their institutions do not merit protection and they do not remember God through revealed law.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r17.anchor: ومعاني هذه الأسماء هي في الأمم التي لها كتاب على قديم الدهر ولم يذكر في هذه المجوس ولا أهل الاشتراك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r18.claim: The pronoun in يذكر فيها refers to all the listed worship places.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r18.anchor: وقوله يذكر فيها الضمير عائد على جميع ما تقدم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r19.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r19.claim: God promises to aid His religion and law, urging battle and persistence; the verse applies to anyone who aids truth until the Resurrection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p125/r19.anchor: ثم وعد الله تعالى بنصره نصرة دينه وشرعه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r1.claim: They were expelled because they professed God's oneness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r1.anchor: وقوله إلا أن يقولوا ربنا الله معناه أخرجوا لتوحيدهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r2.claim: The phrase about God repelling some people by others was explained at 2:251.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r3.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Nāfiʿ read the verb with a light dāl.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r3.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع لهدمت خفيفة والباقون بتشديد الدال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r4.speaker: الباقون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r4.claim: The remaining readers pronounce the dāl geminated.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو العالية ومجاهد وابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū al-ʿĀliya, Mujāhid, and Ibn Zayd identify the ṣawāmiʿ as monks’ cloisters.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r5.anchor: أنها صوامع الرهبان قاله ابن عباس وأبو العالية ومجاهد وابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r6.speaker: قتادة وابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r6.claim: Qatāda and Ibn Qutayba identify them as the ṣawāmiʿ of the Ṣābiʾans.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r6.anchor: أنها صوامع الصابئين قاله قتادة وابن قتيبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r7.claim: Buyūʿ is the plural of bayʿa, meaning Christian churches.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r7.anchor: فأما البيع فهي جمع بيعة وهي بيع النصارى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r8.speaker: قتادة والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r8.claim: On the view that ṣalawāt are places of prayer, Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk identify them as Jewish synagogues; Abu Mansur says the word is Hebrew ṣlotha.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r8.anchor: أنها كنائس اليهود قاله قتادة والضحاك وقرأ على شيخنا أبي منصور اللغوي قال قوله وصلوات هي كنائس اليهود وهي بالعبرانية صلوثا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r9.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r9.claim: On the places-of-prayer view, Abū al-ʿĀliya identifies them as Ṣābiʾan temples.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r9.anchor: أنها مساجد الصابئين قاله أبو العالية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd takes ṣalawāt literally as prayers: without God defending Muslims through fighters, prayers in mosques would cease.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r10.anchor: أنها الصلوات حقيقة والمعنى لولا دفع الله عن المسلمين بالمجاهدين لانقطعت الصلوات في المساجد قاله ابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the masājid are Muslim mosques.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r11.anchor: فأما المساجد فقال ابن عباس هي مساجد المسلمين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r12.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r12.claim: Al-Zajjāj assigns the places to successive eras: churches in Moses’ time, cloisters and churches in Jesus’ time, and mosques in Muhammad’s time.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r12.anchor: معنى الآية لولا دفع بعض الناس ببعض لهدمت في زمن موسى الكنائس وفي زمن عيسى الصوامع والبيع وفي زمن محمد المساجد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r13.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r13.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk takes the pronoun “in them” to refer to all the places listed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r13.anchor: أن الكناية ترجع إلى جميع الأماكن المذكورات قاله الضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r14.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r14.claim: Abū Sulaymān al-Dimashqī says the pronoun refers only to mosques, since the other listed places are mostly associated with shirk.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r14.anchor: إلى المساجد خاصة لأن جميع المواضع المذكورة الغالب فيها الشرك قاله أبو سليمان الدمشقي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r15.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p436/r15.claim: Helping God means helping His religion and law.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435/r1.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435/r1.claim: Al-Awfi transmits from Ibn Abbas that those expelled without right were Muhammad and his companions, driven from Mecca to Medina.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435/r1.anchor: قال العوفي، عن ابن عباس: أخرجوا من مكة إلى المدينة بغير حق، يعني: محمدا وأصحابه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435/r2.claim: The believers had done no wrong except worshipping God alone; this is a disconnected exception in reality, though the polytheists regarded it as their greatest offense.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435/r2.anchor: وحده لا شريك له. وهذا استثناء منقطع بالنسبة إلى ما في نفس الأمر، وأما عند المشركين فهو أكبر الذنوب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435/r3.claim: During the trench digging, Muslims chanted that God had guided them and asked for steadfastness in battle; the Prophet joined in, repeating the end of each rhyme and stretching the final word about refusing sedition.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435/r3.anchor: فيوافقهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، ويقول معهم آخر كل قافية، فإذا قالوا:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435/r4.claim: God wards off one group through another and removes harm by created and decreed means; without this, the earth would be corrupted and the strong would destroy the weak.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435/r4.anchor: أي: لولا أنه يدفع عن قوم بقوم، ويكشف شر أناس عن غيرهم، بما يخلقه ويقدره من الأسباب، لفسدت الأرض، وأهلك القوي الضعيف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، أبو العالية، عكرمة، الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Abu al-Aliyah, Ikrima, and al-Dahhak explain the ṣawāmiʿ as small hermitages for monks.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r1.anchor: وهي المعابد الصغار للرهبان، قاله ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وأبو العالية، وعكرمة، والضحاك، وغيرهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r2.claim: Qatada says the ṣawāmiʿ are temples of the Sabians.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r3.claim: Another report from Qatada identifies the ṣawāmiʿ as Magian temples.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r4.claim: Maqatil ibn Hayyan says the ṣawāmiʿ are roadside houses.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن حيان: هي البيوت التي على الطرق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r5.speaker: أبو العالية، قتادة، الضحاك، ابن صخر، مقاتل بن حيان، خصيف
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r5.claim: The churches are broader than hermitages and have more worshippers; these authorities also identify them as Christian churches.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r5.anchor: وهي أوسع منها، وأكثر عابدين فيها. وهي للنصارى أيضا. قاله أبو العالية، وقتادة، والضحاك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r6.speaker: ابن جبير عن مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r6.claim: Ibn Jubayr relates from Mujahid and others that the churches meant here are Jewish synagogues.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r6.anchor: وحكى ابن جبير عن مجاهد وغيره: أنها كنائس اليهود

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r7.speaker: السدي عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r7.claim: Al-Suddi, through an unnamed transmitter from Ibn Abbas, also identifies them as Jewish churches; Ibn Kathir clarifies that Mujahid only said churches generally.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r7.anchor: وحكى السدي، عمن حدثه، عن ابن عباس: أنها كنائس اليهود، ومجاهد إنما قال: هي الكنائس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r8.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس، عكرمة، الضحاك، قتادة
