IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r8.claim: Al-Awfi transmits from Ibn Abbas, and Ikrima, al-Dahhak, and Qatada also say, that ṣalawāt are Jewish churches, called ṣalota.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r8.anchor: قال العوفي، عن ابن عباس: الصلوات: الكنائس. وكذا قال عكرمة، والضحاك، وقتادة: إنها كنائس اليهود

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r9.speaker: السدي عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r9.claim: Al-Suddi transmits from Ibn Abbas that ṣalawāt are Christian churches.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r9.anchor: وحكى السدي، عمن حدثه، عن ابن عباس: أنها كنائس النصارى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r10.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r10.claim: Abu al-Aliyah and others identify ṣalawāt as Sabian temples.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r10.anchor: وقال أبو العالية، وغيره: الصلوات: معابد الصابئين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r11.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r11.claim: Mujahid says ṣalawāt are roadside places of worship used by the People of the Book and Muslims, while mosques are specifically for Muslims.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p435#2/r11.anchor: وقال ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: الصلوات: مساجد لأهل الكتاب ولأهل الإسلام بالطرق. وأما المساجد فهي للمسلمين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436/r1.claim: One proposed antecedent for the pronoun in yudhkaru fīhā is mosques, the nearest preceding noun.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436/r1.anchor: فقد قيل: الضمير في قوله: {يذكر فيها} عائد إلى المساجد؛ لأنها أقرب المذكورات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says God's name is remembered often in all the listed places of worship.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436/r2.anchor: وقال الضحاك: الجميع يذكر فيها اسم الله كثيرا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436/r3.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436/r3.claim: Ibn Jarir says the terms refer respectively to monks' hermitages, Christian churches, Jewish synagogues, and Muslim mosques, following established Arabic usage.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436/r3.anchor: وقال ابن جرير: الصواب: لهدمت صوامع الرهبان وبيع النصارى وصلوات اليهود، وهي كنائسهم، ومساجد المسلمين التي يذكر فيها اسم الله كثيرا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436/r4.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436/r4.claim: Some scholars see an ascent from the least to the most, ending with mosques, which are more frequented and attended by worshippers with sound intent.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436/r4.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء: هذا ترق من الأقل إلى الأكثر إلى أن ينتهي إلى المساجد، وهي أكثر عمارا وأكثر عبادا، وهم ذوو القصد الصحيح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436/r5.claim: The promise that God will support those who support Him parallels the promise that if believers support God, He will support them and steady their feet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436/r5.anchor: تعالى: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن تنصروا الله ينصركم ويثبت أقدامكم. والذين كفروا فتعسا لهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436#2/r1.claim: God describes Himself as strong and mighty: by His strength He created and measured everything; by His might none can conquer Him, and all things are humble and dependent on Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436#2/r1.anchor: فبقوته خلق كل شيء فقدره تقديرا، وبعزته لا يقهره قاهر، ولا يغلبه غالب، بل كل شيء ذليل لديه، فقير إليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436#2/r2.claim: Those aided by the Strong and Mighty are victorious, while their enemies are overcome; Ibn Kathir links this to God's promise to the messengers and His troops.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p436#2/r2.anchor: ومن كان القوي العزيز ناصره فهو المنصور، وعدوه هو المقهور، قال الله تعالى: {ولقد سبقت كلمتنا لعبادنا المرسلين. إنهم لهم المنصورون

JISHUMI:v7p4967/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4967/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو
JISHUMI:v7p4967/r5.claim: Abu Amr reads yadfaʿu and dafʿ without alif in both places.
JISHUMI:v7p4967/r5.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو: إن الله يدفع عن الذين آمنوا .. ولولا دفع الله بغير ألف فيهما.

JISHUMI:v7p4967/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4967/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع
JISHUMI:v7p4967/r6.claim: Abu Ja'far and Nafi read yudāfiʿu and difāʿ, with alif in both places.
JISHUMI:v7p4967/r6.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع: إن الله يدافع، ولولا دفاع بالألف.

JISHUMI:v7p4967/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4967/r7.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
JISHUMI:v7p4967/r7.claim: Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read yudāfiʿu with alif, then dafʿ without alif.
JISHUMI:v7p4967/r7.anchor: إن الله يدافع بالألف ولولا دفع الله بغير ألف، قرأ كذلك عاصم وحمزة والكسائي

JISHUMI:v7p4967/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4967/r8.speaker: يعقوب
JISHUMI:v7p4967/r8.claim: Yaqub reads yadfaʿu without alif and difāʿ with alif; difāʿ is reciprocal, while dafʿ is a single action.
JISHUMI:v7p4967/r8.anchor: ورابعها: إن الله يدفع بغير ألف، ولولا دفاع الله بألف، قراءة يعقوب

JISHUMI:v7p4968/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4968/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير
JISHUMI:v7p4968/r3.claim: They lighten لهدمت; other readers double it for extensive destruction.
JISHUMI:v7p4968/r3.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير: لهدمت خفيفة، وقرأ الباقون مشددة

JISHUMI:v7p4968/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4968/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير وعاصم ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v7p4968/r4.claim: These readers pronounce the tāʾ of لهدمت distinctly.
JISHUMI:v7p4968/r4.anchor: فأظهرها أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير وعاصم ويعقوب

JISHUMI:v7p4968/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4968/r5.speaker: الآخرون
JISHUMI:v7p4968/r5.claim: The remaining readers assimilate the tāʾ in لهدمت.
JISHUMI:v7p4968/r5.anchor: ابن كثير وعاصم ويعقوب، وأدغمها الآخرون

JISHUMI:v7p4968/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4968/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4968/r6.claim: دفع is the verbal noun of دفع; دافع عنك السوء is another verbal form for God warding off harm.
JISHUMI:v7p4968/r6.anchor: الدفع: مصدر دفعت الرجل دفعا، ودافع الله عنك السوء دفاعا

JISHUMI:v7p4968/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4968/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4968/r7.claim: المدفع means a poor person because everyone pushes him away from themselves.
JISHUMI:v7p4968/r7.anchor: والمدفع الفقير؛ لأن كلا يدفعه عن نفسه

JISHUMI:v7p4968/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4968/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4968/r9.claim: A صومعة is a known structure; its name derives from compactness, as does الأصمع for ears close to the head.
JISHUMI:v7p4968/r9.anchor: والصومعة: معروفة، وأصله من الانضمام، ومنه: الأصمع: اللاصق الأذنين

JISHUMI:v7p4968/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4968/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4968/r10.claim: بيع is the plural of بيعة.

JISHUMI:v7p4968/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4968/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4968/r13.claim: One analysis treats إلا أن يقولوا as a disconnected exception.

JISHUMI:v7p4968/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4968/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4968/r14.claim: Another treats it as connected: they were expelled only for saying their Lord is God; أن may be governed by ب or be accusative as exception.
JISHUMI:v7p4968/r14.anchor: وقيل: استثناء متصل، بتقدير: ما أخرجوهم لخصلة إلا لقولهم: ربنا الله

JISHUMI:v7p4974/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4974/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4974/r1.claim: God supports believers with subtle aid and strengthens their hearts; their fighting alone is insufficient, so God must defend by turning some people against others.
JISHUMI:v7p4974/r1.anchor: وتدل على أنه ينصر المؤمنين بألطافه، ويقوي قلوبهم، ثم بين أن قتالهم لا يكفي؛ بل لا بد من دفاع من جهته

JISHUMI:v7p4974/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4974/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4974/r2.claim: God’s counteraction completes His ordering and prevents unbelievers from gaining control; without it they would dominate.
JISHUMI:v7p4974/r2.anchor: فيرد بعضهم ببعض حتى يتم التدبير، ولايستولي الكفار، ولولا ذلك لاستولوا

JISHUMI:v7p4974/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4974/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4974/r3.claim: The final clause indicates God wards off unbelievers’ harm through the believers He supports.
JISHUMI:v7p4974/r3.anchor: ويدل آخر الآيات أن المراد دفع معرة الكفار بالمؤمنين ولذلك قال: (ولينصرن الله من ينصره)

JISHUMI:v7p4974/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4974/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4974/r4.claim: The passage indicates the obligation to command right and forbid wrong.
JISHUMI:v7p4974/r4.anchor: وتدل على [وجوب الأمر] بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر

JISHUMI:v7p4974/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4974/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4974/r5.claim: Being driven from their homes for faith marks the merit of the emigrants.
JISHUMI:v7p4974/r5.anchor: ويدل قوله: (الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم) على فضل المهاجرين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r5.claim: God's assertion that He can aid them is a promise of victory phrased in the authoritative manner of rulers; the earlier promise to protect believers signals the same.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r5.anchor: والأخبار بكونه قادرا على نصرهم عدة منه بالنصر واردة على سنن كلام الجبابرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r6.claim: The exception “except that they say” is a genitive apposition to “right,” stating that their sole alleged offense was professing God as Lord.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r6.anchor: أن يقولوا } في محل الجر على الإبدال من { حق إلا أن يقولوا ربنا الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r7.claim: The same point is expressed in the question, “Do you resent us for anything but that we believe in God?”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r7.anchor: ومثله : { هل تنقمون منا إلا أن ءامنا بالله } ( المائدة : 59 )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r8.claim: God's repelling people by one another means empowering Muslims to prevail over unbelievers through struggle; otherwise polytheists would have destroyed other communities' worship places.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r8.anchor: دفع الله بعض الناس ببعض : إظهاره وتسليطه المسلمين منهم على الكافرين بالمجاهدة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r9.claim: An alternative is that the Prophet's polytheist community would have overpowered Muslims and protected People of the Book and demolished both groups' sanctuaries.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r9.anchor: أو لغلب المشركون من أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم على المسلمين وعلى أهل الكتاب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r10.claim: The word is also read difāʿ with an alif, and lahuddimat is read with a lightened consonant.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r11.claim: A church is called ṣalāt because prayer is performed in it; another account derives the word from Hebrew ṣlothā.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r11.anchor: وسميت الكنيسة ( صلاة ) لأنه يصلى فيها . وقيل : هي كلمة معربة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r12.claim: Supporting God means supporting His religion and His allies.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r12.anchor: من ينصره } أي ينصر دينه وأولياءه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r13.claim: This is God's unseen announcement of how the emigrants will conduct themselves in faith if empowered and given worldly means.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r13.anchor: هو إخبار من الله عز وجل بظهر الغيب عما ستكون عليه سيرة المهاجرين رضي الله عنهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r14.speaker: عثمان
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r14.claim: ʿUthmān calls this praise before trial: God praised the emigrants before they performed the later good deeds.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r14.anchor: وعن عثمان رضي الله عنه : هذا والله ثناء قبل بلاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r18.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r18.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r18.claim: The apparent parsing is genitive, with alladhīna following alladhīna ukhrijū.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p161/r18.anchor: والظاهر أنه مجرور ، تابع للذين أخرجوا

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj interprets the mutual repelling as God repelling polytheists through Muslims.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r3.anchor: ولولا دفع الله المشركين بالمسلمين , وهذا قول ابن جريج

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says God protects religion through those who strive in His cause.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r4.anchor: ولولا دفع الله عن الدين بالمجاهدين , وهذا قول ابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r5.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi says God protects believers through the prophets.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r5.anchor: ولولا دفع الله بالنبيين عن المؤمنين , وهذا قول الكلبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r6.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talib says the Companions protected later generations of Successors through God's repelling.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r6.anchor: ولولا دفع الله بأصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عمن بعدهم من التابعين

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r7.claim: Mujahid interprets it as God repelling harm through witnesses' testimony concerning rights.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r7.anchor: ولولا دفع الله بشهادة الشهود على الحقوق , وهذا قول مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r8.speaker: قطرب
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r8.claim: Qutrub says God protects people from harm through virtues.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r8.anchor: ولولا دفع الله على النفوس بالفضائل , وهذا قول قطرب

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r9.claim: The author adds that God repels evil through good.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r9.anchor: ولولا دفع الله عن المنكر بالمعروف

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r10.claim: Mujahid says the ṣawāmiʿ are monks' hermitages.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r10.anchor: أنها صوامع الرهبان , وهذا قول مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r11.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r11.claim: Qatada says the ṣawāmiʿ are the places of prayer of the Sabeans.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r11.anchor: أنها مصلى الصابئين , وهو قول قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r12.speaker: النبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r12.claim: A report from the Prophet says, “The believer's monastery is his house.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r12.anchor: وقد روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( صومعة المؤمن بيته )

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r13.claim: The word is named for the narrowing together of its two sides; المنصمع means joined or contracted, as in أذن صمعاء.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r13.anchor: وسميت صومعة لانضمام طرفيها , والمنصمع : المنضم , ومنه أذن صمعاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r14.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r14.claim: Qatada says the biyaʿ are Christian churches.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r14.anchor: أنها بيع النصارى , وهو قول قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r15.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r15.claim: Mujahid says the biyaʿ are Jewish synagogues.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r15.anchor: أنها كنائس اليهود , وهو قول مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r16.claim: بيعة is a foreign word adapted into Arabic.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r17.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r17.claim: Al-Dahhak says the ṣalawāt are Jewish synagogues, which Jews call ṣalotā; the Arabic plural was adapted from that name.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r17.anchor: أنها كنائس اليهود يسمونها : صلوتا , فعرب جمعها , فقيل صلوات , وهذا قول الضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r18.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r18.claim: Ibn ʿIsa says ṣalawāt means prayers that were abandoned.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r18.anchor: معناه : وتركت صلوات , ذكره ابن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r19.claim: The masājid are the mosques of Muslims.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r20.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r20.claim: Al-Dahhak says polytheists would demolish the mosques in the present era if God did not repel them through Muslims.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r20.anchor: لهدمها الآن المشركون لولا دفع الله بالمسلمين , وهو معنى قول الضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r21.speaker: الزجاج
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r21.claim: Al-Zajjaj assigns hermitages to Moses' law, churches to Jesus' law, and mosques to Muhammad's law; the verse thus means every place where God is worshiped in each dispensation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p28#2/r21.anchor: لهدمت صوامع في أيام شريعة موسى , وبيع في أيام شريعة عيسى ومساجد في أيام شريعة محمد

MUJAHID:v2p426#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p426#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p426#2/r1.claim: God checks people through one another in matters of testimony and justice; without this, the listed houses of worship would have been destroyed.
MUJAHID:v2p426#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض ﴾ يقول يدفع بعضهم بعضا في الشهادة وفي الحق

MUJAHID:v2p426#2/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p426#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p426#2/r2.claim: Mujahid identifies the ṣawāmiʿ as monks' hermitages; the churches, synagogues, and mosques belong to the People of the Book and Muslims and lie along the road.
MUJAHID:v2p426#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد قال الصوامع صوامع الرهبان والبيع والكنائس

MUQATIL:22:40/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:40/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:40/r1.claim: Meccan unbelievers tortured some believers and verbally harmed others until they fled from Mecca to Medina.
MUQATIL:22:40/r1.anchor: ذلك أنهم عذبوا منهم طائفة، وآذوا بعضهم بالألسن

MUQATIL:22:40/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:40/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:40/r2.claim: The believers were expelled only for saying that God was their Lord, knowing and affirming His oneness.
MUQATIL:22:40/r2.anchor: إلا أن يقولوا: { ربنا الله } فعرفوه ووحدوه

MUQATIL:22:40/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:40/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:40/r3.claim: If God did not repel polytheists through Muslims, the polytheists would overcome and kill the Muslims.
MUQATIL:22:40/r3.anchor: لولا أن يدفع الله المشركين بالمسلمين لغلب المشركون فقتلوا المسلمين

MUQATIL:22:40/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:40/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:40/r4.claim: The protected worship places are monks’ hermitages, Christian churches, Jewish prayer houses, and Muslim mosques.
MUQATIL:22:40/r4.anchor: { صوامع } الرهبان { وبيع } النصارى { وصلوات } يعنى اليهود

MUQATIL:22:40/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:40/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:40/r5.claim: These religious communities remember God frequently in their worship places, which Muslims protect by repelling the polytheists.
MUQATIL:22:40/r5.anchor: كل هؤلاء الملل يذكرون الله كثيرا فى مساجدهم

MUQATIL:22:40/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:40/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:40/r6.claim: God will help whoever aids Him by affirming His oneness; He is strong in helping His allies and invincible in His dominion.
MUQATIL:22:40/r6.anchor: يعن من يعينه حتى يوحد الله، عز وجل،

MUQATIL:22:40/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:40/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:40/r7.claim: The wording “who helps Him” is linked to 57:25, where it means whoever affirms God’s oneness.
MUQATIL:22:40/r7.anchor: يعني من يوحده، وغيرها فى الأحزاب، وهود.

MUQATIL:22:40/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:40/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:40/r8.claim: God is more protective and mightier than His creation.
MUQATIL:22:40/r8.anchor: وهو سبحانه أوقى وأعز من خلقه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r1.claim: Alladhina can be genitive as an apposition, accusative with an implied aʿni, or nominative with an implied hum.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r1.anchor: فى محل جر بدل من الذين أو نصب بأعنى أو رفع باضمارهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r2.claim: The people expelled from their homes are the believers expelled from Mecca.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r3.claim: They were expelled without cause except their profession of God's oneness, which should have entitled them to remain, not caused expulsion; the phrase is a genitive apposition to haqq.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r3.anchor: بغير موجب سوى التوحيد الذى ينبغى أن يكون موجب التمكن لا موجب الاخراج

NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r4.claim: Nasafi compares the wording with the verse asking whether believers are resented for believing in God.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r4.anchor: ومثله هل تنقمون منا إلا أن آمنا بالله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r5.speaker: مدني ويعقوب
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r5.claim: Madinan and Yaqub read difaa, the verbal noun of mutual defense, in place of dafʿ.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r5.anchor: ﴿ ولولا دفع الله ﴾ دفاع مدنى ويعقوب

NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r6.speaker: حجازى
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r6.claim: The Hijazis read the verb with a light form.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r6.anchor: ﴿ الناس بعضهم ببعض لهدمت ﴾ وبالتخفيف حجازى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r7.claim: Without Muslims being empowered to struggle against disbelievers, polytheists would dominate religious communities and demolish their houses of worship; alternatively, they would overrun Muslims and protected People of the Book and destroy both groups' worship places.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r7.anchor: أى لولا اظهاره وتسليطه المسلمين على الكافرين بالمجاهدة لا ستولى المشركون على أهل الملل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r8.claim: The other worship places are named before mosques because they existed earlier or were closer to demolition.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r8.anchor: وقدم غير المساجد عليها لتقدمها وجودا أو لقربها من التهديم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r9.claim: The phrase about frequent remembrance applies either only to mosques or to all the previously listed places of worship.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r9.anchor: فى المساجد أو فى جميع ما تقدم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r10.claim: Helping God means helping His religion and His allies.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r11.claim: God is strong enough to help His allies and mighty in taking vengeance on His enemies.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p106/r11.anchor: ﴿ إن الله لقوي ﴾ على نصرأوليائه ﴿ عزيز ﴾ على انتقام أعدائه

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r1.claim: The believers were expelled unjustly for professing that God alone is their Lord.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم } هذا أحد ما ظلموا به وإنما أخرجوا لقولهم: ربنا الله وحده

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r2.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r2.claim: Sibawayh parses the exception as disconnected: they were expelled unjustly, but because they said, 'Our Lord is God.'
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r2.anchor: استثناء منقطع أي لكن لقولهم ربنا الله قاله سيبويه

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r3.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r3.claim: Al-Farra, with al-Zajjaj, allows a genitive construction returning to the preceding bi: they were expelled on account of monotheism by idolaters.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء يجوز أن تكون في موضع خفض، يقدرها مردودة على الباء

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r4.claim: Alladhina ukhriju is genitive as an appositive to alladhina yuqatilun.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r4.anchor: و { الذين أخرجوا } في موضع خفض بدلا من قوله: { للذين يقاتلون }

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r5.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r5.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says that before the Aqaba pledge the Prophet had no permission to fight or shed blood; for ten years he called people to God, endured harm, and overlooked the ignorant, fulfilling the promise in 17:15.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r5.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل بيعة العقبة لم يؤذن له في الحرب ولم تحل له الدماء

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r6.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r6.claim: Quraysh persecuted the Prophet's migrant followers, tempted some away from faith, and drove them from home; some fled to Abyssinia, some to Medina, and some endured.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r6.anchor: فمنهم من فر إلى أرض الحبشة، ومنهم من خرج إلى المدينة، ومنهم من صبر على الأذى

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r7.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r7.claim: After Quraysh rejected God's command, denied the Prophet, and tortured believers, God permitted fighting, self-defense, and resistance, revealing 22:39–40.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r7.anchor: وأنزل { أذن للذين يقاتلون بأنهم ظلموا إلى قوله الأمور }

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r8.claim: The verse shows that a coerced act is attributed to the one who compels it: God ascribes the expulsion to the unbelievers to assign the blame.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r8.anchor: دليل على أن نسبة الفعل الموجود من الملجأ المكره إلى الذي ألجأه وأكرهه

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r9.claim: Qurtubi says the same attribution is used in 9:40, 'when the unbelievers expelled him.'
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r9.anchor: وهذه الآية مثل قوله تعالى: إذ أخرجه الذين كفروا

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r10.claim: God prescribed fighting for prophets and believers so polytheists would not take over and disable religious worship; required jihad lets adherents worship freely.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r10.anchor: أي لولا ما شرعه الله تعالى للأنبياء والمؤمنين من قتال الأعداء، لاستولى أهل الشرك

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r11.claim: Jihad preceded Islam among earlier communities and preserved their religious laws and places of worship; the verse strengthens the command to fight for truth.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r11.anchor: فالجهاد أمر متقدم في الأمم، وبه صلحت الشرائع واجتمعت المتعبدات

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r12.claim: Christians or Sabians who condemn jihad contradict their own position, since without fighting the religions they defend would not have survived.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r12.anchor: فمن استبشع من النصارى والصابئين الجهاد فهو مناقض لمذهبه إذ لولا القتال لما بقي الدين

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r13.claim: The listed sanctuaries existed before their communities' alterations and before Islam superseded those laws: churches under Moses, monasteries and churches under Jesus, and mosques under Muhammad.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40/r13.anchor: أي لولا هذا الدفع لهدم في زمن موسى الكنائس، وفي زمن عيسى الصوامع والبيع

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the reading and interpretation as 'they would be demolished' is the soundest explanation.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطية: هذا أصوب ما قيل في تأويل الآية

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r2.claim: Ali says God wards off unbelievers from later generations through Muhammad's Companions; Qurtubi accepts the general defense but says fighting fits the verse better.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r2.anchor: وروي عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه أنه قال: ولولا دفع الله بأصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r3.claim: Mujahid says God wards off one people's oppression through the testimony of upright witnesses.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: لولا دفع الله ظلم قوم بشهادة العدول

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r4.speaker: فرقة
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r4.claim: One group says God wards off oppressors' wrongdoing through governors' justice.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r4.anchor: وقالت فرقة: ولولا دفع الله ظلم الظلمة بعدل الولاة

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r5.speaker: أبو الدرداء
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r5.claim: Abu al-Darda says God protects those outside mosques through mosque-goers and those who do not fight through those who fight, or punishment would come.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r5.anchor: وقال أبو الدرداء: لولا أن الله عز وجل يدفع بمن في المساجد عمن ليس في المساجد

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r6.speaker: فرقة
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r6.claim: Another group says God wards off punishment through the supplication of virtuous and righteous people; the verse necessarily implies both a defender and one defended.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r6.anchor: وقالت فرقة: ولولا دفع الله العذاب بدعاء الفضلاء والأخيار

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r7.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r7.claim: Ibn Khuzaymandad says the verse bars destroying protected non-Muslims' churches, synagogues, and fire temples in Muslim lands because the treaty protects them like their homes and property.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r7.anchor: تضمنت هذه الآية المنع من هدم كنائس أهل الذمة وبيعهم وبيوت نيرانهم

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r8.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r8.claim: He says protected communities may not construct new sanctuaries or expand or heighten existing ones, and Muslims should not enter or pray there; additions must be demolished and temples in enemy territory may be destroyed.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r8.anchor: ولا يتركون أن يحدثوا ما لم يكن، ولا يزيدون في البنيان لا سعة ولا ارتفاعا

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r9.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r9.claim: He allows a mosque to be demolished for rebuilding, citing Uthman's rebuilding of the Prophet's mosque.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r9.anchor: وجائز أن ينقض المسجد ليعاد بنيانه وقد فعل ذلك عثمان رضي الله عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r10.speaker: قراءة
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r10.claim: The verb is read with a light or doubled dal.

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r11.claim: Sawami is the plural of sawma'a, a tall structure pointed at the top, named from raising and sharpening the top of a thārid dish.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r11.anchor: { صوامع } جمع صومعة، وزنها فوعلة، وهي بناء مرتفع حديد الأعلى

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r12.claim: The root also describes a sharp-hearted, keen-witted person or sharp speech; it can additionally denote a person or animal with a small ear.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r12.anchor: ورجل أصمع القلب أي حاد الفطنة. والأصمع من الرجال الحديد القول

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r13.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r13.claim: Qatada says monasteries originally belonged to Christian monks and Sabian worshippers, then the term was used for Muslim minarets.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r13.anchor: وكانت قبل الإسلام مختصة برهبان النصارى وبعباد الصابئين قاله قتادة

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r14.claim: Biya' is the plural of bi'a, the Christian church.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r14.anchor: والبيع جمع بيعة، وهي كنيسة النصارى

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r15.speaker: الزجاج والحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r15.claim: Al-Zajjaj and al-Hasan identify salawat as Jewish synagogues, called salota in Aramaic.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r15.anchor: قال الزجاج والحسن: هي كنائس اليهود وهي بالعبرانية صلوتا

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r16.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r16.claim: Abu Ubayda says salawat are Christian prayer houses in the wilderness for travelers, called salota and Arabized as salawat.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r16.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: الصلوات بيوت تبنى للنصارى في البراري يصلون فيها في أسفارهم

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r17.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r17.claim: Ibn Atiyya records nine readings of salawat, including salawat, salula, salub, and saluth, with further forms distinguished by vowel, consonant, and final spelling.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#2/r17.anchor: وفي «صلوات» تسع قراءات ذكرها ابن عطية

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r1.speaker: عاصم الجحدري والضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r1.claim: Al-Nahhas adds Asim al-Jahdari's salub and al-Dahhak's saluth, with the latter's sad vowel uncertain, bringing the total to twelve readings.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r1.anchor: وروى عن عاصم الجحدري أنه قرأ «وصلوب». وروي عن الضحاك «وصلوث» بالثاء

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says salawat are churches.

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r3.claim: Abu al-Aliya says salawat are the Sabians' mosques.

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd takes salawat as Muslims' prayer sites, whose worship is interrupted when enemies arrive; on this view 'demolished' is metaphorical for disabled worship or omits 'places of.'
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r4.anchor: ابن زيد: هي صلوات المسلمين تنقطع إذا دخل عليهم العدو وتهدم المساجد

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس والزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r5.claim: On Ibn Abbas's and al-Zajjaj's explanations, destruction of the worship sites is literal.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r5.anchor: وعلى قول ابن عباس والزجاج وغيرهم يكون الهدم حقيقة

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r6.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says demolishing salawat means abandoning them.

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r7.speaker: قطرب
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r7.claim: Qutrub identifies salawat as small monasteries, with no singular form known.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r7.anchor: قطرب: هي الصوامع الصغار ولم يسمع لها واحد

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r8.speaker: خصيف
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r8.claim: Khasif assigns each name to a community's worship place: monasteries to monks, churches to Christians, salawat to Jews, and mosques to Muslims.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r8.anchor: فالصوامع للرهبان، والبيع للنصارى، والصلوات لليهود، والمساجد للمسلمين

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r9.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers that the list rhetorically amplifies the range of worship sites; most names are shared across scriptural communities except bi'a, specifically Christian in Arabic.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r9.anchor: قال ابن عطية: والأظهر أنها قصد بها المبالغة في ذكر المتعبدات

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r10.claim: The terms concern ancient scriptural communities; Magians and polytheists are omitted because they have no sanctuaries requiring protection and do not invoke God's name as adherents of revealed laws do.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r10.anchor: ولم يذكر في هذه الآية المجوس ولا أهل الإشراك لأن هؤلاء ليس لهم ما يجب حمايته

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r11.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r11.claim: Al-Nahhas says the pronoun in 'God's name is mentioned therein' should, by the nearest-noun rule, refer to mosques; it may instead refer to all listed sites during their laws and practice of truth.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r11.anchor: وقال النحاس: «يذكر فيها اسم الله» الذي يجب في كلام العرب على حقيقة النظر أن يكون

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r12.claim: Mosques and prayer sites of protected communities are placed first because they were older buildings.

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r13.claim: Another explanation is that the earlier sites are nearer destruction, while mosques are closer to remembrance; Qurtubi compares the delayed mention of the foremost in 35:32.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r13.anchor: وقيل لقربها من الهدم وقرب المساجد من الذكر كما أخر السابق

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r14.claim: Helping God means helping His religion and His Prophet.

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r15.speaker: الخطابي
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r15.claim: Al-Khattabi says strong can mean capable, since whoever is strong enough to do something can accomplish it.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r15.anchor: القوي يكون بمعنى القادر، ومن قوي على شيء فقد قدر عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r16.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r16.claim: Al-Zajjaj glosses aziz as exalted and noble.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r16.anchor: { عزيز } أي جليل شريف قاله الزجاج

QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r17.claim: Another gloss is the one who is inviolable and cannot be overcome, as Qurtubi explains in his book on the divine names.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:40#3/r17.anchor: وقيل الممتنع الذي لا يرام وقد بيناهما في الكتاب الأسنى

NASHR:v2p5/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p5/r5.speaker: صاحب المبهج
NASHR:v2p5/r5.claim: Al-Mubhij uniquely reports an exception for ḥaṣirat and lahudimat, assimilating them; the author says he does not know this report.
NASHR:v2p5/r5.anchor: وانفرد صاحب المبهج عنه باستثناء حصرت، ولهدمت فأدغمها ولا نعرفه
